MEMBER.NAME: request
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: malloc(0x138) (block 0x150, usable 0x140). Decoded BleProvRequest target (not zeroed before Pb_DecodeSubmessagePtr).

MEMBER.NAME: response
MEMBER.REGULAR_CMT: malloc(0x138) (block 0x150, usable 0x140). Zeroed by DispatchRequest each command. Allocated immediately after `request` in the ctor, so it is the forward neighbour of the request buffer; the next block after `response` is whatever the provisioning task allocates next (task stacks / std::deque nodes). OOB write must pass +0x140 from here to hit the next block header.

COMMENTS.COMMENT: crt0: mie=mip=0; FPU on if misa&0x10028; mtvec=0x700d0080|2 (vectored, handler not in image); fence.i; zero BSS [0x700d9400,0x700d9bae); call main(); hang if main returns.
Frame work pump: if pending_encode_tick set -> avc_stream_select_ctx(0), then avc_stream_run_frame(0) + avc_stream_run_frame(1) (both channels).
Mailbox handshake on ep mbox_ep_sync: poll mbox_rx_poll until != 1 (empty), then mbox_send ack. Stage args 0..3 around the frame pipeline in avc_stream_frame_cmd.
Copy 0x4c-byte params struct to host-shared ptr params_shared_ptr (memcpy), then host_sync_barrier handshake. Echoes encoder params back to host.
Assert: syslog_printf("ASSERT: {%s:%d:0x%X}", file, line, val) then halt forever.
Disable IRQs, mbox_init(), open ep(3,0,0)->ctrl-rx, ep(3,0,1)->sync, register rx handler, block on first 12-byte message (timestamp for syslog prefix).
Ctrl-rx handler (ep 9b6e): busy-guard 9b7c; blocking recv; if msg cmd==4 -> clear mbox_shutdown_flag, reply ack on 9b6e, then HALT (infinite loop) = shutdown cmd.
Encoder go: *(u32*)0x700b0794 = 1.
Spin until 0x700b0790 bit 8 (frame done).

Master frame encode over enc_reg_image: AUD/SEI/SPS/PPS/slice writers per flag bits in +0x30 (1=AUD? 2=SPS,4=PPS,0x20=SEI,0x40=prefix - see callers); per-slice loop (spe_slice_stats/cost reads, enc_frame_dim_set, enc_quant_tables_load, enc_scan_table_load, enc_qp_table_build, spe_exec_and_wait, spe_result_read); avp_wait_status_release at end.
avp.c:0x2b5: xlate write slot via shm_alias_xlate, memcpy 16-byte desc + optional param_4-byte payload (UNBOUNDED, host-controlled), advance write ptr.

avc_stream.c:0x313: execute one 0x48-byte host frame command: luma/chroma ptrs -> 0x700d9408/0x700d940c; update bits in cmd[5]: 0x80=bitrate chg (rc_set_bitrate), 0x10=GOP chg + rc_set_framerate, 0x02/0x01=qp max/min, 0x08=force IDR (ctx+0x74), 0x04=force key (ctx+0x78), 0x40=rc restart (rc_enable, assert if already on), 0x20=flush; then enc_cmd_reg_write_wait, host_sync_barrier(0..3), rc_frame_qp, build full register image, encode_one_frame, enc_status_read, rc_post_frame -> ctx+0x79 needs-more-frames flag; rc_disable on flush.

Slice header (NAL 5/1): first_mb=0, slice_type=nal flags>>6, pps_id ctx+0x8b, frame_num 6b ctx+0x9d, idr_pic_id ctx+0x9f (type 5), poc_lsb 6b ctx+0x9e, qp_delta se(param_4+3 - +2), deblock idc/alpha/beta offsets, slice-QP rewind via bw checkpoints (bw_pos_restore).

SPS NAL (avc_nal.c): profile ctx+0x7c (High=100 adds 0x2c constraint byte), pic_width/height_in_mbs_minus1 from ctx+0x30/0x31, crop = MB*16 - ctx+0x2c/0x2e, VUI timing_info (0x3011) num_units_in_tick=ctx+0x94 / time_scale=ctx+0x90 (32b); assert if HRD flag ctx+0x98 set.

PPS NAL: pps/sps ids ctx+0x8b/0x8a, deblock_control_present regimage+0x2c, init_qp se(pic_init_qp-26) regimage+0x02, chroma_qp_offset regimage+0x2e, constrained_intra +0x2d, High-profile extra chroma offset.
0x700b0c90 = (p4&1)<<17 | (p1&1)<<16 | (p3&0xff)<<8 | (p2&0xff) (go bit16 + MB dims); spin until enc_done_flag set by SPE IRQ, then clear it.
Build AVP output descriptor from host buffer struct; spin avp_queue_not_empty; optional 2-byte trailer; avp_queue_push_desc into SHM queue (xlate via shm_alias_xlate).
Spin while 0x70094754 sign bit set (result valid), then post status&0x3fff... back to AVP queue via avp_release_buf_post.

Post-frame: store bits 0x94bc; complexity/overflow (0x94a8/0x9474 90% -> 0x94dc, recovery 0x9498); cplxr 0x94b0 clamp +-1.5*0x94cc; mode-3 lookahead (qp +-1, streak 0x94e6, avg 0x94b4); ends rc_update_cplx_accum.
Append cmd word ((n&0x1f)<<3 | v<<12 | class) to SPE FIFO 0x70092c00+idx*4; assert spe.c:0x12a if idx>199 (overflow guard).

Reset spe_fifo_idx + 0x70092004; copy 0x6d8 bytes of SPE firmware from spe_fw_blob_0x6d8 into load window 0x70092008. The SPE is a separate DSP running this downloaded code (bit-writer + slice-encode engine).
spe.c:0x5e: assert no pending; build cmd word spe_cmd_word; doorbell 0x70093000=1; job desc 0x70092020; commit immediately or defer (spe_job_deferred_flag=1).
Wait deferred job: halt if inconsistent; result = *(u32*)0x70093010 -> *param_1; clear flags; commit next cmd (0x7009201c = spe_cmd_word).
One-shot: 0x7009200c=3 (SPE bit-writer mode), spe_cmd_pending=1, deferred=0, active flag=1. All NAL bit-writing is delegated to the SPE bit-writer engine.
Full init: memset avc_ctx_array (0x170=2x0xb8); spe_code_download(); enc_reg_clear(); enc_me_regs_clear(); spe_irq_flag_clear(); enc_ids_invalidate().
avc_stream.c: assert ch<2; g_avc_ctx_ptr = avc_ctx_array_2x0xb8 + ch*0xb8; return enc_done_flag if ctx->enabled else 0.

avc_stream.c: dbg_mark(0); select ctx; drain 3-deep cmd ring (cmd_queue_pop into 0x48-byte buf); on frame boundary (img+0x28 vs +0x20): mark(3), avc_stream_frame_cmd (ctx+0x58, ctx+0x5d, cmd), mark(4), mark(0xffff).
Returns constant 5 = this coprocessor node/CPU id (syslog channel id, mbox self id).
True iff param (as signed long) < 5 AND addr in SHM alias window ((addr & 0xf0000000) maps to +0x50000000 offset) - accepts 0xB0000000-0xBFFFFFFF.
Bidirectional shared-memory alias: 0xB0000000 domain <-> 0x40000000, 0xC0000000 <-> 0x60000000 (xor 0xF0000000 / 0xA0000000), else identity. Maps this core's view onto the other domain's SHM window.
interrupts.c:0xa2: assert id<=0x6f; irq_priority_table[id]=prio; irq_handler_table[id]=handler.
clic0.c:0x23: assert id<=0x6f; *(u8*)(0x2800400+id)=enable - Core-Local Interruptor.
mailbox.c:0x5c: assert current class; scan 25-entry mbox desc table for {owner,cpu,fn} match; claim slot (inuse=1); class 1 = IRQ rx: install mbox_rx_dispatch handler + CLIC enable; returns ep index.
mailbox.c:0xbe: validate, read peer id from desc table, assert loop on transfer, mbox_data_write payload to peer mbox register (base from DAT_700d6708).
Separate helper reads bit 0 from MMIO address 0x9012184C. This is distinct from the OTP data-row window at 0x90126000; its semantic relationship to OTP provisioning is not established.

FreeRTOS heap_5_ext region allocator (read-only context). Block header = 0x10 bytes: [0]=next free ptr XOR'd with global cookie DAT_ram_b021f788 (safe-linking); [8]=u32 block size (incl 0x10 header). User ptr = block+0x10. Request size is rounded up: total = req+0x10, then if (req&0xf) total=(total&~0xf)+0x10; i.e. usable = total-0x10 >= req. For malloc(0x138): total=0x150, user usable 0x140. Consequence: an OOB write past a 0x138 buffer must exceed offset 0x140 (from user ptr) to hit the next block's size/next fields; the free-list next pointer is XOR-encoded so it cannot be forged without the global cookie (not BLE-leakable).

System_HaltForever: clears mstatus.MIE immediately, invokes the optional system halt hook and two firmware shutdown helpers, then enters a non-returning infinite loop. A direct saved-ra target can reach this entirely in resident firmware without a cache flush or attacker-supplied instruction bytes.
Single-instruction c.j self-loop at the end of System_HaltForever. Redirecting saved ra here bypasses the preceding MIE clear and shutdown hooks; this instruction itself leaves mstatus unchanged.

check_flash_area_writeable(fm, partition, addr, len): the ONLY write confinement.
- partition valid: allow iff ((*(u32*)(partition+0x18) >> 1) & 3) == 3. - partition == 0 (ProgramFlashRange path): iterate the global table (fm+0x30, count byte fm+0x38, stride 0x1c). For each entry: if addr < size(+0x10)+base(+0x14) then (a) if addr+len <= base -> no overlap, accept; (b) else overlap -> reject only when type != 3. addr past every partition -> accept.
NO-OP IN THIS BUILD (proven): the table at ram:0xb01f59b8 (gp=0xb01f5f00, 20 entries) has field_18 == 0x06 or 0x07 for EVERY entry, so ((field>>1)&3) == 3 (writable) for all. The function therefore never returns false on the global path, and gaps outside all partitions are accepted too. Note also the overlap test uses a 32-bit add (int)addr+(int)len which can wrap, and fm_flash_write later truncates addr with c.addiw (sign-extend low 32 bits).

source address is truncated: s1 = (int)src_addr (sext.w), i.e. only low 32 bits of the (base+offset) reach the flash driver. Combined with the wrapping check above this can address an arbitrary 32-bit flash location.

RingUart_ConfigureHardware: low-level UART hardware initialization used by RingUart_OpenConfigured. It derives the baud divisor from the current clock, sets UART pin routing through IOMUX (or UART4 clock gates), programs line control/divisor/FIFO and modem-control bits, then sets g_uart_open and per-port character timing on success. Stage3 calls this directly for UART0 at 921600 baud, 8N1, to match the serial console setting; it does not call Notify_Enable.

iot_flash_read(a0=handle,a1=offset,a2=dst,a3=len). Bound: a1 <= (long)(int)g_spi_flash_size AND a3 + (a1 & 0xffffffff) <= g_spi_flash_size then flash_xip_read_to_ram(a1 & 0xffffffff, a2, a3, 0). BUG CANDIDATE (integer overflow): a3 is a signed 64-bit long fed into an unsigned add; a negative/huge a3 (e.g. -1) wraps the sum to offset-1, passes, then the XIP memcpy uses a3 as an enormous size_t -> OOB write. fm_flash_read masks a3 to 32 bits, but flash_read_retry passes it through unmasked. main_app::media_video_video_tuning_file_load. Loads flash bundle element type 0xb into global tuning buffer DAT_ram_b0206b80 (8 x 0x1a5a-byte ISP tuning slots). Asserts if bundle_load_element_to_addr fails. Called from media_video_init. The data is SHA-256 verified against an authenticated digest, so tuning bytes are not attacker-forgeable when secure boot is enforced.

CHealthReport ACMD handler is a two-instruction success no-op: it returns 0 for every opcode and does not inspect arguments. The constructor separately logs that the task load monitor is not supported.

CHealthReport registers its primary RuntimeObject with target name CHealthReport. Its slot +8 points to CHealthReport_AcmdNoop at b00f1a0c, which returns success 0 for all opcodes; constructor log says the task load monitor is not supported.

CPowerModeManager registered ACMD interface body (called through adjustor thunk at b00f21ac, which subtracts 0x10 from this). Recognizes opcodes 0x10001, 0x1006C, and 0x1009F. 0x10001 handles subtypes 1..4 with selectors 0x101/0x102/0x103 to query or update power/timer state; 0x1006C logs and performs a delay/time-based state operation; 0x1009F sets a boolean state through a helper. Unknown combinations return 0. Exact public semantic names for the internal state fields are unresolved.
a3/param_4 = 0 -> selects the production HTTPS endpoint branch; the http://ckms / http://cmms branch is not taken here

CStreamingSessionMars subtype dispatcher used by opcode 0x10001. Subtype 2 selectors 0x101/0x102/0x103 return the current ding ID, LV termination reason (and refreshes/reset sentinel state), and uptime. Subtype 9 conditionally snapshots/locks the ding ID when request flags intersect 0x380; subtype 10 conditionally unlocks and clears the cached ding ID. Other subtype/selector paths return null.

CStreamingSessionMars ACMD handler. Opcode 0x10001 delegates to CStreamingSessionMars_SubtypeDispatch. Opcode 0x10018 selectors 0/1/2 invoke a streaming command virtual method; selector 8 logs/forwards a termination reason (0..2 accepted), selector 9 invokes a virtual abort/stop operation, selector 10 logs active state and session ID, and selector 12 stores LV termination reason when <=0x2C0. Invalid selector 8 returns 0x0D; unhandled selector/opcode paths return success 0.

CStreamingSessionMars registers its embedded RuntimeObject at offset +8. Its actual ACMD vtable slot +8 is adjustor thunk b00f8422 -> CStreamingSessionMars_AcmdDispatch at b00f82bc; supported operations are 0x10001 and 0x10018.
Shared base ACMD slot: accepts any opcode by storing the 32-bit opcode at this+0xEC and returns success 0. Targets retaining the base vtable therefore accept calls without opcode-specific behavior.

CDingerStatsGT registered ACMD thunk adjusts the secondary-interface pointer by -8 and enters CDingerStatsGT_AcmdDispatchBody. Opcode 0x10001 supports subtype 2 selectors 1..19, returning pointers to metric fields at offsets +0x184..+0x1BC, +0x140, +0x14C, +0x154, and +0x30C; subtype 5 with selectors 1..19 clears the corresponding metric. Unknown opcodes return 0x0D; unsupported subtype/selector combinations return 0.

CMars_CoPro registered ACMD interface body (adjustor thunk b0103436 subtracts 0xC8 from this). Opcode 0x10001 forwards subtype handling to b0102ae0. Opcode 0x10023 succeeds only when object field +0x890 indicates the operation is allowed, toggles state and sets +0x89C; 0x10024 clears +0x89C, resets helpers and issues operation 0x34. Opcode 0x10073 starts/stops a timer-like force-MD request (interval param3*1000) through the timer service. Opcode 0x10091 selector 0 calls vtable +0xB0; selector 1 calls vtable +0x40 with operation 0x11D and supplied value. Unknown commands return 0x0D; unsupported 0x10091 selectors return 0x0D.

OTP bit-range reader exposed through the COtp_Mars class vtable. In current cross-reference data, references to this function are data/vtable pointers only; no direct app-shell ACMD/CMD call or numeric opcode mapping was found.

CPcuUploader handler (class from s_CPcuUploader_ram_b01d2308). Runs in the CPcu/'MARS' captalk task. Callers: FUN_ram_b010662c @ ram:b0106826 and FUN_ram_b0108c88 @ ram:b0108d7a (CCentcom state machines). At ram:b0107924 it calls JsonDocument_ParseString(&uStack_e0,&body) on the HTTP response body (heap std::string buffer built by FUN_ram_b01be5ce(&buf,0x900)); this is attacker-influenced cloud JSON. It then reads keys upload_url. The recursive parser is Json_ParseValue ram:b017cfc0 (see that plate for the stack-exhaustion analysis).
CALL: JsonDocument_ParseString(cloud PCU HTTP response body) -- attacker-controlled JSON path into the recursive Json_ParseValue.

RSL-pipeline RX callback invoked with (this, incomingPacketHolder). Forwards to RTP_DepacketizePacket(this+0x5b0, packetHolder). this+0x5b0 is the embedded RTP/CBufferPool session whose first field is the pool object pointer used by RTP_AcquirePayloadBuffer. Logs s_stream_pipeline on failure.

CStreamPipeline_ConfigureRtpSession: builds the pipeline from the SDP/session config (param_3). Copies attacker-independent config into the stream object; if the crypto mask (this+0x70 & 0xffff00) != 0, mallocs a 0x460 SRTP session and SRTP_Session_Construct(this+0x70, codec ids, ssrcs, auth-tag len this+0xd4). Stored at +0x608/+0x618. No packet data reaches here.

The second store profile_out->wep_keys[slot].key_length occurs at copy offset +26. For the current online-handler plan (slot 16, 34-byte passphrase), the memcpy begins at PushNetworkConfigToRnm sp+0x7a: bytes 0..25 cover saved s0 at +0x90, byte 26 overwrites saved s0 byte 4 at +0x94, and bytes 30..33 overwrite saved ra at +0x98. The saved s0 corruption is consistent with a successful non-returning ROP chain, but would break normal return to the event handler if the hijack failed.

Security review: ACMD opcode 0x10012 selector 8 reaches this scan-result enumerator. For each scan record it uses the reported SSID length byte as memcpy size into local_a0, a 33-byte SSID field, with no length validation. Lengths above 32 corrupt adjacent stack locals; sufficiently large lengths overwrite the stack canary and potentially saved control data. Exploitability depends on whether the lower Wi-Fi scan path can emit an SSID length >32; trace source at CWifi_ScanResultsCallback and CWifi_CopyScanResultsToControlBuffer.

CRingNM ACMD dispatcher (network manager). Opcode 0x10001 forwards a subtype to the profile/event routine. Opcode 0x10012 takes subcommand 0..15: profile event, apply config, status transition, MAC query/log, initialize result object, status query/log, ping fixed address, enumerate profiles, log status, netif name, retry router query, set/transition field, or parse-and-ping supplied IPv4. Invalid subcommands return 0x0D.
CRingNM destructor for the 0x7d8-byte object. The primary and secondary vptr locations correspond to CRingNM and its Centcom sink interface at +0x50.

Constructs the 0x7d8-byte CRingNM object. Installs the primary vptr at +0 and the secondary Centcom sink interface vptr at +0x50; the secondary subobject is exposed through g_CentcomNetworkConfigSink. The class layout is represented by the CRingNM structure in the Data Type Manager.

CDingerGT registered ACMD interface body (adjustor thunk b0119750 subtracts 8 from this). Opcode 0x10001 forwards subtype handling to b011924e; 0x10018 logs the RF opcode. Explicit controls: 0x1004D stores/logs four IPv4 bytes; 0x1004E updates a port; 0x1004F enables/disables TLS on the streaming protocol; 0x10051, 0x1005C, and 0x1005D update enable/value pairs; 0x10058 updates rotation state and refreshes it; 0x1006E updates a two-byte feature setting; 0x1007B sets early-stream-start and broadcasts event 0x9F; 0x10080 toggles forced dynamic resolution; 0x10085 forwards a boolean through vtable +0x100; 0x1009B stores/updates a 3-value configuration; 0x1009C sets another value/enable pair. Other opcodes in 0x1004D..0x1005D not explicitly handled fall through as successful no-ops; unknown opcodes also return 0.
Flash-read analysis: Read one-byte audio manifest entry count from storage element 0x1A. Retry indefinitely until exactly 1 byte is read.
Flash-read analysis: Read 40-byte audio manifest entry: name[32], LE32 data-relative offset, LE32 length. Retry indefinitely.

main_app::CAudioPrompt_OggParsePages. NEGATIVE: container->data_post_header region is 0x101 bytes (struct 0x130, field at 0x2f) and len_after_header_to_read is a single byte (<=0xff), so the flash read cannot overrun. Packet length is capped at 200 and copied to buf_ptr + index*0xd0 + 8 (slot 0xd0), and the slot is only used when currently zero. No overflow found.
Flash-read analysis: Read 27-byte Ogg page header at absolute base+position; up to 3 attempts; verify OggS.
Flash-read analysis: Read audio segment <=200 bytes into ring slot+8, up to 3 attempts; skip Opus metadata packets.
Flash-read analysis: Read Ogg lacing table, byte-sized count <=255, up to 3 attempts.

CAudioPrompt ACMD opcode 0x10056: selector 3 queries a virtual status method; selector 1 obtains audio prompt/file details for the selected country/voice; selectors 0 and 2 dispatch prompt playback variants. Country index is constrained to 0/1 (invalid values log and reset to 0). Other selectors return 0x0D.

Computes a CRC32 over the present string values for the three keys in CentcomCredentialHashFieldNames: ssid, passphrase, secret. The values are streamed sequentially into the CRC; key names, separators/lengths, sectype, keyindex, encoding fields, and other config fields are not included. CCentcom_CheckConfigCopiesAndPersistStatus compares this result across primary, backup, and secondary config copies, so equal credential strings can make copies compare equal despite differences in omitted fields.

Timer callback posts ordinary RDK event 0x28 to the CCentcom dispatcher queue. That event is consumed by the RDK FSM and reaches CCentcom_Rdk_RetryRecoveryEventHandler, which reloads a config file/tree and pushes it to the network-config sink. If enqueue fails, the timer is rearmed for one second.

Copies a 16-byte UUID out of the parsed RSS tree (key s_pir_sensitivity_3+0x10). CTree_GetByStringKey result is null-checked, but prov_memcpy always copies 0x10 regardless of stored value length -> potential over-read of adjacent tree storage (infoleak). Dest zeroed first.

Copies file contents between CFile_KVS_ACS-compatible objects through CCentcom_Rdk's 0x8FC-byte scratch buffer at +0x2C0. Queries source size (slot +0x68), opens source in mode 1 and destination in mode 0x14, then copies chunks capped at 0x8FC via source Read (+0x48) and destination Write (+0x50). Used for ring-config backup/restore: primary -> backup before config replacement, and backup -> primary when restoring. Source-size or open failures call RFW_AssertAndHalt and do not continue, so the stack size output is not consumed on a failed size query. A zero-byte read or short destination write is logged and exits the copy loop; both files are then closed, but the function does not propagate that partial-copy failure to its callers. If either close fails, the outer loop reaches the fatal assertion helper. No chunk can exceed the 0x8FC-byte scratch buffer based on the requested size.

Post-boot parser for flash-backed config files. Reads chunks up to 0x8fc into a matching fixed-size serializer input buffer, so the chunk-size guard is satisfied. It subtracts Read's return count without checking for zero; a truncated/corrupt file that returns zero leaves the loop non-progressing. It invokes the JSON serializer on each chunk and ignores the final parse result. Confirmed callers include CCentcom_CheckConfigCopiesAndPersistStatus and config restore paths.
Validates the backup config 8-byte header: requires read length 8, magic 0x6c656f6d, and a nonzero embedded payload length. It does not bound the declared length against storage size.

Fallback RSS handler: takes CTaggedBuffer, gets data, membership-tests the msg id (data+8) against the list at *(DAT_ram_b021f9d0)+0x10, then pushes the tag onto the Rss list via Centcom_RssLst_Get/FUN_b013b96a. No attacker-length copy.

Cloud RSS JSON-RPC handler (RssMsgHandler msg id 0x7b). Reads attacker-controlled CTree fields: the JSON-RPC request text under key "5" (b01cdb30) + its u16 length via CTree_GetShortByStringKey, and a 16-byte "uuid"/ECDSA value. Builds a heap CJsonRpcResponseRss (malloc 0x40, vtable b01e8f40) and dispatches via JsonRpc_ProcessMessage(DAT_ram_b021fa58, reqText, reqLen, uuid, respObj). Endpoint/handler resolution is by method name in the CJsonRpc map -> call target NOT attacker-controlled. NOTE: prov_memcpy(respObj+0x2c, uuidValue, 0x10) is fixed-length with no check that the tree value is >= 0x10 (over-read/infoleak candidate). Auth = cloud/TLS session (no in-function credential gate observed).

Snapshot request (RSS msg 0x6f). CTree_GetByStringKey for the uuid key is NOT null-checked before prov_memcpy(auStack_68, uVar3, 0x10): a request omitting that key yields memcpy(dst,NULL,16) -> NULL-deref DoS. Fixed 0x10 copy otherwise.

CCentcom_Rdk::BuildBleProvCallbacks(this=CCentcom_Rdk, eventHandler). Builds a 0x220 on-stack "callback table" (BleProvProvider) of 17 std::function members at 0x0,0x20,...,0x200, each capturing `this` (CCentcom_Rdk). Then passes it to CSetupSystem_Construct (ram:c0c242ae) which moves it into a malloc(0x220) BleProvProvider handed to CDeviceProvisionFlow at flow+0x70. Called from CCentcom_Rdk_Constructor (ram:b0127b90) when CPlatform vtable[0xa0]==0. INFERRED class identity (proven caller); member-to-command mapping not fully enumerated.

Cloud RSS message dispatch, keyed on msg id at treeNode[1] (offset 8). Attacker reaches this via CCentcom_Rdk_EventDispatcher case 0x8e (param_5 = CTaggedBuffer carrying parsed CTree). Handlers: 0x68/0x73 VOD, 0x6a/0x79, 0x6c->FUN_c0c2691e, 0x6e siren, 0x6f snapshot (CCentcom_HandleSnapshotRequest), 0x70/0x75 autochime uuid, 0x72, 0x74, 0x78, 0x7a FactoryRestore, 0x7b Centcom_RssJsonRpc_Handler, default->CCentcom_RssDefaultHandler. No in-function auth check; trust is at the RSS transport.

CCentcom event dispatcher: case 0x8e routes a cloud RSS message to Centcom_Rdk_RssMsgHandler(this, param_5=buffer, param_2=state). Other cases drive setup/power/motion state. Indirect calls via platform singleton vtables.

CCentcom_Rdk registers target ID "CcomRdk" directly and installs CCentcom_Rdk_AcmdVtable at +0. The ACMD slot +8 is CCentcom_Rdk_AcmdDispatch at b012e8d4. This is the main Centcom command multiplexer; see its function comment for opcode/subcommand behavior.

Restores config from the backup storage element. Reads an 8-byte header and calls CCentcom_ValidateBackupConfigHeader, which checks the magic and only that the embedded 32-bit payload length is nonzero. The restore loop trusts that length without comparing it with Stat/file size and subtracts each Read result without a zero-progress check. A corrupt/truncated backup can therefore cause a non-progressing loop; a very large declared length also drives excessive reads.

Maps sectype='wep' to mode 1, copies keyindex with a two-byte bound but no range validation, and obtains passphrase through Centcom_DecryptCredIntoBuffer with non-decrypting mode/capacity 0x40. Centcom_ValidateCredsEncoding requires passphrase_encoding to be present and not 'encrypted' but does not restrict it to a safe allowlist; Centcom_CopyOrBase64DecodeValue supports base64 output up to 0x3f bytes. CCentcom_PushNetworkConfigToRnm dispatches this generated config through g_CentcomNetworkConfigSink + 0x18 to CRingNM_SetNetworkConfigThunk, which forwards to CRingNM_SetNetworkConfig.

Sink call chain for flash-backed Wi-Fi configuration: build config from the Centcom tree, then invoke g_CentcomNetworkConfigSink->SetNetworkConfig via the secondary interface vtable. This dispatches through CRingNM_SetNetworkConfigThunk into CRingNM_SetNetworkConfig and CRingNM_ApplyE2eeNetworkConfig.

Asynchronous Chime Pro/DNCS credential result callback. On successful result/status checks it calls CCentcom_BuildNetworkConfigFromTree, compares the generated config with the supplied credentials, and either broadcasts event 0x9F when they match or updates provisioning state when they differ. Failed requests are logged and scheduled for retry.

Starts the asynchronous Chime Pro/DNCS credential request. It prepares callback state, registers the callback thunk at ram:b012a240 (which dereferences the callback context and tail-calls CCentcom_Rdk_ChimeProCredentialResultCallback), and submits the request. Callers include CCentcom_Rdk_NetworkStateEventHandler, CCentcom_Rdk_RetryRecoveryEventHandler, and other RDK event/state paths.

CCentcom_WriteConfigFileFromHttpBody(this): network-reachable config write.
open(this+0x2a8, mode 2) -> SetWritePosition(this+0x2a8, 0) -> loop { n = CSerializer_ParseHttpBody(serializer, buf, 0x8fc); if (n==0) break; PWrite(this+0x2a8, buf, n, -1); // vtable +0x50 if (PRead error) ... } then SetWritePosition(0) and writes an 8-byte "moel"+len trailer.
PWrite -> CFileDesc::PWrite -> CFileDesc::WriteDevice -> CStorageElement::Write (linear mode). CStorageElement::Write has NO capacity check, so an HTTP body larger than the target partition overflows write_position into the next flash partition (confinement is only the no-op check_flash_area_writeable). ATTACKER SOURCE: HTTP request body (cloud/app command path).

RDK network-state callback. On event 0xe0 it creates a 45-second ccom_setup timer; if timer creation/start succeeds, it calls FUN_ram_b0123526, zeroes the config output, and immediately calls CCentcom_PushNetworkConfigToRnm. This is a direct asynchronous route from the registered event callback into the WEP profile builder.

Confirmed overwrite trigger route: when the RDK FSM dispatches event 0x28 here, this handler selects primary/backup config loading (CCentcom_LoadConfigFileIntoTree or CCentcom_LoadBackupConfigIntoTree), then calls CCentcom_PushNetworkConfigToRnm. That sink path reaches CRingNM_BuildProfileFromE2eeConfig; a flash-backed WEP key index outside '1'..'6' selects an unchecked profile offset and can overwrite this handler's downstream stack frame.

Log3 reaches this 0xe0 handler: it logs Connect Wifi Sleep Lock at 23:11:29.809, then proceeds to CCentcom_PushNetworkConfigToRnm. The current ROP config omits staticip fields, so the absence of the older Static IP Setting log is expected. Retry events continue afterward, which shows the stage3 payload did not disable interrupts on this app hart.

Factory credential override is the live failure mode for log3.txt. The completed CPfmHdkMarsRed vtable is at ram:b01cab60 (not the base vtable at b01c9488); its +0xa0 entry is CPfmHdkMarsRed::IsFqcModeEnabled at b00d1cf2. InitStorage sets fqc_mode_enabled from byte 0 of the raw fqc_main partition. log3.txt prints aSSID <ringmfg>, aKey <doorbot0>, and pSecType wpa-personal, matching this override branch and proving the flash-backed WEP settings are replaced before Online(0xe0) calls PushNetworkConfigToRnm. Clear fqc_main[0] in the generated image so the injected RingConfig fields reach the WEP profile builder.
possible overwrite here, but according to bot it doesn't trigger

Copies a 0xa0 Wi-Fi network configuration into the Ring config tree: stores SSID and passphrase, maps security type to sectype, copies WEP key_index from input offset +0x88 without range checking, and stores static IP fields. Input validation for BLE WEP occurs earlier in BleProv_DecodeWepCredentials; this function itself does not enforce it.

Inbound RDK/setup callback dispatcher. Event 0xb copies a 0xd0 tagged-buffer payload into a local network-config structure and calls CCentcom_ApplyNetworkConfigToTree, then marks credentials received. This branch changes the live config tree; persistence is performed later by separate config-save paths.

Serial ACMD case 0x1b subcommands 5/6 call overwrite_config_value(config_tree, value=param_6, key=param_5) and save the modified primary/backup config tree. The setter updates existing schema entries and reallocates for longer strings. Case 0x1a posts param_4 as an event before falling through to the 0x1b subcommand range check, so event IDs above 6 may still be queued even though the ACMD returns unsupported.

Startup callback reached from CPfmHdkMarsRed::ProcessDeviceLock. After one-time initialization and device startup work, it posts ordinary RDK event 2 to the dispatcher queue; this begins the non-retry startup path.

CJsonRpc ACMD interface handler. Only opcode 0x10001 is recognized; it requires subtype 2 and selector 0x101, calls CJsonRpc's request-processing helper at b013045c, then returns the stored result/handle at object+0x1F8. All other argument combinations return the default error path.

JsonRpc_ParseAndDispatch: tokenizes attacker JSON-RPC (jsonrpc/method params), requires jsonrpc=="2.0" and a method string, looks the method up in the CJsonRpc endpoint std::map (map head at this+0x1d0), then calls endpoint+0x18. Handler address comes from the registration table (JsonRpc_RegisterEndpoint callers), so method name does not directly control the call target. Timeout param parsed via JsonRpc_TokenToInt. Negative for direct CF hijack.

JsonRpc_ProcessMessage: builds request context (param_6 = CJsonRpcResponseRss), calls JsonRpc_ParseAndDispatch, then serializes the response via param_6 vtable. Param_5 is the 16-byte uuid copied into the response object.

Security review: opcode 0x10059 / selector 3 uses param_4 as an unbounded repetition count for state changes and an IR-delay action. Large values can monopolize the dispatcher/task and cause denial of service. The loop exits at equality (so UINT64_MAX is extremely long but not an arithmetic-wrap infinite loop). Potentially command-triggerable if ACMD console is reachable; no memory corruption observed in this path.
Json_ParseString(out, str): wrapper -> Json_ParseString_Internal(str). xrefs: 0c_networking computed calls ram:c0c3dcf6 / c0c5574e / c0c40240.

JsonDocument_ParseString(out, std::string* body): wrapper -> Json_ParseString_Internal(*body). ATTACKER-CONTROLLED JSON ENTRY. xrefs (canonical): ram:b0107924 (CPcuUploader parses cloud PCU/HTTP response body), ram:b01b3f28 (CSetupMethodWifi_HandleE2eeSetup parses local E2EE enrollment body), plus 0c_networking computed calls ram:c0c57a2e / c0c56eb0 / c0c55d6c / c0c5621a / c0c31756. No depth/stack budget until Json_ParseValue.

RssCmd_BuildJsonRequest(cmdTable, jsonrpc?, cmdId, out_len_key, out_len_val, flags). Linear scan over a 0x18-byte-stride command table until entry.id > 999 (sentinel) or entry.id == cmdId; the >999 gate bounds the scan so it cannot walk off the table for a valid table. Builds a std::string request via the b016-c serialization helpers. No attacker length reaches a fixed buffer here.

Rss_ParseUuid(dst[0x21], uuid16). Hex-formats 16 binary UUID bytes into dst using snprintf(dst+2*i, 0x21-2*i, "%02x", in[i]) -> 32 chars + NUL. Size argument shrinks correctly; no overflow. Caller RSS_Cmd_Dispatcher copies 16 bytes from the parsed DX buffer at global+idx+0x1f.

Rss_ParseFrame(RssStreamBuffer *buf) [buf = DAT_ram_b0212d88].
Inline stream-frame scanner for the RSS/Centcom command protocol. Scans buf->data[scanned .. len] for the '#' (0x23) delimiter; records last delimiter index at +0x10; computes out_len at +0x14 and completion flag / parsed flag. When a full 0x25-byte command tail is delimited and len==0x3d00 it memmoves the tail to the front (FUN_ram_b01c3414). Callers: RSS_Cmd_Dispatcher (b013e8aa, b013e96e). Buffer is fixed 0x3d00 (see the len==0x3d00 gate), so indices are bounded by the stream reader. No attacker-controlled allocation or unchecked copy found in this routine.

RSS_Cmd_Dispatcher(centcom). Main RSS/Centcom command loop: RSS_ParseFrame on the fixed 0x3d00 global stream buffer -> Rss_ParseUuid -> vtable dispatch (param_1->vtable+0x40/+0x48) -> CTree/CTaggedBuffer handoff. The 0x17-byte and 0x18 (uVar4-100) range gates are command-ID filters, not length checks. Reviewed: no attacker-length copy; RSS state is a fixed-size global.

CIsp_MARS interface handler body. The registered secondary-interface vtable slot +8 points to adjustor thunk b01401f6, which subtracts 8 from this before entering here. The handler checks ISP state with FUN_ram_b0140698, then opcode 0x10023 runs actions at b014065e and b014127c; opcode 0x10024 runs b0140dfe. Failure status is 0x15; unsupported opcode returns 0x0D.
Reads exactly 64 bytes from kvsHW/mask_center. On exact success copies first 8 bytes into calibration fields; called from VideoCore_SubmitEncoderConfig.

CSframeE2ee_Decrypt(e2ee, data, len, &outLen) - inbound E2EE entry for audio media frames.
Order of operations: *outLen>=len; len!=0; data!=NULL; (data&0x3f)==0; len<=0x140 ELSE prov_stack_chk_fail_report(0x14a) NORETURN; lock e2ee->0x210; require key-installed flag *(e2ee+0xf48); prov_memcpy(DAT_ram_b0217940, data, len); SFrame_Decrypt(e2ee+0x908, DAT_ram_b0217940, len, data, &outLen); unlock; *outLen updated.
NOTE: CMediaStreamAudio_HandleFrame (b018e13e) calls this ONLY AFTER it already did prov_memcpy(DAT_ram_b021b480, frame, len) with no bound. Any len that overflows that 0x2b2 buffer (>0x2b2) is also >0x140 and therefore triggers the noreturn abort above immediately after the copy. => bounded BSS corruption followed by a guaranteed halt (DoS), not code exec. The ABI-visible check is len<=0x140; staging copy is therefore always in-bounds (0x141 buffer).

CSpeakerJitterBuffer_PushFrame: inserts (param_2,len,param_3) into the CFrameRingBuffer at this+0x10. CFrameRingBuffer_Insert rejects (len+3&~3)+4 > ring capacity (0x854 for the 0xa0/0x104/0x14 ctor args), so the reassembly copy is bounded. Called from HandleFrame with the SFrame-decrypted length (<=0x140) and, on the no-E2EE path, with raw len (<=0x850) - both in-bounds.

CTempSensor dispatch entry. Opcode 0x10001 forwards the subtype and selector to a helper. The helper handles subtype 2 selectors 0x101/0x102/0x103 by returning pointers to object fields at +0x84/+0x88/+0x8C, and subtype 5 selectors 0x102/0x103 via a separate helper. The other observed vtable methods include constant-zero methods and a value at +0x108; exact field meanings are unresolved.

CLightSensor dispatch entry. Opcode 0x10001 forwards subtype/selector to the light-sensor helper; subtype 2 selector 0/1 follows the vtable's getter path, returning 0x0D for unsupported cases. Nearby vtable methods read object fields at +0x10 and +0x78 and compare a measured value against a bound of 1000. Field semantics beyond light-sensor value/range remain unresolved.

CDnsClient ACMD handler. Only opcode 0x10003 is accepted. It requires non-null nested/string pointers, arg4==0, and exact strcmp equality between the nested hostname and supplied string; returns 0 on match and 0x0D otherwise. Null required pointers enter the stack-check failure path.

CHttpClient_ParseResponseHeaders(client). Reads status line into a 1000-byte stack buffer via CHttpClient_ReadLine; alloca-copies the status-line portion; parses the 3-digit status with an explicitly NUL-terminated 4-byte local (disasm b014a378 sb zero,-0x43d), strtoul, range-checks 100..504. Then parses headers, Transfer-Encoding: chunked, and Content-Length (stored at client+0x150). Reviewed: status parse is correctly terminated and bounded -> no memory-safety issue found here.

CEndpointControl ACMD dispatcher. Opcode 0x10001 is accepted only for subtype 6 and forwards to the endpoint-control routine; opcode 0x10047 forwards its subtype and remaining arguments to the endpoint operation routine. Other inputs return 0x0D.

TLS trust-anchor selection: endpoint 0 returns three embedded DER CAs (Amazon Root CA 1, Amazon Root CA 2, Starfield Services Root Certificate Authority - G2); endpoint 3 returns two embedded Amazon Postill/EEA MultiMedia server CA rollover certificates. Other endpoint IDs return no table. CCertStorage_LoadCertsIntoX509 parses the selected DER entries into the mbedTLS CA chain.

Parses only entries returned by CCertStorage_GetEndpointTable for the requested endpoint ID. In this firmware the returned tables are fixed embedded DER arrays (endpoint 0: three roots; endpoint 3: two Amazon EEA Media CA rollover certs); this loader has no file/KVS/ACMD input path and no append/add-certificate path.
Setup HTTPS server TLS: mbedtls_ssl_conf_authmode(cfg, 0) == MBEDTLS_SSL_VERIFY_NONE. No client certificate / mutual auth on the local setup channel.

Initializes the socket's mbedTLS CA chain by loading the embedded CCertStorage table selected by the socket endpoint ID at +0x520. Endpoint 0 is the three public roots (Amazon Root CA 1, Amazon Root CA 2, Starfield Services Root G2); endpoint 3 is the pair of Amazon Postill/EEA MultiMedia server CA rollover certificates. This is distinct from the E2EE ASK/producer certificates.

Runtime client-identity setter: parses caller-provided certificate and private key buffers and installs them as the TLS client's own certificate/key. This is separate from the CA trust chain loaded by CSocket_Mbed_LoadEmbeddedCA; no direct ACMD call path was found in the registered ACMD handler set.

CPwm ACMD handler. Opcode 0x100A1 takes a selector and channel/index: selector 0 writes a byte, selector 1 reads a byte, selector 2 writes a 32-bit value, selector 3 reads a 32-bit value from separate channel tables. Helpers check the index against each table's configured count; nonmatching opcodes return 0x0D.
CLedSpinner ACMD dispatcher. Opcode 0x10032 forwards its one-byte argument to vtable slot +0x10; returns 0 on success, 9 when the callee reports failure, and 0x0D for other opcodes.
CIRLed's registered ACMD vtable slot points here; the handler unconditionally returns 0x0D (unsupported). The adjacent CIRLed methods are not exposed through this target's ACMD slot.

INFOLEAK ASSESSMENT (CFlashConfig::GetConfigField 4-byte heap OOB read): BUG PROVEN: this->cfg_fields(+0x118) = pvPortMalloc(0xc) but GetConfigField always reads 8 bytes at +(idx-0x40); idx=0x48 (used by the ctor itself) reads 4 bytes past the block. EGRESS: the over-read dword lands in the caller's local and is consumed only as a flash read length / base offset (FUN_ram_b01568da / FUN_ram_b015725c), never returned to the attacker. No egress. CANARY: unreachable — heap-adjacent bytes, not the .data canary at b0297260.

Parses flash-backed RingConfig JSON in chunks of at most 0x41 bytes into a 0x578-byte serializer buffer. Chunk capacity is adequate. The loop subtracts the storage Read result from remaining length without checking for zero, so a truncated payload can cause a non-progressing loop.

CRingConfig_BuildFromNvs(this, storage): builds the RingConfig tree from factory NVS. Calls FUN_b0162bd2(fixed_key, "", 0) ~58x to append key nodes into the global CTree builder (DAT_b0220088), then FUN_b0162e84/FUN_b0162c70 to nest the ledpattern/streaming groups, then FUN_b01636a4(CConfig,"RingConfig",tree,0) and stores it at this->ring_config (+0x120). NOTE: the NVS values here are the constant empty string DAT_b01edec0; the key list is static. No flash-controlled length is used to size a local buffer in this function. BuildFromNvs is not itself a memory-safety bug; the untrusted flash bytes go through CSerializer_JSON (capacity-checked, see CFlashConfig/CSerializer). Also installs this->ring_config and calls FUN_b015695c(this, ringconfig, this->storage_element2) to parse flash JSON. Proven.

CFlashConfig::ReloadFactoryConfig: cfg_fields = pvPortMalloc(0xc) is filled with 12 flash bytes. GetConfigField(this,0x44,&local_20) reads offsets 4..11 (ok, must == 0x4c); GetConfigField(this,0x48,&lStack_18) reads offsets 8..15 -> 4 bytes of heap OOB read past the 12-byte block (see CFlashConfig::GetConfigField). The over-read high dword pollutes lStack_18, which is then used as the byte count for FUN_ram_b01568da (flash read in 0x41-byte chunks into factory_buf[0x41]) and as the base offset in FUN_ram_b015725c (b01572c6: *param_2 = *param_3 + 0x4c). Chunking keeps the destination bounded, so this is an OOB READ / read-length influence bug, not a write-overflow primitive, unless the storage-element vtable+0x50 consumer copies more than the chunk.

CFlashConfig ctor (caller allocates 0x130 bytes). Layout proven from disasm: +0x00 vtable=&CFlashConfig_vtable (ram:b01e1d10) +0x08 storage_element (param_2, CStorageElement_ACS*) +0x10 char factory_buf[0x41] (scratch for raw flash/NVS reads) +0x58 lock (passed to FUN_b00cd3c0(4,...) and scope-locked by FUN_b01015bc/FUN_b00dfd6a) +0x100 field_100 (FUN_b00cd3c0 result) +0x108 storage_element2 (param_3, used for factory NVS reads) +0x110 loaded flag +0x118 cfg_fields = malloc(0xc) (12 x 8-byte fields, indices 0x40..0x4b) +0x120 ring_config (CRingConfig*, malloc(0x28)) +0x128 json_serializer (CSerializer_JSON*, malloc(0xf0); base CSerializer allocs a 0x578 data buffer, capacity stored at CSerializer+0x20) Asserts s_CFlashConfig (ram:b01e1bc0). DAT_ram_b021ffd0 = this is a singleton pointer.

CTimeTrig ACMD dispatcher. Opcode 0x10003 validates a non-null event record and compares its event ID/type with the supplied value; opcode 0x10004 processes timer/event state (including next-deadline updates, expiry/repeat handling, and trigger-state notification). Opcode 0x10023 calls the global time-trigger scheduling helper; opcode 0x10024 calls a second schedule/update helper; opcode 0x1002A invokes the per-object scheduling helper. Unsupported commands return 0x0D; malformed required event pointers trigger the stack-check failure path.

CCheckpoint ACMD handler: accepts opcode 0x10049 only, requires one argument of type 1, then writes the two payload values as 16-bit checkpoint category/value fields at b01fa3a0 and b01fa3a2. Other opcode/type combinations return 0x0D. Evidence supports the storage behavior; higher-level consumer semantics of the two fields remain unresolved.

main_app::CFile_KVS_makeClusterName(name, uint cluster, char ctx[0x30]) -> bool
Zero-fills ctx then formats "%s%c%hx" (name, '#', cluster). Returns false if the formatted length would reach 0x30 (=> "Filename too big"). The %hx format truncates the cluster index to 16 bits.

CFile_KVS_ACS::CFile_KVS_ACS (ctor)
Class: CFile_KVS_ACS (name string ram:0xb01e3240, vtable ram:0xb01e3420). Allocation: callers malloc(0x228). Base ctor CFile::CFile (ram:0xc0c8047e) zeroes the CFileDesc fields, sets the CFile vtable ram:0xc0cb4fd0 and stores the name pointer at this+0x220. This ctor then swaps in the CFile_KVS_ACS vtable. Asserts strlen(name) < 0x2e (0xf7).
Proven: decompiled ctor + xrefs at ram:0xb00db414..b00db544, c0c1b8a0.

Reads cluster 0 and returns the flash-controlled signed 32-bit logical value length from header offset +4 after checking KVS magic and Flash_ReadFileDecode status. It applies no upper bound to positive lengths. CFile_KVS_ACS::Stat preserves this value; readers that allocate by Stat size must impose their own cap.
CFile_KVS_makeClusterName(name,0,ctx): boolean formatting result ignored here. This is NOT the Flash_ReadFileDecode call; decode status is checked at b015bb16.
Reads cluster zero (512-byte buffer), maps decode return through CFile_KVS_mapFlashError, checks magic 0x4B565300, then consumes stored signed length at +4. Decode status is NOT ignored.
Reads existing cluster zero to retain payload/header and determine previous cluster count during file-length update/shrink.

CFile_KVS_ACS::Stat(this, int out[3]) [vtable slot 13]
Fills out[0]=size (signed 32-bit from header, ram:b015be2e), out[1]=(size+0x207)&0xfffffe00 (rounded cluster bytes), out[2]=(short)this->field_98 (0x98). If getValueSize<0, zeroes the 12-byte output. Asserts out != 0 (0x117).
BUG B4 (inferred, integer overflow): (int)size + 0x207 at ram:b015be34 can overflow int32 when the on-flash size is near 0x7fffffff.

CFile_KVS_ACS::ReadInternal(this, dst, len, offset)
On-flash KVS read primitive (called by ::Read). * locks (FUN_b01015bc), size = CFile_KVS_getValueSize(this->name). * rejects if size<0 or offset >= (unsigned)size [ram:b015c0ee-b015c0f4] * file byte offset = (int)(offset + 8) [ram:b015c116, 32-bit addiw] * cluster index = (fileoff >> 9) & 0xffff, in-cluster = fileoff & 0x1ff * per cluster: makeClusterName -> Flash_ReadFileDecode(handle,ctx,buf,0x200) then copies min(len - copied, bytes-to-end-of-cluster) into dst.
BUGS (see plate on ram:b015c0ee / b015c116): B1 missing bound: only offset<size is checked, never offset+len<=size, and len is not clamped to size-offset. Reading past a record's length walks into later clusters (other records / stale data) => over-read. B2 32-bit signed overflow: offset+8 at ram:b015c116 (addiw) can wrap for large on-flash size (>=0x7ffffff8), yielding negative file offset. B3 cluster index is truncated to 16 bits (ram:b015c118-b015c11e), and makeClusterName formats it with %hx => aliasing for >64K clusters.

INFOLEAK ASSESSMENT (CFile_KVS_ACS::ReadInternal over-read): BUG PROVEN (missing offset+len<=size clamp; see plate). Reached via the CFile_KVS_ACS vtable Read slot ram:0xb015c29c / b015c07e, which skips the base CFileDesc::ReadBuffered clamp at ram:0xc0c8067e. DATA SOURCE = SPI flash: Flash_ReadFileDecode @ ram:b00e3c14 reads 0x200-byte clusters from the KVS file into the local 512-byte auStack_278, then copies [min(len-copied, bytes-to-end-of-cluster)] to the caller dst. So the over-read exposes *later flash clusters* (other KVS records / stale flash), NOT RAM. EGRESS = caller-supplied dst; no handler in the reviewed BLE/RSS/JSON paths returns that raw buffer, so no attacker-facing egress was proven (inferred: adjacent KVS records e.g. wificred/ringconfig could be exposed if a stats/config reader forwards an oversized buffer; needs runtime confirmation). CANARY: unreachable. g_stack_canary is in RAM @ ram:0xb0297260, not the SPI flash this primitive reads, and the value is regenerated every boot.
B1: only checks offset < size; no offset+len<=size clamp, and len is never reduced to size-offset (base CFileDesc::ReadBuffered clamps to valid_len-offset).
B2: 32-bit signed add (addiw) of offset+8, can overflow for large on-flash size.
B3: cluster index truncated to 16 bits (and makeClusterName formats with %hx).
Reads a named 512-byte file cluster before copying requested portion to file-reader output. CFile_KVS_mapFlashError accepts any nonnegative decode result.

CFile_KVS_ACS::Read (vtable slot 2, overrides CFileDesc::ReadBuffered)
Signature (RISC-V ABI): Read(CFile_KVS_ACS *this, void *dst, ulong len, ulong offset) a0=this, a1=dst, a2=len, a3=offset (the 4th arg is forwarded to CFile_KVS_ACS::ReadInternal; it is NOT stale). Zeroes this->last_error (0x210); if dst==0 or len==0 sets last_error=5 and returns 0; otherwise tail-jumps to ReadInternal.
NOTE vs base: CFileDesc::ReadBuffered clamps len to valid_len(0x218)-offset; this override does not (see ReadInternal bug notes).

CFile_KVS_ACS::WriteInternal(this, void *src, ulong len, int offset): writes `len` bytes of a KVS value starting at logical byte offset `offset` (a3; CFile_KVS_ACS::Write tail-jumps here passing the caller's a3 through). It splits the value into 0x200-byte clusters named "%s#%hx" where cluster = (offset+8)>>9, TRUNCATED to 16 bits by %hx, and calls Flash_WriteFileEncode per cluster.
The flash address is derived from the cluster NAME, not from `offset`, so a huge offset does not directly index flash; the practical risk is cluster-name aliasing / writing beyond the value's declared size (CFile_KVS_getValueSize is fetched but not enforced). This is NOT the strongest raw-address primitive — see CStorageElement_ACS::WriteRaw.
Read-modify-write: reads existing cluster to preserve bytes preceding an unaligned file write.
Reads back newly written 512-byte cluster into global verification buffer and compares all 512 bytes against intended data.

CGpio ACMD handler for opcode 0x1000F. It accepts argument type 0 or 1 and delegates to GPIO virtual methods (vtable offsets +0x70/+0xB0 or +0xC0); this is an operation on GPIO state, not an OTP/eFuse access path.

Fallback stub-chain pivot: the preceding instruction at b015d2c4 is jalr ra,20(sp). The current flash_rce.bin.rce.json instead selects the zero-preflush trampoline at c0c247b4 and landing at b0193fdc; this fallback is not used by that plan.

CTimer_Rtc_ACS registered ACMD interface body (called through adjustor thunk b015d454, which subtracts 0xE8 from this). Recognizes opcode 0x10011 with selector 0x309; if object+0x138 is absent it logs an RTC handler error, otherwise calls vtable slot +0x10 and logs the RTC tick value. Returns 0 for this exact command and also 0 for unrecognized commands.

CTimer_Rtc_ACS registers its RuntimeObject at outer offset +0xE8. Its vtable at b01e38c8 slot +8 is thunk b015d454, which adjusts by -0xE8 and enters the RTC tick handler b015d3ec; opcode 0x10011 selector 0x309 triggers the RTC tick/log path. Other operations are ignored.

CSerializer_ReadHttpBody (AddData, serializer vtable slot +0xd8): appends a chunk (param_2, length param_3) byte-by-byte into this+0x80, bounded by this+0x88 < this+0x20 (capacity). Asserts (this+0x20 < param_3). The JSON callback then parses incrementally. Because the buffer capacity (0x578 for CFlashConfig) is enforced before every byte write, the JSON parse path is NOT an overflow here. Proven.

CTree::InsertKeyStr(name, value, type): appends one 0x18-byte CTreeNode at DAT_b0220088 + count*0x18 (count=DAT_b0220082) with NO capacity check, then pushes `count` at index slot DAT_b0220078 + DAT_b0220080*4 while DAT_b0220080 decrements. The 0xfffe underflow guard fires only AFTER the slot store. Node fields: +0x00 name, +0x08 value, +0x10 type/value_len, +0x12 order=0xffff, +0x14/0x15 flags=0, +0x16/0x17=0. UNBOUNDED-INSERT BUG (proven arithmetic, latent): a caller inserting more than `capacity` nodes overruns the node region into/past the contiguous index stack and ultimately the FreeRTOS heap block. Audited callers (BuildFromNvs, CSetupMethodWifi, CEventReporter, CFastpingTest, CEgressTest, CRingNM, CHttpServer, CHttpClient, RssCmd, token/JSON-RPC serializers) all size capacity to the exact node count; no attacker-derived count was found, so it is not reachable as of this audit.

CTree::InsertGroup(name, flags): same unbounded append path as InsertKeyStr; zeroes the value and stores `flags` at CTreeNode+0x14. Consumes one node slot and one index slot. Used for group/parent nodes.
CTree::InsertSchemaKey(name, type_word): same unbounded append path; zeroes the value and stores type_word at CTreeNode+0x14. Builds schema-only leaves (no value). One node + one index slot.

CTree::CloneNode(src): appends a new CTreeNode copying src->name/src->value/src->type, using the same unbounded node-index path as InsertKeyStr, and pushes its index. Returns the new node. Used by CTree::RepeatGroup. LATENT unbounded-insert bug; node growth is members*(repeat-1).

CTree::PushChildCount(neg_count): pushes -neg_count into the index stack (group marker for the preceding neg_count nodes). No node is allocated; consumes one index-stack slot without a capacity check. Guard 0xfffe after store.

CTree::RepeatGroup(group_marker_handle, repeat): repeats the preceding child group (repeat-1) extra times by cloning each member node and re-pushing its marker; node growth = members*(repeat-1). No capacity check. Callers must size BeginBuild capacity for the multiplied node count; e.g. 0c_networking::FUN_c0c63f5e passes repeat=10 with capacity S+3+6*10 (over-allocates, safe). repeat<1 -> assert.

CTree::InsertChecksumArray(prefix, n, shorts): for n in [1,1000) inserts n named nodes (prefix+checksum, value from shorts[n]) and pushes the -n child marker. n==0 or n>=1000 -> assert. Used by RssCmd_BuildJsonRequest with n == the table-entry byte field; BeginBuild(n,1) is an exact fit. Proven.

CTree::InsertStringArray(char** vec, n): inserts n key nodes (one per vec entry) then pushes the -n child marker; consumes n node slots + n+1 index slots. n==0 -> assert. Unbounded; used by CHttpClient ctor (BeginBuild(8,1), n=8 exact) and 0c_networking::FUN_c0c62d6a (BeginBuild(N+1,2), n=N exact).

CTree global builder allocator: BeginBuild(node_capacity, extra_index_slots). Allocates (extra + capacity*7)*4 bytes = capacity*0x18 node region + (capacity+extra)*4 index stack. Globals: DAT_b0220088=node base; DAT_b0220078=base+capacity*0x18 (index stack top); DAT_b0220080=capacity+extra-1 (index cursor, ushort, decrements); DAT_b0220082=0 (node count, ushort). capacity==0 -> assert/halt. PROVEN: node region holds exactly `capacity` 0x18-byte CTreeNode slots; index stack holds capacity+extra 4-byte signed entries (negative value = child-count marker). No capacity check exists in the Insert* family, so every caller MUST pass capacity == number of inserted nodes.

CTree::ClearValues(node): walks a materialized CTree's node list (count at node[idx+0x18]-2) and releases each node's value object via vtable+0x18, clearing node+0x08/+0x10. No writes outside the materialized CTree; not related to the builder overflow.

CTree::Materialize(dst, root_name, tree_handle, external_src): converts the global builder arena into a permanent CTree object (size 0x28). Allocates depth*2 + (count+1)*0x18 and deep-copies the `count` nodes (DAT_b0220082), allocating value objects via FUN_b01619a6 and vtable +0x28/+0x30, then frees the arena and clears the builder globals. Reads DAT_b0220082 directly, so an over-count from the unbounded insert would also drive this copy out of bounds. CTree layout: +0x00 node_array, +0x08 value_alloc, +0x10 nodes_copy, +0x18 index_table, +0x20 depth, +0x21 owns_nodes.

CTree helper: find an existing entry by key and replace its value. The actual entry writer reallocates when the replacement string exceeds the current storage capacity; this helper does not impose a key-specific value-length cap.

During Wi-Fi/network initialization, reads three OTP rows 0x36B..0x36D (six bytes) through the app OTP accessor and passes the bytes to a networking helper if nonzero. This looks like a provisioned network identity/MAC, but the callee semantics are unresolved.

main_app::bundle_load_element_to_addr(type, dst). Reads bundle element `type` from flash into dst. PROVEN: header comes from Peripherals::SYSCTL.BUND_HDR @0x90000000; offset/size = BUND_HDR_ELEMENT0_FILE_OFF/SIZE[idx]. flash_xip_read_to_ram(file_off+0x200+slot_base, dst, size). Then SHA-256(data) is compared to the 0x20-byte digest at 0x9000022c+idx*0x34; on mismatch dst is zeroed and error returned. NOTE: the flash read into dst happens BEFORE the hash check, so an oversized (authenticated) size would overflow dst transiently, then be zeroed. bundle_hdr_install copies the 0xd20-byte header from the authenticated/decrypted SBIH image (sbih_auth_and_decrypt_G), so size+digest are authenticated under secure boot.

flash_read(offset,dst,len) -> flash_xip_read_to_ram(offset & 0xffffffff, dst, len, 0). No bound check here and len is NOT masked to 32 bits. The only guard is the (offset+len) <= chip->size 64-bit add inside flash_xip_read_to_ram, which wraps for huge/negative len. In practice the only caller (FUN_b016845a) uses a constant 0x10.

Checked app OTP row accessor: requires initialized handle and output pointer, rejects row indices >= 0x400, then delegates to otp_read_row_app. COtp_Mars_ReadBits uses this to read rows and extract requested bitfields.

main_app::crypt_LoadPublicKey(pk_ctx, keybuf, keylen) == mbedtls pubkey parse Attacker fully controls (keybuf,keylen) (flash-resident bundle key). Requires keybuf[keylen-1]==0 to take the PEM path (mbedtls_pem_read_buffer needs a NUL-terminated buffer; the NUL is checked before strstr -> no over-read if the caller's buffer is exactly keylen and last byte is 0 -- the caller even mallocs exactly keylen, so keybuf[keylen-1] is in bounds). Non-NUL-terminated -> treated as DER via mbedtls_x509_get_pubkey with an explicit end pointer keybuf+keylen. ASN.1 lengths are bounds-checked against that end pointer. No length-prefix used as a copy/alloc size without an end check found. NOTE: caller must still provide 1 spare NUL byte; only keylen bytes are allocated, so a PEM blob lacking an internal NUL is still parsed as DER (bounded).

x509_crt_parse_der_core(crt, buf, len, alloc_mode, ext_cb, ext_ctx). This is the standard mbedtls DER certificate parser (own_buffer path copies the raw cert with prov_memcpy(...,raw_len) into a buffer allocated via thunk_FUN_ram_b00c4436(1,<size>)). All ASN.1 field reads go through mbedtls_asn1_get_tag/get_len which bound each field against the end pointer for that TLV; the many explicit end-pointer comparisons (pbVar4/pbVar14/pbVar15) enforce it. Reviewed: no missing bounds check found in the length math; this is upstream mbedtls. Attack surface is the TLS server certificate (pre-auth), but the code is the stock parser.

main_app::crypt_RsaVerify(sig, siglen, msg, msglen, expected, explen, key, keylen, mode) s4=sig s5=siglen s2=msg s3=msglen s1=expected s9=explen s6=keyblob s8=keybloblen. Guards: msg,msglen,expected non-NULL, explen==0x100 exactly, keyblob,keybloblen non-NULL. Parses the flash keyblob via crypt_LoadPublicKey(this=&pk_ctx_on_stack, keyblob, keybloblen) then verifies with crypt_RsaPkcs1Verify @ b017499e using expected (hdr+0xa0,0x100). Stack has a canary (g_stack_canary checked on exit). pk_ctx is a 16-byte mbedtls_pk_context {pk_info*, pk_ctx*}; the RSA context itself is heap-allocated (mbedtls_pk_setup b0171a3a). No attacker-controlled write reaches pk_ctx here.

crypt_RsaVerify_BundleKey(sig, siglen, msg, msglen, expected, explen, key, keylen) Thin trampoline: stores 1 as the 9th (stack) argument and tail-calls crypt_RsaVerify @ b017c318. The extra arg is the pk type/mode used by the b0171a7a pk_info dispatch. All eight register args are forwarded unchanged (a0..a7), so VerifySignature's call maps 1:1 onto crypt_RsaVerify. Verified: disasm b017c452 sets sp[0]=1 then calls b017c318 (no register clobber).

Json_DecodeString(node, ctx): decodes a quoted JSON string in place. Output buffer is allocated with size = raw_span - backslash_count + 1 (ctx[4] allocator), which is always >= the number of decoded bytes (a \uXXXX escape consumes 6 raw bytes for <=4 UTF-8 output), so no overflow. Sets node+0x18=0x10 and node+0x20=decoded buffer. Uses node+0x100/0x200 flag bits in the free path.

Json_NodeAlloc(alloc_fn): (*alloc_fn)(0x40) + memset. alloc_fn comes from ParseCtx[4] = PTR_pvPortMalloc (ram:b01f8ef8 -> ram:b00d0c72), i.e. the FreeRTOS heap_5_ext pvPortMalloc (malloc_sram/psram per DAT_ram_b01fa270). Always 0x40-byte Json_Node. This is the allocation performed *during* a recursive parse, so it is the consumer of any heap metadata corrupted below a task stack; free-list pointers are XOR-masked with the mcycle-derived cookie and range-asserted, so forging is infeasible.

Json_ParseStringCore(str,out_end,strict): builds the stack ParseCtx {ptr,len,pos,depth=0,alloc=PTR_pvPortMalloc ram:b01f8ef8 -> ram:b00d0c72/ram:b00c43ea}, allocates the 0x40 root node and calls the recursive Json_ParseValue. NO stack/depth budget of its own; the only bound is ctx[3]<1000 inside Json_ParseValue. On overflow it frees the partial tree (Json_NodeFreeRecursive). Security analysis: see Json_ParseValue ram:b017cfc0 (RULED OUT for CF hijack; DoS).
Json_ParseString_Internal(str): thin wrapper -> Json_ParseStringCore(str,0,0). Reached from Json_ParseString ram:b0138638 and JsonDocument_ParseString ram:b0138652.

Audio inbound E2EE/decrypt entry (network RX). param_2 is a holder whose *param_2 is the depacketized packet; vtable slot1 returns {data=obj+0x50, len=*(u32*)(obj+0x44)} (CRtpPayloadBuffer). If E2EE ctx (media+0x408)==0 the raw frame is pushed straight to CSpeakerJitterBuffer (no copy). Otherwise prov_memcpy(&g_audioStaging_b021b480, data, len) is UNBOUNDED but is immediately followed by CSframeE2ee_Decrypt which noreturn-aborts for len>0x140; staging is 0x2b2 and max len = pool node 0x540-0x50 = 0x4f0, so any len>0x140 corrupts <=0x23e bytes of adjacent BSS then halts (DoS). len<=0x140 copy is in-bounds. VERDICT: bounded-BSS + guaranteed halt, no in-hart control-flow target; not RCE.

RISK (Round18-T2): prov_memcpy(0xb021b480, frame, len) with NO cap; SFrame's len<0x141 check runs later in CSframeE2ee_Decrypt 0xb014392e. g_sframe_rx_stage = 0x2b2 B BSS; inbound len up to ~0x4f0 -> up to ~574 B overflow. len>0x140 then hits noreturn abort -> remote DoS (post-SRTP/E2EE). No function ptr in window -> RCE not demonstrated.

RTP_AcquirePayloadBuffer(outHolder, poolObj, srcCtx): gets a fixed-size buffer from the media pool, sets vtable to CRtpPayloadBuffer_vtable (b01e8630), capacity=*(u32*)(pool+0x9320)-0x50, payload_len=0, and binds srcCtx (packet+0x20) via FUN_ram_b010ba0a. Pool slot2 (b00fac56) returns pool+0x9318; slot3 (b0100f60) aborts if requested size > *(u32*)(pool+8). Capacity is thus a fixed node size, not attacker-controlled.

RTP depacketizer. Input packet object (CRtpPayloadBuffer) read via vtable slot2 -> {data=+0x50, len=+0x44}. All accesses bounds-checked against end=data+len: version==2, header=12+CC*4<=end, extension header bounded, padding `end-=end[-1]` re-checked by `hdr<=end`. Payload len=end-hdr. Allocates via RTP_AcquirePayloadBuffer; capacity = node_size-0x50 (fixed, pool slot2 = pool+0x9318/field+8); memcpy only if capacity>=payload_len. VERDICT: no OOB found.
Maps an incoming SSRC (param_2) to a fixed stream slot 0..3 by comparing against session+0x14/+0x18/+0x1c/+0x20. Returns 0 for the first match / unknown. Bounded: never yields >3.

SRTP_BuildNonceAndIndex(session, idx, seq, roc, outNonce16, outLen, isRtcp): copies the 12-byte session nonce salt (session+0x6a RTP / +0x8a RTCP) to outNonce, XORs seq bytes, and for RTP XORs the 4-byte session+0xa0+idx*0xc counter; for RTCP XORs the 4-byte session+0x9c+idx*0xc index. idx is the 0..3 value from SRTP_GetStreamIndexFromSsrc, so all offsets are bounded (<=0xc7). Sets *outLen=0xc.

SRTP AES-GCM decrypt helper. Copies param_8 (ciphertext length) into a 1400-byte stack staging buffer AFTER checking `if (0x540 < param_8) noreturn abort`; then mbedtls_gcm_auth_decrypt. Max 0x540 < 1400 => staging copy in-bounds. VERDICT: bounded.

SRTP/SRTCP inbound processing. Packet is {void*data; u32 len}. Rejects CSRC!=0. SSRC (RTP data[8..11]; SRTCP data[4..7]) mapped by SRTP_GetStreamIndexFromSsrc to a fixed 0..3 index; index only addresses session+0x9c+idx*0xc and session+0xa0+idx*0xc. Len validated >= header (0xc RTP/8 RTCP) before header reads. SRTP_BuildNonceAndIndex derives nonce/rollover. SRTP_AesGcmCrypt enforces len>=hdr+0x10(+4 RTCP). VERDICT: index and lengths bounded; no OOB found.

CJsonRpcResponseRss::SendResponse (vtable slot +0x10): builds a response CTree (Centcom_RssLst_Get + opcode 0xdf), writes byteswapped int and the response string (length *(short*)(this+8)) via FUN_ram_b01648ca, then enqueues via the Rss list vtable+0x28. Note the copy length is this+8 low 16 bits, i.e. attacker-influenced response content; tree setter allocates, so bounded by tree semantics (inferred).

CJsonRpcResponseRss::SetDingId (vtable slot +0x18): parses attacker "ding_id" field to an int and stores it as a std::string at this+8. Called by JsonRpc_ParseAndDispatch before handler invocation. No memory-unsafe copy.

CJsonRpcResponseRss::BuildResponseJson (vtable slot +0x38): formats "{\"jsonrpc\":\"2.0\",\"id\":..., ...}" response with the stored ding_id/std::string. Uses fixed format strings; no attacker format string.

CCvSettings ACMD dispatcher. Opcode 0x10096 sets a boolean setting and propagates; 0x10097 updates an integer and propagates; 0x10020 writes indexed setting tuples (indices <0x13, 100..118, or 200..218); 0x10093 refreshes CV settings; 0x10001 subtype 6 copies pending 0x16C-byte settings into active once, propagates, and notifies another subsystem; 0x10099 copies pending settings into active if different; 0x10013 builds the event-notification list. Unknown commands return 0x0D.

CIpV4 ACMD dispatcher. Opcode 0x10001 forwards a subtype to the IPv4 state/query routine. Opcode 0x10009 subcommands: 0 static mode (virtual slot +0x68); 1 enable DHCP (+0x78); 2 renew (+0x88); 3 release (+0x90); 4 rebind (+0x98); 5 logs IPv4 address, mask, DNS and DHCP counters. Unknown subcommands/opcodes return 0x0D.

CNwAccessWifi ACMD dispatcher. Opcode 0x10007 subcommands: 0 mount, 1 dismount, 2 connect, 3 disconnect, 4 factory reset, 5 read/log MAC, 8 stop AP, 9 set profile, 10 get profile, 11 config placeholder, 12 invoke a vtable operation, 13 enumerate/log profiles, 14 invoke another vtable operation, 16 read/log current SSID+BSSID, 17 read/log profile SSID+BSSID, and 33 read/log Wi-Fi channel. Other selectors in the allowed range through 33 are no-op/default paths. Opcode 0x10001 includes status subtypes: 2 exposes RSSI/channel/MAC/integrity/beacon-loss/profile/activity fields; 5 resets counters for arg4==10; 6 calls two virtual status methods. Unsupported opcodes/subtypes generally return 0x0D.

CWdt ACMD opcode 0x1002C accepts selector 0..7. Selector 0 logs software callback threshold/free heap; 1 kicks watchdog; 2 enables; 3 disables; 4 reinitializes with the supplied reload value; 5 logs post-reinit reload; 6 runs the disable-software-kick path; 7 logs initialized/enabled/reload status. Unknown selectors return 0x0D. The operations are delegated through the watchdog object's virtual methods.
Named-property wrapper: split/validate namespace.key, clear output, decode with capacity truncated to 16 bits, map negative errors. Used by device-property lookup and Wi-Fi credential slot loader.
App OTP row read transaction: saves OTP CLK_CTRL, selects read clock mode 0x164, reads the row via otp_read_row_raw_app, reads/clears INT_STATUS, then restores the prior clock setting.

CSetupMethodWifi registered interface body (adjustor thunk b01b46ba subtracts 8 from this). It recognizes opcodes 0x1000B (selector 11 path) and 0x1004B (selectors 0/1); the latter branches into setup-state helpers and uses state stored in the object. Further semantic names for those helper paths are unresolved. Unknown commands/selectors fall through the handler's default result.

RX path: SFrame_Decrypt 0xc0c59b68 calls SFrame_ParseNalUnits with parse-flag param_6=0, so the Avc_ParseSps/Pps branch here is skipped for attacker/AEAD frames. Deep SPS/PPS/slice parse runs only on TX via SFrame_RewriteSpsH264/SFrame_InsertCodecConfigH264 (callers: SFrame_Encrypt 0xc0c59154).

SFrame_ParseNalUnitsH264: walks up to n_units descriptors. SPS(NAL 7) -> Avc_ParseSps into ctx+0x120 (stride 0x14, cap 6, count at ctx+0x198); PPS(NAL 8) -> Avc_ParsePps into ctx+0x19c (stride 0xc, cap 6, count at ctx+0x1e4). Existing entries matched by id and overwritten; otherwise count is only incremented while != 6 and slot = count-1, so indices stay 0..5. Copies exactly sizeof(AvcSps)/sizeof(AvcPps). AUDIT: NEGATIVE.

SFrame_ParseNalUnits: splits a media payload into AvcNalUnit descriptors. Mode selection: (ctx[0]-2)&0xfffffffd == 0 (ctx[0]==2 || ctx[0]==3) => length-prefixed (AVCC): iterates 4-byte big-endian lengths; descriptor = {offset=(int)(p+4)-(int)data, length=be32, type=0, flags=0}. Else Annex-B: scans for 00 00 01 / 00 00 00 01 start codes. Both branches: descriptor writes are gated by index < max_units; zero-length rejected; final index clamped to max_units. Then dispatches by ctx[0] to SFrame_ClassifyNalUnitsHevc (ctx[0]==3/4) or SFrame_ParseNalUnitsH264. REACHABILITY: network. Called via computed calls from 0c_networking at ram:c0c59270 / c0c5931a / c0c59c64. AUDIT: NEGATIVE (bounds above re-verified this pass).

SFrame_InsertCodecConfigH264: parses an AVCC config blob (param_8[0]==1, param_8[5]=numSPS, then 16-bit big-endian length+payload entries, then numPPS). Extracts last SPS and last PPS, bounds-checks total (sps_len+pps_len+8 + ctx_len <= dst_cap) before shift+memcpy. Clamps on overrun. AUDIT: no OOB write found; note puStack_58 is only used when high word of the saved length is nonzero, which requires a PPS entry to have been accepted.
SFrame_RewriteSpsH264: NAL type 7 -> Avc_ParseSps, then Avc_WriteSps into dst. All three memmove/extents are gated by (uVar2<=dst_cap) && (src_len - delta <= dst_cap - uVar2). AUDIT: NEGATIVE.
Varint decode with strict 32-bit overflow rejection (sign-extended high bytes must be 0xff/0x00; rejects >5 bytes). param_3 optional eof flag.

Raw read helper. If dest param2==0 and stream is a plain buffer (not callback), it drains in 0x10-byte chunks (discard). Otherwise requires bytes_left>=len else "end_of_stream"; calls stream->read_cb; on failure sets "io_error"; else bytes_left-=len.
Init pb_istream_t from a memory buffer: read_cb=plain-buffer reader (LAB_ram_b01b85b8), data=param2, bytes_left=param3, errmsg=0.
Skip unknown/ignored field by wire type: 0=varint (<=10B), 1=8B, 2=len-prefixed (Pb_Read len), 5=4B; other -> "invalid_wire_type".

Read length-prefixed submessage: varint32 len; memcpy substream=stream(0x20); require parent bytes_left>=len else "parent_stream_too_short"; substream.bytes_left=len; parent.bytes_left-=len. Bounds nested messages to the parent buffer.
Require substream fully consumed (bytes_left==0), then copy data pointer/errmsg back to parent stream.

Pb_DecodeField - protobuf field decoder. BOUNDS (proven): wire type 0 varint: value must fit the descriptor data_size (1/2/4/8) else "integer_too_large". wire type 6 bytes: u16 len read as varint32; requires len<0x10000 and len+2 <= field.data_size (else "bytes_overflow"); stores u16 len at dest, copies len bytes to dest+2. wire type 7 string: requires len+1 <= field.data_size (else "string_overflow"); copies len bytes and writes a NUL at dest+len. wire type 8 submessage: length from Pb_ReadFieldLength, which rejects len > remaining parent bytes ("parent_stream_too_short"); submessage fields are placed by their own fixed descriptor offsets. arrays: index bounded by descriptor count ("array_overflow"). => Every length the provisioning handlers later read from a bytes/string field is capped by the descriptor data_size. This is why Req0C creds(<=16)/secret(<=12) cannot overflow its 0x1e buffer.

Repeated-nested (modifier 0x30, kind 8) reset: prov_memset(dest=iter->dest, 0, desc->data_size) + Pb_ReleaseMessage when *ctrl != tag. For the provisioning union (ram:0xc0ca1478 -> member12 ram:0xc0ca0ef0 -> ram:0xc0ca0eb0) this zeroes dest..dest+0x20, which covers the handler's mis-offset secretLen/secret slots. This is what neutralizes the data_offset==0 overlap.

Message decode loop (stream, table, dest). Reads tags via Pb_ReadTag; Pb_FieldIterFind; for repeated nested (modifier 0x30, kind 8) performs reset prov_memset(dest,0,data_size)+Pb_ReleaseMessage when the ctrl tag word != tag, then writes tag. Unknown tags -> Pb_SkipField. Extension/unknown handler linked list + kind==9 catch-all. Enforces packed fixed-count (array_size) and required-field presence bitmap ("missing_required_field"). Feeds Pb_DecodeField.

DecodeSubmessagePtr: Pb_ReleaseMessage(table,dest) then Pb_DecodeMessage(stream,table,dest). Entry used by CDeviceProvision_DecodeMessage with table ram:0xc0ca0d48 and dest=CDeviceProvisionFlow+0x58 buffer.
App OTP clock control helper: saves CLK_CTRL and writes 0x164 for read mode, or 0 when disabling; caller restores the saved value after the read.
App OTP interrupt/status helper: returns INT_STATUS; when passed nonzero, clears the status register before returning.
App raw OTP row-window read: loads 32 bits from 0x90126000 + byte_offset and returns the value. The app wrapper supplies row_index * 4, matching the bootloader OTP data alias.

Avc_ParseSps: H.264 SPS parser. All bit reads go through the bounded BitReader; writes AvcSps (0x14 bytes) into out. Every parsed count that indexes a table (num_ref_frames_in_pic_order, etc.) is range-checked. Returns true(1) on failure, false(0) on success. AUDIT: NEGATIVE.
Avc_ParsePps: H.264 PPS parser; BitReader-bounded; writes AvcPps (0xc bytes). FMO (slice_group) rejected; id fields bounded. AUDIT: NEGATIVE.

Avc_ParseSliceHeader: parses slice header against caller-supplied SPS/PPS arrays (sps_count/pps_count). PPS lookup loops while index < pps_count; SPS lookup loops while index < sps_count; no unchecked index. ref_pic_list_modification / dec_ref_pic_marking loops are BitReader_InBounds-gated and reject counts > 0x1f/3. Returns consumed bit position or 0. AUDIT: NEGATIVE.

Init pb_field_iter_t: [0]=table,[1]=cursor,[0x10]=int index=0,[0x18]=base. If base!=0: dest=[0x20]=base+first.data_offset; ctrl=[0x28]=dest+first.size (size is signed, may be negative). Returns first.tag!=0.

Advance cursor by one 0x13-byte pb_field_t. If the next tag is 0, re-init and return 0. SPECIAL CASE: if current.type&0x30==0x30 AND next.type&0x30==0x30 AND next.data_offset==0xffff (union/oneof alias, e.g. ram:0xc0ca1478 members f2..f14), dest/ctrl are left UNCHANGED. Otherwise dest = prev_dest + cur.data_size*(cur.array_size if packed) + next.data_offset; ctrl = dest + next.size. Reads next.data_offset at byte 0x16 and next.size at 0x18 (= next+3 / next+5).

Find field with tag==param_2 by walking the table; skips entries with (type&0xf)==9 (callback/catch-all marker). Wraps to start and returns 0 if absent. On success iter->dest corresponds to the matched field.

BitReader_ReadBits: reads up to 32 bits MSB-first from br->buffer, with optional H.264 emulation-prevention (0x000003) removal. Bounds: if length*8 < cur_byte*8+bit_offset+nbits it only advances bit_offset (marks out-of-bounds, returns 0). The per-byte loop advances cur_byte only while cur_byte+1 < length. The initial partial-byte read is reached only when length*8 >= cur_byte*8+bit_offset+nbits, so cur_byte < length. AUDITED (this pass): no OOB byte read found. NOTE: length<<3 is 32-bit; safe for the sub-2^29 media-frame lengths used here.

BitReader_InBounds: (cur_byte*8 + bit_offset) <= length*8. ReadBits/TellValid use this to decide success. Returned bit position is used by Avc_Parse* to set the "valid bits" / consumed length fields in the output structs.

vtable of class CPfmHdkMarsRed (derives from CPlatform, base vtable at ram_b01c9488). 32 slots, each a __thiscall member with `this` = CPfmHdkMarsRed*. 00 Shutdown 01 ProcessCommand 02 Destructor 03 DeletingDestructor 04 InitStage1 05 InitStage2 06 ConsoleInit 07 InitStorage 08 InitLocalSetupNetwork 09 Start 10 ThunkStart 11 ProcessDeviceLock 12 EventFilter 13 EventFilter2 14 HandleEvent 15 DefaultVfunc15 16 DefaultVfunc16 17 GetBootMode 18 GetDeviceLockType 19 EraseIfUnlocked 20 GetField_0xd0 21 DefaultVfunc21 22 DefaultVfunc22 23 ForwardToOtaClient 24 DefaultVfunc24 25 DefaultVfunc25 26 DefaultVfunc26 27 SetShipMode 28 IsShipModeEnabled 29 Reset 30 DefaultVfunc30 31 DefaultVfunc31

Five-entry RingUart peripheral base table indexed by port: UART0 0x20028000, UART1 0x20029000, UART2 0x2002A000, UART3 0x2002B000, and UART4 0x90125000. RingUart_AdoptIfMuxed and RingUart_ConfigureHardware use this table.
CMars_CoPro registered interface vtable at outer-object offset +0xC8. Slot +8 is the adjustor thunk b0103436, which subtracts 0xC8 then dispatches at b010329a.

COtp_Mars constructor installs this table as its object vptr. Slot +0 points to COtp_Mars_ReadBits; slot +8 is null. This is not evidence of a RuntimeObject shell message-handler vtable or numeric ACMD opcode.

CRingNM primary vtable address point: 39 function-pointer slots (0x138 bytes). The preceding RTTI/offset-to-top metadata is outside this structure; offset-to-top is -0x50 and the secondary address point begins at ram:b01d3f08.

CRingNM secondary Centcom sink vtable address point: five adjusting slots for destructor, deleting destructor, profile event, SetNetworkConfig, and network-status handling. Each thunk adjusts this by -0x50 before forwarding to the CRingNM implementation.
CDingerGT registered interface vtable at outer-object offset +8. Slot +8 is adjustor thunk b0119750, which subtracts 8 then dispatches at b01193a0.

CCentcom_Rdk primary vtable: 24 pointer-sized slots (0xC0 bytes). Constructor evidence shows this table installed at object offset 0. Null slots are reserved/unused; slot names reflect observed behavior where confirmed, otherwise they remain adapter/unresolved labels.
CRiidManager registered interface vtable at outer-object offset +8. Slot +8 is adjustor thunk c0c35012 (subtracts 8 then dispatches to c0c34fb6).

CEventitoChannelRss registered interface vtable: first slot is generic unsupported handler, second slot is b00df5fe (returns 0x0D). This registered interface therefore rejects ACMD opcodes in the analyzed build; this does not imply the class has no other event callbacks.

CHttpClient registered ACMD interface vtable. Its slot +8 is b00df5fe, the generic unsupported-command method that returns 0x0D. This is the nested interface at outer-object offset +8, not the enclosing CHttpClient vtable.

Vtable-like dispatch table for the object constructed at ram:b015a982/ram:b015a9b4. Slot +8 is ram:b015a950, whose only accepted opcode is 0x10049 (with arg0 == 1); handler writes two 16-bit values to ram:b01fa3a0. Constructor references the name string CCheckpoint, but target-ID binding should be verified via runtime object info.

CFile_KVS_ACS vtable (17 slots), applied as CFile_KVS_ACS_vtable. Slots 0-12 mirror CFileDesc/CFile (CFileDesc vtable ram:0xc0cb50c8, CFile vtable ram:0xc0cb4fd0); slots 13-15 are the CFile virtuals Stat/Delete/CheckExists, slot 16 is a base default (returns 0xf).
CProcess registered target vtable. Slot +8 is b00df5fe, the shared unsupported-command method that returns 0x0D.
CSetupMethodWifi registered interface vtable at outer-object offset +8. Slot +8 points to adjustor thunk b01b46ba (subtracts 8 then dispatches to b01b35ac).
PEM marker state-transition table indexed by the state byte in CUpdate_PemMarkerStateMachine (matches expected marker bytes).

FlashPartition table (20 entries, stride 0x1c) passed to fm_multi_flash_init via `gp-0x548` (gp=0xb01f5f00) at ram:0xb00d3b02.
