Layout: name[16] @+0x00, size u32 @+0x10, base/flash offset u32 @+0x14, field_18 u8 @+0x18, instance_index u8 @+0x19.
# name size offset f18 0 dhav2 0x1000 0x1ffe000 06 1 bootCtl 0x1000 0x40000 06 2 otaA 0x900000 0x50000 06 3 otaB 0x900000 0x950000 06 4 fwblA 0x20000 0x0 06 5 fwblB 0x20000 0x20000 06 6 fota 0x40000 0x16fd000 06 7 ftmp 0x400000 0x16fd000 06 8 log_main 0 0x1cfd000 07 9 fqc_main 0x1000 0x1dfd000 06 10 log_backup 0 0x1cfd000 06 11 kvsShared 0x40000 0x1e3e000 06 12 kvsBackup 0x40000 0x1dfe000 06 13 kvsData 0x40000 0x1e7e000 06 14 kvsSettings 0x2000 0x1ebe000 06 15 config_backup 0x1000 0x16fc000 06 16 log_crash 0 0x1cfd000 06 17 kvsHW 0x40000 0x1efe000 06 18 log 0x1000 0x1cfd000 06 19 log_meta 0 0x1cfd000 06
field_18 is the region-type field read by check_flash_area_writeable as `(*(u32*)(p+0x18) >> 1) & 3`. ALL entries are 0x06/0x07 -> type 3 (writable), so that guard is a no-op. The OTA bundle (BUND header at flash 0x50200, app element offset 0x1ba240) lives inside otaA/otaB.

fqc_main FlashPartition descriptor: size 0x1000, flash offset 0x01dfd000, flags 6. Separate from otaA [0x50000,0x950000) and otaB [0x950000,0x1250000). Byte 0 is read directly as application FQC enable flag. SetFqcFlagFromResetMode writes 0 or 1 through WriteRaw without signing data.

Main application stack-protector guard. Initialized image bytes at this address are 0x00000000A1BEEF1A. Enumerated code xrefs are loads/checks only; no runtime store/entropy reseed to this application guard was found. Distinct from FWBL ram::stack_canary_init_trng, which obtains 8 bytes from trng_fill and stores its own guard at ram:b0297260. Verify startup data-copy semantics if assessing execution-time value.
NO BLOCK

SFrame inbound staging buffer (0x141 bytes). CSframeE2ee_Decrypt copies the frame here, then SFrame_Decrypt parses/decrypts from it in place. SFrame_ReadHeaderFields can over-read up to +0x18 past this buffer when the attacker sets footer_size as low as 6 (header is expected to be 0x1b). The over-read bytes only feed bounded header fields / key-id lookup, never a write length. Sole xrefs: CSframeE2ee_Decrypt b01439d0/b01439e8.
NO BLOCK

Fixed 0x2b2-byte BSS staging buffer shared by CMediaStreamAudio_EncryptFrame and CMediaStreamAudio_HandleFrame. TX path bounds len<=0x2b2 (abort otherwise). RX path copies here unbounded BEFORE CSframeE2ee_Decrypt rejects len>0x140, so len in (0x140,0x4f0] overflows into adjacent BSS then the process halts. Next named global is at +0x2b8 (a static map ctor at b00bbbc0).

CMediaStreamAudio RX/TX frame scratch buffer, 0x2b2 bytes (encrypt path enforces len<=0x2b2 via noreturn abort at b018dd4x). DECRYPT path CMediaStreamAudio_HandleFrame @ b018e13e does prov_memcpy(this, frame, len) BEFORE CSframeE2ee_Decrypt's len<0x141 check -> if an SRTP/peer frame has len in (0x2b2, upstream max ~0x4f0] this overflows into adjacent BSS (HashMap object at b021b738) and is immediately followed by the noreturn abort in CSframeE2ee_Decrypt (len>0x140). No function pointers in the window -> DoS, not RCE.

Global sink pointer assigned in CPfmHdkMarsRed::InitLocalSetupNetwork to the CRingNM secondary Centcom interface subobject at object_base + 0x50. The backing CRingNM allocation is 0x7d8 bytes; its secondary vptr points at ram:b01d3f08. g_CentcomNetworkConfigSink is used by CCentcom_PushNetworkConfigToRnm, which dispatches its SetNetworkConfig method via secondary vtable slot +0x18.

uart_settings_load reads the persisted UART settings at flash offset 0x43000. If validation fails, it sets the baud field to 0xe1000 (921600) and marks settings initialized; this is the firmware default console baud.
boot_retry_fallback_check: OtpContents.BOOT_ATTEMPT (reg 6) nibble [7:4] vs system-controller boot count (@0x90000091); switch boot slot + reboot if otp+1 < sysc.
reads OtpContents.BOOT_ATTEMPT (reg 6); nibble [7:4]

First-stage secure-boot flow confirmed from disassembly/decompilation: actually_boot_the_device reads SBIH header from active OTA slot, calls sbih_auth_and_decrypt_G(header,0xf20), and compares the result against BL_OK 0xc0ab6. A failure logs secure-boot authentication failed and reboots/marks the slot unsuccessful; bundle_hdr_init_G and second-stage loading occur only after success.

stack_canary_init_trng: one-shot boot init of the global stack canary. Calls trng_fill(&buf,8,0); if it fails -> reboot_device_G(0). Stores the 8 TRNG bytes to g_stack_canary @ ram:0xb0297260 (disasm ram:b0280a42-b0280a4a: c.ldsp a5,0x8(sp); sd a5,-0x7e6(a4) with a4=b0297a46). Canonical caller: ram:b0280a64 (boot init), UNCONDITIONAL_CALL. NOTE: g_stack_canary is a single process-wide global, NOT per-task and not copied into the TCB; every function reloads it in its prologue and compares on return. So one 8-byte disclosure defeats the canary for every task/frame.

FWBL main boot: init uart/flash/OTP, regenerate unique number, security thermometer check, rotatable key provisioning, SBIH verify, unlock state eval (reboots-left lockout), then cli_boot_entry_gate (50ms '=' window) before booting image.
keyslot_blank_check(slot): all 16 regs of OtpContents.AES_KEY_SLOTn must read 0 (base from otp_partition_key_base_table @0xB0292DD0).
OtpContents.AES_KEY_SLOTn[i] blank check (base tbl 0xB0292DD0)
OtpContents.CNT5_ROTATABLE_KEY_IDX / CNT6_STATIC_KEY_IDX (counter 5/6)
burn OtpContents.CNT6_STATIC_KEY_IDX (counter 6)
keyslot_read_key: reads 16 regs of OtpContents.AES_KEY_SLOTn (raw AES-256 key material) into buffer; slot from OtpContents key-index counters; zeroize+panic on ECC error.
OtpContents.AES_KEY_SLOTn[i] -> 32-byte raw AES key (base tbl 0xB0292DD0)
keyslot_provision_new_key: TRNG 32 bytes -> OtpContents.AES_KEY_SLOTn regs (otpw path), then bumps OtpContents.CNT5_ROTATABLE_KEY_IDX via otp_counter_burn(5).
burn OtpContents.CNT5_ROTATABLE_KEY_IDX (counter 5) = new slot

FWBL anti-rollback startup check: target level is hdr_get_fwbl_ar_level() == 5; reads OTP counter 1, and when current < 5 < max, sets SYSCTL.boot_ctr_greater_than_10 bits via sysc_burn_counter_fwbl, clears boot-attempt count, and reboots to advance the thermometer counter. This routine alone does not reject when the OTP counter is already above this image's target level; do not interpret it as proof that an older FWBL is rejected. External ROM behavior is outside this loaded binary.
OtpContents.CNT1_FWBL_ANTIROLLBACK
OtpContents.CNT0_IMG_PUBKEY_SLOT
OtpContents.CNT2_DEBUG_PUBKEY_SLOT

FreeRTOS+CLI prvProcessCommand: walks registered command list (head at gp-0x7f0), matches name (case-insensitive), checks cExpectedNumberOfParameters @+0x18 (-1 = any), calls handler @+0x10 with (writeBuf, writeBufLen, params).

FreeRTOS+CLI console main loop. Reads chars via function ptrs set up by serial_console_enter (a0=cmd buffer ctx, a1=console out fn, a2/a3=uart in/out bufs). Echoes/backspaces, on ENTER calls cli_process_input_chars -> cli_process_command.

Serial-console input helper: calls uart_readc() for UART0, stores one received byte at the supplied buffer and returns 1; when no byte is available, kicks the watchdog and returns -1. Used by the stage3_memconsole payload for line input.

Anti-tamper gate: checks unlock_get_last_status()==0x95432 and stack cookie; if OK -> cli_register_standard_commands (b0282d0c) and return; else loops calling cli_register_debug_commands + error print forever (bricked state).
Enters the serial console: loads uart in/out fn ptrs + prompts ("\r\n[Input a command and press ENTER]\r\n>") and tail-calls cli_console_main_loop.

FWBL CLI command handler, not an ACMD target. Parses a flash start offset and maximum transfer size, then calls xmodem_write_flash. The command itself has no partition/writeable-area whitelist check; xmodem_write_flash erases the sector-rounded range and receives/programs up to the supplied size. Lower-level spi_flash_erase enforces sector alignment and checks range against flash_end.
OtpContents.CNT3_VENDOR_REBOOTS (status print)

Restricted FWBL command setup: resets command list; registers status, getunlock, unlock; publishes unlock mode 4 in validated RAM handoff. Application maps mode 4 to boot_mode=1, suppressing application serial shell unless FQC flag is set.

Registers 12 standard commands from CliCommand table at b0293c58 using index table b0293c48 (order: genpekey,fwxmod,frxmod,poa,pob,aerasebcb,get,l,otpr,otpw,chbr). Only reached when cli_setup_gate_check passes (magic 0x95432).
Console command handler for `otpr <addr>`: decimal row index 0..0x3FF, reads a 16-bit OTP row through otp_read_register, reports ECC/status, and prints the value.
user-indexed OtpContents read (cmd_otpr <idx>)

FWBL CLI OTP write command, separate from ACMD. Restricts row index to 0..0x3ff and, for nonblank rows, only permits valid non-decreasing thermometer updates; this is not an arbitrary RAM/flash write.
user-indexed OtpContents read (cmd_otpw verify)

Console OTP write path: cmd_otpw checks row < 0x400, reads the current value, permits a blank row or a valid non-decreasing thermometer update, then invokes otp_write_register and verifies by rereading. The underlying low-level writer itself is not limited to thermometer semantics.
user-indexed OtpContents read (cmd_otpw monotonicity check)

getunlock [load|store]: generates/loads/stores 256-byte vendor unlock challenge. Challenge contains unique-number hash(0x14)@+0x08, reboot counter@+0x1c, 0x10 random bytes; exported from unlock partition record at 0xb02b10e0. Prints hex for signing.
Boot-time CLI entry gate. If setup OK: 50ms window polling UART for '=' (0x3d) to enter CLI; else prints "Setup is not correct, entering CLI." and enters CLI unconditionally.

Bootloader CLI XMODEM flash writer used by cmd_fwxmod and OTA slot programming. Erases the sector-rounded [start, start+size) range, then receives data and writes at start+offset. This is an SPI flash write primitive, not a general RAM/MMIO write.
Boot-time OTP verification setup: enqueues the three ranges in verified_data and starts the controller's queued verification operation.
OtpContents.CNT1_FWBL_ANTIROLLBACK -> config 'fwbl_antirollback'

Early hardware initialization processes the app anti-rollback bump request staged in SYSCTL/BL-PUBLIC config: clears the trigger, reads OTP CNT4_BUNDLE_ANTIROLLBACK, compares it with staged bundle_ar, and calls otp_counter_burn(4) when OTP is lower. This is the irreversible commit path for a newer signed app version; the config shadow is a staging/control record, not the OTP fuse itself.
OtpContents.CNT4_BUNDLE_ANTIROLLBACK -> config 'bundle_ar'
OtpContents.CNT4_BUNDLE_ANTIROLLBACK vs expected (AR bump path)
burn OtpContents.CNT4_BUNDLE_ANTIROLLBACK (app AR bump)

FWBL bounds-checked flash read: requires len!=0, read_to!=0, param_1 <= flash_end and param_1+len <= flash_end. NOTE: `len + param_1` is a 64-bit add, so a very large caller-supplied len can wrap the sum and bypass the end check (callers today pass small lengths, e.g. 0xF20).

Polled UART transmitter: uart_write_byte_polled(port, byte, retries). Checks periph_is_initialized(), polls uart_tx_idle_any(port), then writes the byte with periph_reg_write(port, 0, byte); returns 0 if unavailable or the retry limit expires. Candidate for a one-byte observable ROP marker, provided the chosen UART port is initialized and configured to the host baud.

FWBL's per-hart serial-console byte writer. It selects g_uart_port_by_hart[mhartid] and calls the bounded polling UART transmit path. In this image, the hart-0 mapping is port 0. Stage3 can use this initialized console route directly without reconfiguring the app RingUart driver or depending on interrupts.

Raw OTP word-window read: reads a 32-bit value from 0x90126000 + byte_offset. otp_read_register passes row_index*4 as the offset; the indexed counters use rows listed in g_otp_counter_ranges. This is a platform-specific MMIO/OTP alias, not a RISC-V architectural address.
Peripherals::OTP.CONTENTS.<field> - indexed fuse regfile read (reg = byte_offset>>2; content map in OtpContents)
Fatal halt "loop": stops/re-inits timer then spins forever. Reached from FUN_ram_b02802a6 on unrecoverable init failure.

Reads a fixed 0xF20-byte SBIH header from flash at `read_from` into `read_to`. Caller MUST provide a >= 0xF20-byte buffer (actually_boot_the_device passes the 0xF20 global header_data at 0xB02AF010); there is no length parameter. Returns BL_OK 0xC0AB6 on success, 0x8EC4B on bad args / read error.
transition to secure monitor

Bundle anti-rollback update. Reads OTP counter 4 (CNT4_BUNDLE_ANTIROLLBACK) and its maximum. Equal version stages the same level and succeeds; lower version returns the initialized error status; higher version stages the new level plus feature flag 1 and reboots so the OTP counter can be advanced. sbih_auth_and_decrypt_G rejects this error result on locked devices.
OtpContents.CNT4_BUNDLE_ANTIROLLBACK vs new bundle version

SBIH authorization path: parses the 0x200-byte catalog in the supplied sbih_header, finds `Image.sig` and `Image`, and takes the candidate application version from the `Image` record header's `version_num` byte (first_0x50_sbih_header_bytes +0x39). It checks the signature and invokes bundle_ar_counter_update(version_num); that function compares against OTP counter index 4 (CNT4_BUNDLE_ANTIROLLBACK).
Callsite passes the `Image` record header's version_num byte, parsed from the signed SBIH catalog, into bundle_ar_counter_update for comparison with OTP CNT4_BUNDLE_ANTIROLLBACK.

Thin wrapper: RSA-PSS-SHA256 verify of the Image element (x509_verify_rsassa_pss_sha256_G) with siglen=0x50, sig=param_3, len=param_4, pubkey=param_5, key_len=0x100, blob=param_7, blob_len=param_8). Returns bool.

ram::get_bund_element_load_addr_size: returns BUND_HDR_ELEMENT0_LOAD_ADDR[index] and SIZE[index] for the element type. Note the header already carries both a load address and a size, yet callers like bundle_load_element_to_addr ignore the load address and use a caller-supplied dst -- so the header size is not cross-checked against the intended destination at all.

ram::validated_load_bund_element_at_address(type, where): same as FUN_ram_b016820c but "validated" refers only to the post-copy SHA-256/digest check, NOT the size. The element size (BUND_HDR_ELEMENT0_SIZE[index]) is passed verbatim to flash_read_to_ram_G into caller-supplied `where` with no bound. On hash mismatch a memset(where,0,size) also writes `size` bytes. Digest table at 0x9000022c (persist_data) is zero in the image -> populated at boot.

Writes fields in the SYSCTL/BL-PUBLIC shadow at 0x90000f24 through bitfield_write. This is mutable staging state with CRC commit; it is distinct from OTP counters, which otp_read_counter reads from OTP registers.
otp_pubkey_hash_verify: reads OtpContents.IMG_PUBKEY_SHA256[slot][0..15] (regs (slot+0x14)*0x10 + i, slot from signed header), consttime-compares the 32-byte SHA-256 against the bundle pubkey hash.
reads OtpContents.IMG_PUBKEY_SHA256[slot][i], reg (slot+0x14)*0x10+i

SBIH constant gate: compares the u32 at g_sbih_constant (0xB02CB8C0) against 0xA7E5C369. Returns BL_OK 0xC0AB6 when equal, BL_ERR 0x8EC4B otherwise. The decompiler's `_a3a_aec_pipeline_run` alias was a bogus auto-name; renamed g_sbih_constant.
OTP hardware verify queue entry: accepts start/end page values below 0x400, fills one of eight VERIFY_JOB slots with range and mode flags, and returns the slot index.
Starts the OTP controller's queued verification jobs by setting VERIFY_START bits 0x14.

Reads a thermometer-encoded OTP counter using otp_counter_table: each table entry gives a starting OTP word offset and a count of words; each word must decode to a valid monotonic thermometer value. Returns the sum, rejecting invalid/non-monotonic contents.
OtpContents counter regs: base+count from otp_counter_table 0xB02944F0
otp_counter_reg_step_burn: burns next thermometer step into counter reg (OtpContents counter fields; base/count from otp_counter_table @0xB02944F0).

One-way OTP counter burn routine. Reads the current thermometer counter, rejects targets below current or above count*5, encodes the requested level into OTP words, and programs the corresponding OTP registers. App anti-rollback uses index 4 / CNT4_BUNDLE_ANTIROLLBACK.
otp_counter_max_get: computes max = count*5 from otp_counter_table (does NOT write).
otp_read_unique_number: reads OtpContents.UNIQUE_NUMBER (regs 0x2E1..0x2E4). QUIRK: loop index (i&3)+0x2E1 for i=0..9 -> the 8 real bytes are repeated to fill 20.
OtpContents.UNIQUE_NUMBER (0x2E1..0x2E4) - (i&3) repetition quirk
otp_unique_number_provision: burns 4 TRNG bytes into blank OtpContents.UNIQUE_NUMBER regs.
OtpContents.UNIQUE_NUMBER blank check (0x2E1..0x2E4)
OtpContents.CNT3_VENDOR_REBOOTS -> unlock challenge

Unlock record auth state machine. UState@+0x60: 0xff=blank, 0xff0=one-time, 0xf00f/0xff00=vendor. Verifies .unlock magics @+0/+0x166, device unique-number match, RSA-signed blob vs embedded pubkey (PEM @b0295278). If vendor-unlocked reboots exceed 30 (OTP counter idx 3), downgrades UState to 0xf00f (one-time).
OtpContents.CNT3_VENDOR_REBOOTS (>30 => vendor unlock downgrade)
settings_read_var: gates on OtpContents.KEYPROV_STATUS (reg 8) bit 11, then thermometer-reads/burns the caller's counter regs (security thermometer update).
reads OtpContents.KEYPROV_STATUS (reg 8); bit 11 = provision gate
thermometer read/burn of arg counter regs (KEYPROV gate passed)

Pre-authentication SBIH record parser note: catalog_record_next processes attacker-controlled header bytes before signature validation. It bounds record-header assembly to 0x50 bytes, validates record magic and CRC, and limits parsing to the 0x200-byte catalog. Its returned Image record length is checked by sbih_auth_and_decrypt_G before signature verification. The remaining extent concern is Image length <= 0xf20 despite the +0x200 pointer offset into an input buffer filled with 0xf20 bytes.
otp_partition_key_base_table: slot 0 is invalid/sentinel; slot 1 starts at OTP row 0x2F9, then slots 2..4 start at 0x309, 0x319, 0x329. Each AES-256 slot occupies 16 rows (32 bytes).

Eight-byte entries indexed by otp_read_counter: {first OTP word offset, number of OTP words}. Includes image-key slot, FWBL anti-rollback, debug-key slot, vendor reboot, bundle anti-rollback, and key-index counters. Values are offsets in the OTP register space, not offsets in the external flash image.

g_stack_canary: 8-byte global stack cookie, live in the RX "ram" segment (ram:0xb0280000-0xb029750f). Static image value is 0x1; overwritten once at boot by stack_canary_init_trng @ ram:0xb0280a2a with 8 bytes from the TRNG. Shared by all tasks (100+ read xrefs are per-function prologue loads, e.g. ram:b0280586, each compared at epilogue; mismatch -> ram::stack_chk_fail @ ram:b028137c / main_app::prov_stack_chk_fail @ ram:b00c4fc6). Leaking these 8 bytes (any read primitive) fully defeats the canary.
UART port index selected by uart_console_putc_hart using mhartid. The observed first entries are [0, 0, 3, 3, 3, 3, 4, 4], so the app's hart 1 selects port 0.
block=video_parser start=ram:b02b7440 end=ram:b02cfb7f size=18740 init=true r=true w=true

Core3_TrapEntry: machine-mode trap vector target / core3 boot stub. Sets mtvec=ram:b02c84e8 then calls FUN_ram_b02b750e(mhartid,0,0). Reached from sec_mon::core_boot_core3_start (ram:b00009a6) and sec_mon::boot_fwbl_register_type1 (ram:b00052f4). This proves the whole ram:b02b7xxx-b02bdxxx section is the camera/ISP core3 firmware image, not a main-core network parser.

Video_Init: core3 ISP pipeline bring-up (video.c). Allocates SRAM/PSRAM frame buffers, programs VPE1/VPE2 ring buffers via CircBuf_Program, computes buffer counts from sensor dimensions, starts the H.264 encoder via H264_StartEncoder. Inputs are sensor/ISP configuration and hardware state; no network/media parsing. Inferred name.

H264_StartEncoder: h264.c - reads a config struct (param_1[0..0xe]), writes hardware globals b02d1040/b02d1048/b02d1050/b02d1068..b02d1090, programs H.264 FIFO/registers and starts the hardware encoder (dependency of Video_Init). Inferred name; config comes from the ISP pipeline, not from inbound NAL data.

CircBuf_Program (circbuf.c): for buffer index param_1<6, computes a hardware address from ISP registers (700c0028/700c006c region), writes pointer table b02cc990[idx] register fields and the per-index descriptor at b02d2900+idx*0x20 (ptr/current/length/total). Index asserted <6. Data are hardware/DMA addresses, not attacker input. Inferred name.

CbtBuf_Read (cbtbuf.c): drains up to param_3 bytes from circular buffer param_1 (<0x19) into param_2, using FUN_ram_b02bc750 to get a contiguous chunk and FUN_ram_b02bbfa6 to translate it. Advances and wraps the buffer pointer. Lengths come from the buffer's internal state. Inferred name.

A3A AE state init. Creates the pipeline (a3a_aec_pipeline_create) and the weight grid at param_1+0x6b0 with descriptor {storage=param_1+0x700, capacity=0x100}. Fixes the weight-grid storage as a 0x100-byte buffer, which is why all generate_grid writes are capacity-checked.
A3AWeightGrid_ctor. param_1 = weight_grid; a1 = {storage,capacity} descriptor. Embedded A3ABaseWeightCalc at +8 via A3ABaseWeightCalc_ctor. Storage=grid+0x700, capacity=0x100.
Validate a type-3 grid-config blob: requires payload[0]==3 and u32 payload size > 0x3f (>=0x40). Returns the payload pointer (a1) unchanged when valid, else 0. Side-effect-free - no writes.

video_parser::a3a_weight_grid_config - consumes type-3 (grid config) and type-1 (weight-calc) blobs from the TuningGRID bundle (namespace 2, version 3). Storage is the fixed 0x100-byte buffer param_1+0x700, so all grid writes are capacity-checked. Delegates remaining blobs to a3a_base_weightcalc_import_tuning / a3a_weight_grid_parse_fail.

INFOLEAK ASSESSMENT (a3a_base_weightcalc_generate_grid OOB read): BUG PROVEN: entry_count = u32@payload+0x43 is gated only by blob size > 0x4a; the entry loop then reads ~10 bytes * entry_count from payload+4, over-reading the tuning blob. Values feed only the weight-grid math (stores bounded to the 0x100 grid). No write primitive, no egress to attacker. CANARY: unreachable — read bytes are transformed into weight values, never returned, and the target is the tuning blob (heap/flash), not g_stack_canary.

OOB READ: entry_count = *(uint*)(payload+0x43) is validated only by "blob size > 0x4a"; it is never checked against payload_length. The following loop walks entry_count entries of 9 bytes starting at payload+4, reading ~10 bytes each, so a crafted entry_count over-reads far past the tuning blob (heap/flash). No write primitive here; reads feed weight values only.

A3ABaseWeightCalc_ctor: vtable b02cdea0; stores {storage,capacity} from descriptor into +8/+0x10 and zeroes the storage buffer. Called with storage=weight_grid+0x700, capacity=0x100 by a3a_ae_state_init.

Import a type-1 (weight-calc) tuning blob into the base weight-calc object. Reads u16 width@payload[0], u16 height@payload[2]; computes count = (int)(width*height) via mulw and requires storage_capacity >= count before calling a3a_base_weightcalc_generate_grid. The blob's declared size at header+4 must be >0x4a only. Writes in generate_grid are bounded by the capacity check; the OOB is the entry-table over-read there.
A3AAecCameraStage ctor: sets vtable b02ce498 and zeroes +0x18/+0x20/+0x28/+0x30 (gain tables). The type-10 config later fills payload@+8, payload+0xc0@+0x10 and the gain table ptr/count pairs.

A3AAecGridStage ctor (stage #2 at pipeline+0xf8, pipeline+0x70 pointer). Sets vtable b02ce110, +0x20/+0x24/+0x28=0xff, default accessor fn a3a_aec_grid_accessor_direct @+0x458. Type-2 config fills dims/strides/buffer later.

A3AAecPipeline_ctor. Base ctor sets vtable b02ce768 then this sets vtable b02cded0 (A3AAecCamera/Pipeline). Embedded stages: +0x68->+0xc0 (camera, b02ce498), +0x70->+0xf8 (grid, b02ce110), +0x78->+0x590, +0x80->+0x5d8, +0x88->+0x610 (dist, b02ce350). No tuning data involved.
A3AAecGridStage vfunc +0x20: stores *param_2 into +0x470 (input grid buffer pointer). The buffer is caller-owned; +0x470 is only ever READ by a3a_aec_grid_accumulate. No write sink.

A3AAecGridStage::config (type-2 blob, size >0x13). Reads width=byte@payload+0xe, height=byte@payload+0xf (rejects 0 and width*height>0x4000); row_stride=byte@payload+0x12+1; col_stride=row_stride*width+byte@payload+0x13. Clears +0x470 (buffer installed separately). All values byte-derived and area-capped, so the stored dims/strides are themselves bounded; they are only used for READS of +0x470.

A3A_AEC_GRID accumulate. PROVEN: writes only to obj+0x2c histogram (0x400, indexed by min(weight,obj+0x20)<=0x3fc, bounded) and to the 16-byte output struct param_3. The obj+0x470 buffer (set by a3a_aec_grid_set_input_buffer from a caller-owned buffer) and the accessor struct at obj+0x438 are READ only. Loop bounds obj+0x440/0x444 vs dims obj+0x478/0x47c mismatch can cause an OOB READ of obj+0x470, not a write. NO OOB WRITE.
A3AAecGridStage vfunc +0x18: iterates input stat sets (param_2[1]) and calls a3a_aec_grid_accumulate per set. Writes are bounded inside the callee.

A3A_AEC_DIST stage, vtable b02ce350 slot +0x10. Consumes type-6 blob (declared size >99). Stores payload@+0x58, dist_ptr=payload+0x10@+0x60, dist_count=u32@payload+0x60@+0x68, hdr_ptr=payload+4@+0x70, hdr_count=u32@payload+8@+0x78 (must be <=1). Then calls (*(*(this+0x50)+0x20))(obj50,-1,0x400,hdr_count,payload). PROVEN: this+0x50 = pipeline+0xc0 (A3AAecCameraStage, vtable b02ce498); slot +0x20 = a3a_aec_camera_lookup_gain_index (0xb02cb020). That callee ignores a3/a4 (the raw payload) and only indexes the camera stage's own gain tables. No write from the type-6 payload. Consumers of +0x60/+0x68 (a3a_aec_dist_table_interp) are read-only. NO OOB WRITE.

A3AAecDistStage ctor (param_1 = pipeline+0x610). Sets vtable b02ce350; +0x8/+0x20/+0x38 point at the embedded sub-vtable descriptors (b02ce3a0/b02ce3b8/b02ce3d0). Sets +0x50 = pipeline->vfunc_0x10() = A3AAecPipeline_get_camera_stage = pipeline+0xc0. +0x8c=0 (bounded scratch count).

A3AAecDistStage reference-table interpolation. param_2={ptr,count}; count comes from the type-6 payload (dist_count @+0x68). Indexes piVar4[i*2] up to count with no upper bound vs the real array -> OOB READ only. No store.

A3AAecCameraStage::config (type-10 blob, declared size >199). Stores payload@+8, payload+0xc0@+0x10; if payload+0xc selector==1 uses analog table else digital, storing ptr=payload+0x10 and count=u32@payload+0xa0 (only checked !=0, so a huge count is accepted) at +0x18/+0x20 or +0x28/+0x30. Those counts feed A3AAecCameraStage::lookup_gain which only READS -> OOB read, no write.

A3AAecCameraStage vfunc +0x20 (vtable b02ce498). Signature (this, uint value, uint cap). PROVEN from disasm: args a3/a4/a5 are dead; the routine reads this->payload@+8 (u32 selector @payload+0xc), then does a lookup / interpolation over the camera stage's own gain tables (+0x18/+0x20 digital, +0x28/+0x30 analog). No store anywhere; returns a gain index. Called by a3a_aec_ref_distribution_config with the whole type-6 payload in a4, which is IGNORED. Read-only.

video_parser::a3a_aec_pipeline_config. Drives 5 virtual blob parsers (dst objects at this+0x68..+0x88). The grow/shrink loops for the per-channel array at this+0xa4 are bounded because input/output channel sizes are restricted to {1,2} (uVar6 = size-1 < 2). No overflow here; the underlying parsers are the risk surface.

A3AAecPipeline_base_ctor: sets vtable b02ce768, stores the 5 stage pointers at +0x68..+0x88, zeroes +0xa0/+0xac/+0xb8, +0xb0=0xffff00000000. +0xb0 is the output-channel size (<=2) used to bound the +0xa4 loop in a3a_aec_pipeline_run.

A3AAecPipeline run. PROVEN bounded: the +0xa4 u32 copy loop bound is param_3[1], which is pipeline+0xb0 (output channel size, restricted to {1,2} by a3a_aec_pipeline_config), so the 2-int array at +0xa4 is not overflowed. Stage vfuncs +0x18 are invoked for stages +0x70/+0x78/+0x80/+0x88.

Parse 12-byte tuning bundle header {u16 namespace_id@0, u16 version@2, u32 bundle_length@4}. Checks remaining>=0xc and bundle_length<=remaining, then returns a descriptor advanced by 0xc (remaining reduced). NOTE: bundle_length is validated but NOT enforced as the traversal bound for later blobs - only the raw remaining length is. Blobs are still bounded by actual bytes via a3a_tuning_get_blob, so this is leniency, not memory-unsafety.

Pop 8-byte blob header from descriptor: {u32 type@0, u32 payload_len@4}. Bounds-checked: requires remaining>=8 and payload_len<=remaining, then advances cursor and remaining by 8+payload_len. Returns {blob_start, payload=blob_start+8, payload_len}. Sound.
A3AAecDistStage vtable (stage #5 at pipeline+0x610, pipeline+0x88 pointer). slot +0x10=config(type-6), +0x18=run, +0x20=get_hdr_ptr, +0x30=slot_30 (bounded copy into +0x84, max 2). All .rodata.

A3AAecCameraStage vtable (stage #1 at pipeline+0xc0, also pipeline+0x68 pointer). slot +0x10=config(type-10), +0x20=lookup_gain (the delegate invoked by A3AAecDistStage::config). All slots are .rodata constants; none is derived from tuning bytes.

_start (SiFive Freedom Metal crt0, from core.c): gp=0xb02efa00; mtvec=trap_halt_entry; sp=ra=0; call hart_wait_go_and_boot(mhartid,0,0) - all harts spin here until the bootstub writes a go-pointer to mailbox 0x20020000+hartid*4. On failure: mtvec=self+0xc, load from NULL, spin forever. Bundle element type 0x07, 3520 bytes, load 0xb02ee540 (BUND idx 5).
Part of _start: fatal park - retarget mtvec to the lw/spin below, then lw t1,0(zero).

5-hart spin barrier (arg = leader hart, always 1 here). Flags: u32[5] at *(hart_barrier_flags_ptr)=0x02000000. Leader waits for all other harts to set their flag, then clears all 5. Followers set their own flag, fence rw,rw, spin until leader clears it. mstatus.MIE cleared; mie.MSIE set during the wait (IPI-breakable).

Per-hart boot entry (called from _start with a0=hartid,a1=0,a2=0): 1. mscratch=0; spin: t0 = *(u32*)(0x20020000 + mhartid*4) until nonzero. t0==0xFFFFFFFF => clear mailbox, keep waiting (park marker). 2. mscratch = go-ptr (boot data); sp = go_ptr[1] & ~0xf (per-hart stack). 3. copy .data (no-op, LMA==VMA), clear bss [gp-0x4c0, gp-0x338), tp=0. 4. if hartid==1 call hart1_placeholder_hook (ret stub). 5. pmp_unlock_flash_xip(): PMP locked NAPOT RWX 32MB over 0xd0000000+0xe0000000. 6. register_exit_callback(run_fini_runner@b02eed24); mie=0; FPU on if misa has F/D/Q; custom CSR 0x7c1 (cache ctrl) &= ~7. 7. main(1, &argv_ptr, &argv_ptr) -> metal_main; then metal_exit(main_ret).

Tail of hart_shutdown_and_park: clear own mailbox *(u32*)(0x20020000+mhartid*4)=0, then jr to 0x90000fc0 (bootstub park stub in SYSCTL RAM: CSR setup, read mhartid, fence, WFI loop polling shared block 0x402fe000). a0 = caller arg, a1 = 0x90000fc0. Never returns.

Hart shutdown: mstatus.MIE=0 -> execute vendor custom SYSTEM insn 0xFC000073 (not MRET/WFI/SRET - Mars SoC private insn, likely core-idle/stop) -> fence.i -> tail-jump hart_park_into_bootstub (0x90000fc0).
Busy-wait a0 cycles using mcycle CSR (0xb00) delta loop.
Busy-wait us microseconds: delay_cycles((clock_get_rate_hz(7)/1000000) * us).

Write through hart_mailbox_table[idx] (idx<0x30): table holds 48 mailbox addresses = {0x20020000..0x2002003c, 0x20021000..0x2002103c, 0x90124100..0x9012413c}. set_index(hartid,0) = clear own go mailbox.
Look up clock_desc_table[clkid*0x10]: if rate-reg ptr 0 -> 0; check enable bit (entry[8]) in 0x901200c8; return *(u32*)rate_reg (>1) else 2.
PLL frequency from sysctl regs 0x901200e8/0x901200ec: fbdiv=(e8>>2)&0x7ff, postdiv=(e8>>13)&7, refdiv=(ec>>2)&0x3f, bypass bit ec.1; return (fbdiv*25MHz)/postdiv/refdiv.
putchar: uart slot = hart_uart_console_map[mhartid & 0xff], then uart_putc.
Vendor-custom privileged instruction, encoding 0xFC000073 (SYSTEM opcode, funct7=0x7E, all other fields 0). Executed after mstatus.MIE=0 and before fence.i+park. Not a standard RISC-V insn.

Ensure PMP allows both SPI-NOR XIP windows: pmp_find_napot_entry(0xd0000000) / (0xe0000000); if absent, pmp_set_napot_32mb(addr): pmpaddr[i]=(addr>>2)+0x1ffffff (NAPOT 32MB), pmpcfg[i]=0x9b (L=1, NAPOT, R|W|X). Returns AND of both successes.
__assert_func: optional handler at gp-0x348, then prints "\r\nA:<file>:<line>:" over the hart UART and spins forever.
mtvec target (direct mode): read mcause/mepc/mtval into t0/t1/t2, then branch back to itself = freeze the hart for a debugger. The full metal trap dispatcher below (metal_exit) is dead code here.
Shim: exit_callback_register(0, fn, 0, 0).

metal exit path: run registered exit callbacks (exit_callbacks_run), call die hook *(*(metal_runtime_ptr)+0x48) if set, then metal_exit_halt(code). Dead tail: empty fini-array runner (starts at b02eed24) - the function registered as exit callback at boot.
Walk fini_array entries (empty here - no-op).

Register exit callback into lazy-allocated state (gp-0x470, 32 slots): kind param1: 0=fn(void), 1=fn(cause), 2=fn(saved arg w/ flags at +0x200/+0x204). handlers[] at state+0x10; arg slots in sub-struct at state->0x110.
Run registered exit callbacks top-down; arg form depends on kind flags.
exit(code): ecall (traps to trap_halt_entry = freeze); if code<0 store -code at *exit_status_cell target first. Never returns.
Return *(u64*)exit_status_cell (gp-0x748).

hart_mailbox_table: 48 x u32 per-hart go/IPI mailboxes. Bank0 0x20020000+4*hart = boot handoff mailbox polled by hart_wait_go_and_boot (0xFFFFFFFF = stay parked, else pointer to {boot-data, stack-top}). Bank1 0x20021000.., Bank2 0x90124100..
clock_desc_table: 10 x 0x10 {u32 rate_reg 0x901218xx; u32 0x90121848; u32 bitfields (byte0 = enable bit in 0x901200c8); u32 misc}.
uart_base_table: 5 x u64 = 0x20028000, 0x20029000, 0x2002a000, 0x2002b000, 0x90125000. Hart -> slot via hart_uart_console_map.
switch jump table (s32 offsets) for pmp_set_napot_32mb / pmp_find_napot_entry.
argv_ptr -> "libgloss"; main(1, argv_ptr, argv_ptr).
hart_uart_console_map u8[8] (5 used): hart0/1->slot0 (0x20028000), hart2/3->slot3 (0x2002b000), hart4->slot1 (0x20029000).
metal_runtime_ptr -> runtime struct 0xb02ef200 (zeroed); die hook +0x48.
fini_array (empty).
hart_barrier_flags_ptr = 0x02000000: u32[5] barrier flags, one per hart (leader waits for harts 0,2,3,4; flag[0] must be set from outside this image).
exit_status_cell -> 0xb02ef200 (metal_exit_halt writes -exit_code there).

Notify_Enable only sets NotifyOutputEnabled at 0xB0200C40. The stage-3 payload calls this after landing because fqc_main[0]=0 bypasses the factory credential override but skips InitStorage's startup NotifySetEnabled(...,1). This restores the app notification/log gate without re-enabling FQC credentials; direct HELLO output still uses RingUart_PutChar.
App shell command handler. Receives the command-table index plus parsed argv and implements argument validation/conversion and command actions, including target runtime-object dispatch.
DBCMD advanced broadcast path: dispatch parsed opcode and typed argument slots through RuntimeObject_BroadcastOpcode_Entry.
DBCMD argument parser: parses an opcode and up to four type/value pairs (-s, -d, -u), then broadcasts them through RuntimeObject_BroadcastOpcode_Entry.
CMD targeted dispatch path: call RuntimeObject_DispatchToTarget with the selected target ID, opcode, and argument slots.

ACMD argument parser: parses target ID and opcode, then up to four typed payload slots. Supported type tags are -s (string), -d (signed integer), -u (unsigned integer), and -x (hex byte string; parser restricts this variable-length payload to the final slot). The parsed message is sent to RuntimeObject_DispatchToTarget at 0xc0c18c7a.
ACMD targeted dispatch path: after the advanced typed-argument parser has populated the opcode and four argument slots, call RuntimeObject_DispatchToTarget.

App shell text dispatch: uppercases the command token, matches it against the 19-entry CShell_CommandNameDescriptionTable, then passes the matched index and tokenized arguments to CShell_CommandHandler. An unmatched command is dispatched with index 0x13.
Worker consumes a queued console line and calls CShell_DispatchCommand for token matching and command-ID dispatch.
CButton's registered ACMD slot always returns error 0x0D; it is an explicit reject stub.
CButton ACMD vtable slot +8 is the shared unsupported handler b00df5fe.

CHttpServer ACMD handler (function is also used for route matching). Opcode 0x1000B returns success. Opcode 0x10013 accepts selector 0 or 1 and invokes primary-vtable slot +0x30 or +0x38. Opcode 0x10003 requires non-null route/request pointers and returns success only when the extracted route string equals the supplied string; malformed pointers can enter the stack-check failure path, while mismatches return 0x0D.

Provisioning transport read. std::vector reserve(0x1000) via FUN_ram_b0116f26 (an INITIAL reserve only - the vector grows via the same function when the read returns >0x1000, so 0x1000 is NOT a hard cap). Reads from the stream at param_2+0x278 via FUN_ram_c0c20376 -> FUN_ram_b017817a. Returns {status,ptr,len}; caller CDeviceProvision_RxLoop feeds len/ptr to CDeviceProvision_DecodeMessage. Renamed from FUN_ram_c0c1f864.

BLE WEP credential decoder. Requires a nonempty credential and a nonzero key; validates integer key index at input +0x74 with (index-1)<4, then converts it to ASCII '1'..'4' at output +0x88 before the config-tree writer consumes the structure.

CDeviceProvisionFlow_Constructor(this, transport=param_2, param_3, providers=param_4). Layout (this struct /auto_structs/CDeviceProvisionFlow, size 0x3e0): +0x00 vtable (ram:0xc0ca0b00) +0x58 request = malloc(0x138) (decoded BleProvRequest; NOT zeroed before decode) +0x60 response = malloc(0x138) (zeroed by DispatchRequest each command) +0x68 transport (param_2), +0x70 providers (param_4), +0x78 param_3 +0x80 scanActive u8, +0x84 sessionOpen int, +0x1e0 lock, +0x1e8 rxErrorCount Validates provider slots (0x20 stride) at +0x10/0x30/0x50/0x70/0xd0/0x110/0x130/0x150/0x170/0x190/0x1b0/0x1d0. Creates tasks MsgRead (CDeviceProvision_RxLoop, 0x1200) and MsgNotify (CDeviceProvision_NotifyLoop, 0x1000).

BleProv_EncodeAndSendResponse (pre-auth BLE local egress leaf). Encodes the response struct at CDeviceProvisionFlow+0x60 with the protobuf encoder FUN_ram_b01b8374 and sends it via the transport vtable at CDeviceProvisionFlow+0x68. Handlers (Req01..Req0D) set explicit field lengths and copy bounded C-strings / zeroed scratch; no uninitialized or raw RAM bytes are emitted. Reviewed for infoleak: negative.

0c_networking::CDeviceProvision_DispatchRequest
Table g_BleProvDispatchTable (ram:0xc0ca0bd8) stride 16 = {u32 id; u32 pad; code* handler}. Loop ends at ram:0xc0ca0c78 (10 entries). id read from request+8 (u32); request[0] must be 1. handler(flow, request+8) is invoked. No per-field length validation occurs here.
IMPORTANT: several handler pointers point at 4-byte `j`/`addi a1,N; j` thunks that sit just before the Ghidra-named function body, e.g. id 0xc -> c0c22cc0 (`addi a1,8; j c0c22bd6`), id 9 -> c0c22b2e (`j c0c22a86`), id 0xd -> c0c22bd2 (`j c0c22b32`). Account for the a1 adjustment when mapping request offsets to handler fields.
No authentication/pairing check is present on this path; the virtual callback in DecodeMessage (flow+0x78 -> vtable+0x18) runs before this but its result is discarded.

0c_networking::CDeviceProvision_DecodeMessage
Inbound BLE message entry. Inputs: param_2 = decoded-frame length, param_3 = raw frame ptr. Pb_IStreamInit then Pb_DecodeSubmessagePtr(stream, &DAT_ram_c0ca0d48, flow+0x58). The decoded request struct lands in the 0x138 buffer at flow+0x58.
Decode bound (PROVEN in main_app::Pb_DecodeField ram:0xb01b8d5c): a length-prefixed BYTES field (case 6) is accepted only if `len+2 <= field.data_size` else "bytes_overflow"; a STRING field (case 7) only if `len+1 <= field.data_size` else "string_overflow". So any u16 length the handler later trusts is capped by the descriptor's declared data_size, UNLESS the handler reads a length word out of a field that is not actually length-prefixed.
Before DispatchRequest it calls (*(flow+0x78)->vtable+0x18)(obj, &flow) - a notification hook; its return value is NOT used to gate dispatch. No pairing/bonding/encryption check exists in this function or its callee CDeviceProvision_DispatchRequest.
Caller: CDeviceProvision_RxLoop (ram:0xc0c22794) which reads frames from the BLE transport (flow+0x68, vtable slot 1 = ram:0xc0c1f864, refills via FUN_ram_c0c20376).

0c_networking::CDeviceProvision_RxLoop (FreeRTOS task "MsgRead", prio 5, stack 0x1200)
Loops while flow+0x84 (session-open flag) != 0, pulling one frame per iteration from the BLE transport at flow+0x68 (vtable slot 1). Frame type byte: 0 = data -> CDeviceProvision_DecodeMessage; 1 = ignored; 2 = receive error (tears down after 3); 3 = disconnected. Transport c0c1f864 grows a buffer via FUN_ram_b0116f26(...,0x1000) => max reassembled frame 0x1000 bytes. Created from CDeviceProvisionFlow_Constructor (ram:0xc0c21eb4).

BleProv_HandleReq01_Version (dispatch id 1; table thunk ram:0xc0c228c2 -> here). No attacker-controlled fields. Writes response {type=2, cmd=1, field0c=2, payload_field=1, payload u32=2}. BOUNDS: fixed-size writes only, all within the malloc(0x138) response at flow+0x60. No overflow.

BleProv_HandleReq02_GetFirmwareVersion (dispatch id 2; thunk ram:0xc0c2292e -> here). No attacker input. Reads provider (flow+0x70)+0x120/0x138 getFirmwareVersion(), then strncpy-like FUN_ram_b01c3ff8(resp+0x18, ptr, 0x15) (writes <=0x14 chars + NUL). BOUNDS: fixed 0x15 <= 0x138. No overflow.

BleProv_HandleReq03_GetMac (dispatch id 3; thunk ram:0xc0c229dc -> here). No attacker input. snprintf-style FUN_ram_b00c85d4(resp+0x18, 0xd, "%02x..") of provider MAC. BOUNDS: fixed 0xd <= 0x138. No overflow.

BleProv_HandleReq04_GetSerial (dispatch id 4; thunk ram:0xc0c22a82 -> here). No attacker input. Provider getDeviceSerialNumber() copied with FUN_ram_b01c3ff8(resp+0x18, ptr, 0x15). BOUNDS: fixed 0x15 <= 0x138; canary checked. No overflow.

BleProv_HandleReq09_GetDeviceKind (dispatch id 9). COPY SOURCE CORRECTION: source = *(u64*)(sp+8) = the std::string's DATA pointer (_M_p), NOT the object header. So it does NOT copy ptr/size/cap. DEVICE-KIND STRING: CPlatform_GetInstance()->vtable[0x60](3). The platform jump table (ram:b00d1c90, table ram:b01c96b0 indexed by id-3) maps index 3 -> ram:b00d1d5e -> "doorbell_sunray" (15 chars, ram:b01c95c8). strlen=15 => SSO: _M_p = object+0x10 = sp+0x18, and byte 15 is NUL (StdString_ConstructFromCStr). LATENT OOB READ: FUN_b01c3ff8(resp+0x18, sp+0x18, 0x28) reads 0x28 bytes from the 16-byte SSO buffer; sp+0x28 (copy offset 0x10) holds g_stack_canary and sp+0x30/0x38 hold saved s2/s1 (s1 = flow heap ptr). Destination is inside the 0x138 resp buffer: no corruption. EGRESS: the response field f10 is a STRING (prior descriptor note data_size 0x28); BleProv_EncodeAndSendResponse -> FUN_b01b80d4 case 7 uses strlen bounded by data_size, and the source is NUL-terminated at offset 15, so only "doorbell_sunray" is emitted. NO canary/heap leak on the wire (unless the field is encoded as fixed BYTES, which the handler does not set up). Verdict: latent stack OOB read, infoleak REFUTED for the current schema.

BleProv_HandleReq0D (dispatch id 0xd; via thunk ram:c0c22bd2). VERDICT: len is NOT attacker-controlled from BLE. len = *(u64*)(provider_output+0x8). provider_output is the 0x30 stack struct at sp+8 (zeroed, field0=1). The provider callback at flow+0x70 (CSetupSystem->CCentcom_Rdk callback table, "BleProvProvider") is member cb1e0: call (provider+0x1e0)->invoker(provider+0x1e0, provider_output). Invoker = FUN_ram_b0122bea, which runs an RDK transaction (FUN_ram_b0122a8c) then FUN_ram_b011f9a0(provider_output, &DAT_ram_b02128e0): copies tag(+0), u64(+8), 0x11 bytes(+0x10), u32(+0x24), u64(+0x28) from the trusted CCentcom/RDK cache DAT_b02128e0. So len = DAT_b02128e0+8, written only by the CCentcom Rdk path, not by any prior BLE request. The callback only populates 0x11 bytes at +0x10, so any len>0x11 is a stale-stack read; the 0x138 resp block has 0x140 usable bytes, so memcpy overflows only if len>0x126. No BLE-reachable setter for DAT+8 found. NOT a proven primitive. Requires prior RDK compromise.

0c_networking::BleProv_HandleReq0C_CredsMsg (BleProvRequest *param_2; cmd==0xc, credsType==2).
REACHABILITY (proven): g_BleProvDispatchTable id 0xc (entry ram:0xc0ca0c58) -> c0c22cc0, a 4-byte thunk `addi a1,8 ; j c0c22bd6`. DispatchRequest passes request+8, so param_2 == request+0x10. (The prior "id 0xd" note was wrong.)
BODY: serializes {u8 subcmd, u8 2, creds[N], secret[M]} into a fixed 0x1e-byte stack buffer at sp+0x8 and hands &buf to the credentials callback (*(*(this+0x70)+0x1d8))(this+0x1c0,&buf): prov_memcpy(sp+0xa, param_2->creds, param_2->credsLen) prov_memcpy(sp+0x1a, param_2->secret, param_2->secretLen)
BOUNDING (proven, removes the prior "unchecked" claim): - creds and secret are length-prefixed BYTES fields; Pb_DecodeField (ram:0xb01b8d5c) rejects len+2 > field.data_size ("bytes_overflow"). Their descriptors (c0ca0eb0, reached via the id==0xc schema c0ca0ef0) declare data_size 18 (creds, max 16) and 14 (secret, max 12). - Maxima 16/12 exactly tile the buffer: 2 + 16 + 12 = 0x1e (sp+0x8..sp+0x25). Stack geometry: canary g_stack_canary at sp+0x28; saved s4..s0 at sp+0x30..0x50; ra at sp+0x58. To reach the canary would need credsLen>=0x1e or secretLen>=0xe; to reach ra, credsLen>=0x56 or secretLen>=0x46. With the enforced maxima (16/12) NEITHER copy reaches the canary. Both return paths compare against the canary and call prov_stack_chk_fail (noreturn) on mismatch.
VERDICT: bounded by construction - not a stack-buffer overflow.
thunk: addi a1,8 ; j BleProv_HandleReq0C_CredsMsg (c0c22bd6). Dispatch table id 0xc entry points here, not at the named body.

BleProv_HandleReq0C_Notify (notification path; reached from CDeviceProvision_NotifyLoop, not from a BLE request). memset response 0x138 then fixed writes {type=3, cmd=1, payload=status}. No attacker length. No overflow.

BleProv notification-error builder. memset response 0x138; fixed writes; if param_3[1]!=0 copies FUN_ram_b01c3ff8(resp+0x1c, *param_3, 0x65) (<=0x64 chars + NUL). BOUNDS: 0x1c+0x65=0x81 < 0x138. No attacker length. No overflow.

BleProv_HandleReq06_SetRegionCountry (dispatch id 6; thunk ram:0xc0c2309c -> here). Attacker fields (payload f6): country = f6.f1 string abs 0x18 data_size 3 (<=2 chars + NUL); region = f6.f2 string abs 0x1b data_size 0xb (<=10 chars + NUL). Validation: country[2]==0, region[10]==0, region[0]!=0, strlen(country)==2. Copies FIXED 3 bytes from region and 3 from country into a 6-byte local (uStack_a8), then to provider (flow+0x70)+0x40/0x58. BOUNDS: no attacker length reaches a copy. No overflow.

BleProv_HandleReq06_SetCredentials (payload f8; reached via id 7 Req07 when payload oneof selector==8 and u16@payload+0x58==4). Attacker fields live in f8 (abs 0x18..0x12c): f1 string (0x40), f2 string (0xb), f4 submessage (0xc0). credsType = f4 selector at payload+0x5c; credential data at payload+0x60. Decoders FUN_ram_c0c21c62/c9a/d48/dea copy FIXED 0x21/0x40/0x10/0xb bytes into a 0xd0 stack buffer; no attacker length is used as a copy count. BOUNDS: fixed. Canary checked. No overflow.

BleProv_HandleReq07 (dispatch id 7; thunk ram:0xc0c23334 -> here). Checks payload oneof selector==8 and u16@payload+0x58==4, then tail-calls SetCredentials (ram:0xc0c230a2). No attacker length/alloc/index. No overflow.

AP-list builder (called by Req05). Walks the WiFi scan tree (FUN_ram_b0163abe/FUN_ram_b0164a08) and builds a std::vector of 0x34-byte entries. malloc(count*0x34) with count <= DAT_ram_c0ca0bb8 (aborts otherwise); SSID copied with FUN_ram_b01c3ff8(entry+4, str, 0x21); fixed strcmp against known security strings. BOUNDS: allocation and copies are bounded/fixed. No overflow.

BleProv_HandleReq05_SessionClose (dispatch id 5; thunk ram:0xc0c23862 -> here). No attacker input. Builds AP list via FUN_ram_c0c23434 (fixed 0x34-byte entries, <=0x21 strncpy, malloc count bounded by DAT_ram_c0ca0bb8) and installs encoder callback FUN_ram_c0c21b02 with arg=&local vector into response field f7 (type-9 callback field). Encoding is synchronous. BOUNDS: fixed. No overflow.

CDeviceProvisionFlow vtable slot 3 (vtable ram:0xc0ca0b00 +0x18). Atomically clears flow+0x84 (session-open flag) and tears down the BLE transport (transport vtable +0x10/+0x28). Not a BLE request handler; not attacker-reachable directly. Previously mis-named BleProv_HandleReq05_SessionClose.

CSetupSystem_InitProviderCallbacks(provider_new, blueprint): move-constructs a 0x220 BleProvProvider by moving each of the 17 std::function members (functor at +0x00..0x0f, _M_manager at +0x10, _M_invoker at +0x18) from `blueprint` into `provider_new`, zeroing the source. Called by CSetupSystem_Construct right after malloc(0x220).

CRingConnection_LoadBleBundle: loads bundle element type 0x65 (101) directly into the fixed 0x1c2c0-byte BLE-stack segment at ram:0xc0010000 via FUN_ram_b016820c(0x65,0xc0010000). On success zeroes the 0x1058 struct at 0xc002c2c0 and regs the stack. DEST SIZE (0x1c2c0) IS NOT CHECKED AGAINST THE HEADER ELEMENT SIZE -> see FUN_ram_b016820c.

Cache-flush trampoline in 0c_networking::CRingConnection_LoadBleBundle: after bundle load/zeroing, calls app cflush+fence and fence.i helpers, then loads ra from sp+8, adds 0x10 to sp, and returns. This is the cfg_off=8 zero-preflush path the generator should find by scanning the extracted 02_app_type0c_off001ba240.bin at 0xC0C10000.

CRingConnection_LoadBleBundleAndInit: one-shot init. Calls LoadBleBundle (loads element 0x65 into c0010000), sets flag at this+0x11, then opens the BLE session (SUB c001c46c), registers GATT (SUB c002139e with DAT b01f9ed8), enables radio (SUB c001c6ac), waits on stack timeout. The GATT write characteristic is what delivers attacker bytes into the CRingConnection / CDeviceProvision handlers.

Copies the connection handler list at this+0xb8 under mutex (this+0xb0), allocating a 0x30 CRingConnection_Handler per entry, then releases the mutex and invokes each copied handler (node+0x28) with the BLE event param_3. Node layout: +0x10 copied payload, +0x20 copier fn, +0x28 handler fn. Only a !=0 check precedes the indirect calls; if a handler node is heap-corrupted this is a direct control-flow target (inferred). param_2 (transport id) is stored at this+0xd0 and the previous value freed with size 0x18.

App-side GATT write callback candidate (registered table ram:b01f9f20+0x10). Rejects the write unless byte at param_5+0x10 == 0xff (format check only - no pairing/auth check). Builds event {ptr=*(u64*)(param_5+8), len=*(u16*)param_5, type=1} and calls CRingConnection::DispatchBleData. Sends a 25-byte ATT response when param_4==1. UNCERTAIN MAPPING: the BLE-stack write slot _DAT_ram_c0011cee0 is invoked with a4 = ATT offset (integer), not a pointer, so param_5 here is an app-level write-event struct, not the raw ATT request; which registered slot this function occupies is unproven.

Sibling of DispatchBleData for non-data events (connect/disconnect/MTU). Same handler-list copy+invoke. Frees the stored this+0xd0 event with size 4 whereas DispatchBleData frees it with size 0x18 (inconsistent size passed to the tracked allocator; param_2 is always 0 on current callers so the free is not reached). Renamed from FUN_ram_c0c254c8.

CUpdate_ARES::ParseOtafuVersion(this, image_index, version, checksum). Parses the cloud OTAFU descriptor for image_index 0/1, sets update_valid_mask(this+0x2d0) bit image_index, and stores the cloud-provided checksum at img_ver[image_index]+0x10. Attacker (cloud) controls both.

CUpdate_ARES::CommitAndSelectBootSlot(this). Marks *(this+0x25c) bootable then sets it active via bootctl2. This is the persistence sink: the slot selected here is what the device boots next. Commit slot is derived from active/other slot bytes set in PrepareOtaSlotFile.

CUpdate_ARES ACMD handler accepts opcode 0x10048. It checks the updater's +0x1D4 state/sentinel, queries an 8-byte record at +0x1D8, logs current/previous slot or version values, and returns 0. Other opcodes return 0x0D.
CUpdate_ARES adjustor thunk subtracts 0x20 from the registered RuntimeObject pointer and enters CUpdate_ARES_AcmdDispatch.

CUpdate_ARES::VerifyBundleSha256(this, hdr, slot, secureboot). Per-element SHA-256 over data re-read from otaA/otaB (slot selects); expected digest[32] (hdr element stride 0x34) is attacker-controlled. BUG (proven): extent = offset+size uses 32-bit c.addw at ram:c0c28832, wraps at 2^32 and bypasses the capacity guard at c0c2883c, feeding an out-of-range SetReadPosition. Contained by fm_flash_read's own offset+len partition check.
BUG: c.addw performs a 32-bit `size + offset`. If it wraps, the capacity check at c0c2883c is bypassed and SetReadPosition() below gets an out-of-range offset.

CUpdate_ARES::IsFwblUpdateAllowed(this) -> bool. Returns 1 when update_valid_mask(this+0x2d0)&2==0 (no FWBL in the cloud list). With FWBL listed: returns 0 unless fwbl_ota_enabled(this+0x268) is set; then returns fwbl_ota_standalone_enabled(this+0x269) (and requires it, or an APP in the list). Both enable bytes are set by HandleFwblOtaCommand opcodes.

CUpdate_ARES::SetUpdateImageList(this). If IsFwblUpdateAllowed()==0 clears both masks; else update_allowed_mask(this+0x2d8)=update_valid_mask and copies the cloud checksums into img0_checksum(this+0x2e0)/img1_checksum(this+0x2e8).

Bounded: header is fixed 0xf20 (CUpdate_ARES_VerifyImage 0xc0c29bc0 alloc 0xf20, read <=0xf20 after file-size check). VerifyBundleSha256 0xc0c285ea: element count 1..0x40, stride 0x34, base hdr or hdr+0x200, max element byte read = 0xF18 <= 0xF20; chunk reads <=0x100 into 256 B buffer. No OOB write.

Reads the bundle header from OTA slot A/B into the caller buffer (param_2) of size param_3. Rejects param_3 > partition capacity; seeks to 0, PRead, then resets. `this` is otaA_partition when param_4==0, else otaB_partition. Callers use 0xF20 (CUpdate_ARES_VerifyImage).

CUpdate_ARES::GetSlotToVerify(this, image_index) -> 0=otaA,1=otaB,2=invalid. Requires active_slot(this+0x261) < 2 and image_index < 6. 2 -> 0 ; 3 -> 1 ; 4 -> active_slot ; 5 -> active_slot^1 0,1 -> commit_pending(this+0x267)==0 ? active_slot : active_slot^1 NOTE: in a pure FWBL flow commit_pending==0, so VerifyImage(1) verifies the ACTIVE (currently-running) OTA slot, not the FWBL target slot. In the APP flow OtaEventHandler_App event 3 sets commit_pending=1 first, so VerifyImage(0) verifies the other/target slot.

CUpdate_ARES::SetFwblSlot(this, mode). mode 0/1/2 -> FUN_b0167fec(buf,0x80, 2-mode): 0 = compare+sync the two 0x20000 FWBL halves; 1/2 = copy primary<-> secondary. Then SYSCTL_set_fwbl_slot_G(0) selects PRIMARY. This is the FWBL persistence sink (fwbl boot register), analogous to CommitAndSelectBootSlot.

CUpdate_ARES::VerifyFwblImageType(this, restore_slot_mode). Reads the 4-byte magic @flash+0 and the type byte @flash+0x1c of BOTH fwblB (ReadFwblMagicVersion arg1) and fwblA (arg0) directly from the FWBL partitions. PASS iff the two magics are equal AND (typeA==typeB==0 [MFG bootloader] OR both types are in 1..7 [PROD]). Otherwise logs 'FWBL OTA Update flow' and calls SetFwblSlot(this, restore_slot_mode) to restore, returning 0. SECURITY: reads attacker-controlled flash; it compares the two EXISTING slots and does NOT authenticate the newly written fwbl payload (no signature/hash). It only enforces 'same kind as the other slot' and cannot stop an unsigned FWBL.

CUpdate_ARES::PrepareOtaSlotFile(this, image_type). image_type 0 (APP): require update_allowed_mask(this+0x2d8)&1; commit_slot = other_slot (asserted == active^1); running_slot(this+0x258) = active_slot; write target = otaA if commit_slot==0 else otaB; posts event 5. image_type 1 (FWBL): require update_allowed_mask&2; SetFwblSlot(this,2); write target = fwblA (0xb021f9d8); posts event 4. image_type 2: notify finalize (event 6). update_allowed_mask is set from the parsed cloud image list (SetUpdateImageList).

0c_networking::CUpdate_PemMarkerStateMachine(this, state, count, buf, len) Byte-transition matcher for the PEM markers. state is a signed char (init 3), indexes a 4-entry table (safe, state restricted to {0,2,3} by the code). count is incremented when a marker byte matches / reset to 0 otherwise; that count is what FindBundleKeyOffset uses to size the key. No writes past buf+len.

0c_networking::CUpdate_ScanForBundleKey(this, slot, end_out, count_out, scan_start) Uses fwblA/fwblB_partition globals (slot selects). Gets capacity, then walks backwards from scan_start in 0x80-byte windows, PRead() into a 0x80-byte stack buffer (sp+8..sp+0x88, canary at sp+0x90 -> exact fit). Each window is fed to CUpdate_PemMarkerStateMachine(this,&state,&count,buf,0x80) which matches PEM marker bytes against a 4-entry transition table and accumulates a byte count. *end_out = scan_start + accumulated_count. Bounds: requires scan_start < capacity. attacker-controlled flash only changes WHICH offsets are selected, never the window/buffer sizes -> no stack overflow (inferred, high confidence).

0c_networking::CUpdate_FindBundleKeyOffset(this, fwbl_slot, key_end_out, key_size_out, scan_start) Outputs (disasm-verified): - *param3 (&sp[0xc]) = key_end_from_end = (end2 - 4) - cnt2 [0xc0c2941c] - *param4 (&sp[0x10]) = key_size = key_end_from_end - end1 [0xc0c2942c] where end1 = 1st ScanForBundleKey outA, end2 = 2nd outA, cnt2 = 2nd state-machine count. Checks: 1<slot rejected; cnt2+4 < end2; end1 < key_end_from_end (all unsigned 32-bit). NOTE (correcting earlier comment): param5 (scan_start) IS set by the caller (0 or *(this+0x24c)), it is not stale. SECURITY: *param4 (used as malloc size AND as ReadBundleKey length) is strictly smaller than *param3 (from_end), and both are <= partition capacity. No truncation: param4 is zero-extended to 64-bit at 0xc0c29428 before the sd at 0xc0c2942c.
a4 (ScanForBundleKey param_5, scan start) is not set here -> passes the caller's stale register.

0c_networking::CUpdate_ReadBundleKey(this, slot, dst, len, from_end). Re-opens fwblA (0xb021f9d8) / fwblB (0xb021f9e0) by slot, re-reads capacity, and if (from_end < capacity && len < from_end) reads len bytes at capacity-from_end into dst. This is the RSA public-key source used by VerifySignature -> it is attacker-writable flash, not a ROM/OTP anchor. TOCTOU: capacity/offsets are recomputed here after FindBundleKeyOffset's scan.
CUpdate_ARES registers RuntimeObject target CUpdate_ARES at offset +0x20. Its slot +8 is adjustor thunk c0c280ae, which dispatches opcode 0x10048.

Trust-anchor note (static analysis): VerifySignature obtains its PEM public key through FindBundleKeyOffset and ReadBundleKey, which read fwblA/fwblB flash. For image_index==1 the slot is 0 and scan_start is fwbl_dl_size. In the FWBL update flow, fwblA is the write target before this check. Treat the RSA key as flash-sourced; whether a separate hardware/root verification authenticates that key at boot is unresolved.

Updater verification finding (static analysis): param_2/image_index controls whether VerifySignature runs. When image_index==0, the RSA check is skipped; the function still compares SHA-256 digests against values in the same OTA header. OtaEventHandler_App calls VerifyImage(this,0), then AppOtaFinalize can mark and select the slot when write_error==0. This proves an updater authentication gap for APP images. Whether the reset-time secure-boot loader independently rejects such an image remains unverified.

CUpdate_ARES::HandleFwblOtaCommand(this, opcode). Jump-table dispatcher (opcodes 0..10) for the cloud/local bootloader-OTA feature control: 0/1 -> fwbl_ota_enabled(this+0x268)=1/0 ('FWBL OTA enabled/disabled') 2/3 -> fwbl_ota_standalone_enabled(this+0x269)=1/0 4/5 -> SetFwblSlot(this,1/0) 6/7/9/10 -> VerifyImage(this,2/3/4/5) 8 -> VerifyFwblImageType(this,1) default -> 'Bootloader OTA feature opcode %zu not accepted: use %d ~ %d'. These opcodes are the enable gate consumed by IsFwblUpdateAllowed.

CUpdate_ARES::OtaEventHandler_App(this, event, ctx, payload). event 0: open OTA target slot for write. event 2: PWrite chunk. event 3: sets commit_pending(this+0x267)=1 then VerifyImage(this,0) -- APP path, which skips RSA signature verification (see VerifyImage).
OtaEventHandler_App event 3 passes image_index=0 to VerifyImage. This bypasses VerifySignature; VerifyBundleSha256 alone compares payload digests to the OTA header being verified.

Updater verification finding (static analysis): event 3 closes the FWBL target, calls VerifyFwblImageType, compares fwbl_checksum with checksum of bytes written, then calls VerifyImage(this,1). PrepareOtaSlotFile(image_type=1) selects fwblA as target and calls SetFwblSlot(this,2). VerifySignature(image_index=1) selects FWBL slot 0 and uses fwbl_dl_size as scan_start; CUpdate_ReadBundleKey reads the extracted key from fwblA. VerifyImage's bundle header/payload comes from otaA/otaB, so this signature check does not authenticate the FWBL bytes just written. The type check only compares FWBL magic/type fields across slots. Reset-time secure-boot behavior is not established here.
CUpdateStats_ARES registers its RuntimeObject with target name CUpdateStats_ARES. Its actual ACMD slot +8 is CUpdateStats_ARES_AcmdDispatch (c0c2a588), not the shared unsupported handler.
CUpdateStats_ARES subtype-7 ACMD helper clears the three counters at offsets +0x5C, +0x60, and +0x64.
CUpdateStats_ARES ACMD handler recognizes only opcode 0x10001 with subtype 7, which clears three OTA statistics fields (+0x5C/+0x60/+0x64). Other opcode/subtype combinations return 0x0D.

CAuthManager ACMD dispatcher. Opcode 0x10001 virtual-dispatches an auth-manager subtype. Opcode 0x10049 subcommands 1..4: damage/clear a stored access header when its length is at least 0x1E; request token rotation via a Centcom event; switch auth fallback to basic mode; and mark the refresh token corrupt, attempting a storage update. Unsupported selectors return 0x0D.

CConsole_PrintfOrPrompt(console, message): copies the caller-supplied string into the console's internal message buffer, then emits it through the configured channel vtable. This provides a marker path through the application's initialized console and does not depend on Notify_Enable's logger gate.

CConsole_MARS ACMD dispatcher. Opcode 0x10023 invokes the console mode/start path; 0x10024 invokes the corresponding stop/cleanup path; 0x100A4 sets a boolean state field at +0x41C. Exact end-user command labels are not recoverable from this wrapper alone.
Console listener queues a completed command line for CShell_ThreadMain.

0c_networking CFastpingTest report builder (assert tag s_CFastpingTest::CResultStatusRepo). BeginBuild(0x37=55, 10): 55 CTreeNode slots (55*0x18=0x528) + 65 index slots (0x104), total 0x62C bytes. Inserts exactly 55 static key leaves (4 + 1 + 3 + 1 + 2 + 1 + six 7-node groups + 3) and pushes exactly 10 child-count markers (4,3,2, six 6s, 10). EXACT FIT -> the unbounded-insert bug is NOT triggered. All keys/values are static strings/globals; no attacker byte influences the insert count. Materialized via CTree::Materialize into a 0x28 object stored at param_1[0xb]. PROVEN.
CFastpingTest::CResultStatusReport ACMD wrapper. Only opcode 0x10001 is accepted; it sign-extends and forwards the two supplied values to report routine c0c2e438. Other opcodes return 0x0D.

0c_networking CEgressTest report builder (assert tag s_CEgressTest::CResultStatusReport). BeginBuild(0xc=12, 1): 12 node slots + 13 index slots. Inserts exactly 12 static key leaves (ipTarget, nPort, nPacketSize, msDuration, msPushing, nBytesSent, txshape, msMaxStall, pStalled, pContention, SO_SNDBUF, txrate) and pushes one child-count marker (12). EXACT FIT -> the unbounded-insert bug is NOT triggered. No attacker-controlled count. PROVEN.
CEgressTest::CResultStatusReport ACMD wrapper. Only opcode 0x10001 is accepted; it sign-extends and forwards the two supplied values to report routine c0c2f1a4. Other opcodes return 0x0D.

CNetworkCheck ACMD handler. Opcode 0x10049 acts only for subtype 0, invoking the nested object's virtual slot +0x38 with the stored object+0x1228 value. Opcode 0x10087 passes (arg3 != 0) to FUN_ram_c0c331f8, then either calls FUN_ram_c0c325fc when arg4 is zero and arg5 nonzero, or calls FUN_ram_c0c32d42 with arg4. Both recognized opcodes return 0; unsupported opcodes return 0x0D.

CRiidManager registered interface body (adjustor thunk c0c35012 subtracts 8 from this). Opcode 0x10001 forwards a subtype to c0c34e24. Opcode 0x1007A accepts selectors 0/1: selector 0 logs a RIID-related condition; selector 1 stores a boolean through c0c348ba. Other selectors/opcodes return 0x0D.

CDeviceLocation ACMD dispatcher. Opcode 0x10001 accepts subtype 6 and calls CDeviceLocation_UpdateCC only when the enable byte at object+0x108 is nonzero. Opcode 0x1008A forwards to CDeviceLocation_Command. Other inputs return 0x0D.

CBatteryManager ACMD: opcode 0x10001 forwards the supplied subtype to vtable slot +0x110 (CBatteryManager_QueryOrRefreshStats). Opcode 0x1003C selector 0 invokes a virtual operation; selector 1 clears the sampling state/threshold fields and runs the reset helper; selector 2 stores the supplied threshold and marks it valid. Other selectors/opcodes return 0x0D.
CBatteryManager adjustor thunk subtracts 8 from the registered subobject pointer and enters CBatteryManager_AcmdDispatch.

CBatteryManager virtual method used by ACMD opcode 0x10001. For subtype/operation 0, selector 0x200 or 0x80..0xFF requests the virtual query using object+0x154; other selector values refresh external-power diagnostics and derived battery metrics through c0c39f44/c0c3a0ee. Nonzero subtype returns success without action.

CBatteryManager registers an embedded RuntimeObject at offset +8 with target name CBatteryManager. Its vtable slot +8 is CBatteryManager_AcmdThunk (c0c3a29a), which dispatches opcodes 0x10001 and 0x1003C.

CRebootManager handles opcode 0x1002E by recalculating the periodic reboot schedule. Opcode 0x1002F argument type 0 toggles periodic reboot, type 2 toggles reboot-when-idle, type 1 schedules reboot at next idle, and type 3 logs status including idle/periodic timer state. Other types log unsupported and return 0.

CGrecoController_OnMdsMigrationPackage: cloud E2EE migration-message consumer. Gets a package buffer/len from CGrecoController_GetMdsMigrationPackage and calls Greco_TinyMlsMigrate(...,buf+2,len-2,...). Attacker source = cloud Greco/MDS message.

Greco_TinyMls_ParseGroupInfo(out, dst, base, len, &offset): MlsCursor over (base,len); uStack_48/uStack_44 alias cursor.len/pos. Loop over `count` entries; the for-increment (uStack_44 - uVar1) correctly accumulates consumed bytes (NOT an infinite loop). Guard uVar5<0x861 before memcpy into dst (0x864 region) plus len>=pos check -> copies are in-bounds. NO OOB found.

Greco_TinyMls_ImportGroupState(out, group, base, len, ...): MlsCursor reads into fixed sub-fields of the 0x32e8 group state (0x864, 0x1fc8, 0x680, 0x20, ...) all via MlsCursor_ReadBytes(dst,max) which zeroes the copy on overrun; and the entry loop is bounded to 6. Attacker lengths do not translate to unchecked copies. No OOB found.

Greco_TinyMls_MigrateParse: cursor.len/pos alias iStack_d8/uStack_d4. iVar3==0 path (param_5==0): ImportGroupState(base, len) where base=(pos-2)+buf = buf and len=(len+2)-pos = len; in-bounds. iVar3==1 path needs param_5!=0 AND a valid Greco_ExternalKey_VerifyPackageTag (crypto) before reaching ImportGroupState. The prior-pass "underflow" (uStack_d4-2)/(len+2-offset) only yields the intentional 2-byte rewind once pos>=2; not reachable with pos>len. No OOB proven.

Greco_ExternalKey_VerifyPackageTag(ctx, ..., tag, tagLen, ..., outLen). Copies 0x21 bytes from ctx+0x21 into a local 0x21 buffer (bounded). Checks tagLen==0x10 and tagLen <= *outLen before computing/compare the AEAD tag (constant-time 16-byte compare). Returns -1 on failure. No length-driven copy into a fixed buffer; the only memcpy source is the fixed 0x21 context field.
Greco_TinyMlsMigrate: length-relabeling wrapper. Strips 2 bytes when param_5!=0 ((int)len-2), then MigrateParse. Attacker-controlled buf/len from the cloud migration package.

Greco_TinyMls_ProcessMdsPackage: other ImportGroupState caller. Bound checks uStack_58 < uStack_54 (declared vs consumed) before import; the later copy into the 0x168 staging area is guarded by (iStack_70-2U < 0x9d). No unbounded attacker-length copy found.

E2eeCommon_ValidateJsonRequest(str, label) - WEAK validation: only checks str != NULL and str[0] != 0. It does NOT validate JSON syntax/schema. Used by CPolicy_SetTargetsFromJson before handing the string to the JSON parser, so any non-empty attacker string reaches the JSON layer. Informational: not itself memory-unsafe, but defeats the stated "validate request" intent.

CManifest::BuildSignedManifest - assembles manifest JSON (schemaVersion/documentVersion/manifestId/owner/cekDetails/signedManifest/signature/attestationDetails) and signs it (SHA256withECDSA); verifies container/signature before returning.

CPolicy_AddTargetsFromCerts: for cert extension 2 (SKID) the length returned by E2eeCrypto_GetCertExtension (a1) is passed to StdVector_AllocateElements(&vec, a1) (malloc(a1)) and then prov_memcpy(vec, ext_ptr, a1). Allocation size == copy size -> NO heap overflow. Prior-pass suspicion disproven (decompiler printed a single arg but a1=len at the call site). Certificate must pass CE2eeCrypto_VerifyCert first.

CPolicy_SetTargetsFromJson. SECURITY NOTE: its "validation" is E2eeCommon_ValidateJsonRequest, which only checks the string is non-null/non-empty (no schema check). Target public keys are then taken from attacker JSON but must pass CE2eeCrypto_VerifyCert (mbedtls_x509_crt_verify against the provisioned trust store). Per the threat model (crypto sound) that signature gate is the only real barrier; nothing here is pre-auth.
CController ACMD wrapper. Opcode 0x10001 forwards the supplied subtype and arguments to c0c5509a. Other opcodes return 0; deeper controller-state behavior is in that routine.

CController::InitServiceEndpoints - configures base URLs for the Amazon "Cerulean" E2EE backend. prod/gamma branch uses https://{ring.|}{.prod.|.gamma.}<region>.cerulean.devices.amazon.dev with "key_mgmt" (CKMS) and "manifest_mgmt" (CMMS) service labels. The else branch (param_4 != 0) hardcodes PLAINTEXT http://ckms and http://cmms.
http://ckms -> stored at this+0xa8 (CKMS key-management base URL)
http://cmms -> stored at this+0xc8 (CMMS manifest-management base URL)

CController::RegisterProducerWithCKMS - builds a self-signed cert (CN=ProducerDevice, pikX509/keychainId/signedEncryptionPolicy), POSTs it to <CKMS base>/v1/participatingInstance/producer, then persists returned ASK/PIK certs via CE2eeLocalStorage.

CController::UploadManifestToCMMS - builds/signs an E2EE manifest (SHA256withECDSA), POSTs manifest to CMMS, then PUTs per-key /v1/manifest/<id>/cekDetails. Fetches target PIK/AEK lists via GET tPK and parses them with CPolicy.

SFrame_GetFooterSize(in, len, out_version, out_magic).
Reads the 5-byte trailer at in[len-4] (magic LE: 'SCBC'=0x53434243 or 'GRCO'=0x4f435247) and the footer size byte at in[len-5]. Rejects size<6 or size>len. Returns the raw footer size; version = byte at in[len-size]>>4 (must be 1 or 2). NOTE: returns the attacker-controlled size byte directly to callers; see SFrame_ReadHeaderFields for the missing min-size check.

SFrame_ReadHeaderFields - parse attacker header at in+inLen-footer_size.
BUG (proven): footer_size only validated >=6 (and <=inLen) by SFrame_GetFooterSize, but the SCBC path reads header byte [0x15] (key id) and the GRCO path reads [0x1a..0x1e]. With footer_size in [6,0x15] the parser reads up to +0x18 past the *frame* end. For the inbound path the frame is at the start of the fixed staging global DAT_ram_b0217940 (0x141 bytes) with inLen<=0x140, so the overshoot passes the global only when inLen is near max: max read = b0217940+0x140-6+0x1e = b0217a98, i.e. 0x17 past the buffer. When inLen is small the overshoot stays inside the staging buffer (stale/zero bytes). CANARY unreachable (~0x7f920 away).
ESCALATION - NEGATIVE (proven by data-flow): the over-read bytes land in flags/version/keyEpoch/ counter/keyId/salt outputs. keyId is only compared against installed keys (bounded, max 4) and otherwise makes the frame decode fail; no field becomes a write length/offset, none is echoed, so the read cannot be escalated to a write or an infoleak. Callers: SFrame_Decrypt c0c59de6, c0c5a238.

SFrame E2EE encoder (CSframeE2ee). Handles NAL/slice parsing, optional codec padding, header/footer write, AES-GCM encrypt and auth tag. Contains an unimplemented SFRAME_FLAG_CODEC_CONFIG_SEPARATE_AUTH path (see 0xc0c59474).

Security-relevant TODO stub: if a codec-config slice is present (flag bit0) and separate-auth is configured (context+0x118 != 0), the encoder ORs in SFRAME_FLAG_CODEC_CONFIG_SEPARATE_AUTH (bit1) and logs this TODO, then CONTINUES. The flag is emitted in the frame header but the separate authentication is never implemented.

SFrame_Decrypt(SFrame_Context *ctx, in, inLen, out, &outLen) - inbound E2EE decryptor.
Entry checks: ctx->key_count!=0; in/out/outLen != NULL; *outLen >= inLen; no overlap. Then: SFrame_GetFooterSize (validates footer_size in [6,inLen] and version in {1,2}); ctx->version saved; branch on ctx->codec: 1..4 -> video NAL/slice path, >=5 -> simple audio path. Audio path: ReadHeaderFields -> key lookup (bounded by key_count) -> SFrame_BuildNonce* -> FUN_b01b651a setkey/IV -> FUN_b01b66fa start -> FUN_b01b6786 AAD accumulate -> FUN_b01b67f8 GCM/CBC decrypt -> SFrame_VerifyAuthTag at (in+ptLen+5|10) -> replay window.
WRITE-SAFETY (proven by inspection + disasm): the only ciphertext length is ptLen = inLen - footer_size; out capacity was checked >= inLen at entry, so decrypt never writes more than *outLen. Header fields from the attacker (incl. the OOB over-read in ReadHeaderFields) only select a key (bounded index), build the nonce/AAD, or feed the replay counter - none is used as a write length/offset. Cipher is GCM (cipher_mode==1) or CBC; AES-CBC round-down copy is bounded. Video-path emulation-prevention fixup write `*in[inLen-5-cnt] -= cnt` stays inside the frame; out-cap check accounts for added NAL overhead. No escalation of the header OOB read to a write. Only caller: CSframeE2ee_Decrypt (b01439f2).

CAdaptiveIRLed registered interface handler (adjustor thunk c0c5d0fc subtracts 0x10 from this). Opcode 0x10001 forwards a subtype into the LED-state getter/setter helper. Opcode 0x10090 accepts selector 0 or 1: selector 0 forwards several configuration values to the update helper; selector 1 stores a boolean at object+0xB7 and updates LED state/logging. Unsupported selector/opcode returns 1.

CSheilaManager ACMD dispatcher. Opcode 0x10001 accepts subtype 6 and runs two manager routines. Opcode 0x1004A: subtype 1 invokes manager operation 4; subtype 2 sets/query-updates one of seven indexed flags and may trigger the manager update when argument 4 is nonzero; subtype 3 logs and notifies listeners. Invalid selector/index returns 0x0D.

CSettings registered ACMD body (adjustor thunk at c0c6384e subtracts 8 from this). Only accepts opcode 0x10041. Selector 0 logs settings-related information and invokes a helper using a 0x40-byte local buffer; selector 1 builds/logs a second settings record and passes it through conversion/helper routines; selector 2 stores a boolean at object+0x51. Other selectors/opcodes return 0x0D.
IpHold ACMD wrapper. Only opcode 0x10001 is accepted; it forwards the subtype and arguments to c0c663ca. Other opcodes return 0x0D.

CPrerollManager ACMD handler accepts opcode 0x10001 only. Subtype 7 invokes the helper on the object's +0x130 timer/state field with the fixed 0x3C argument; other subtype/opcode combinations return 0.
CPrerollManager adjustor thunk subtracts 8 from the registered subobject pointer and enters CPrerollManager_AcmdDispatch.
CPrerollManager registers an embedded RuntimeObject at offset +8; its actual ACMD slot +8 is CPrerollManager_AcmdThunk (c0c68da6), supporting opcode 0x10001/subtype 7.
CSnapshotMetrics ACMD wrapper. Only opcode 0x10001 is accepted; it forwards subtype and arguments to the snapshot-metrics method at c0c7094a. Other opcodes return 0x0D.

CSysTimer subtype handler. Subtype 2 selectors 0x101, 0x102, 0x103 access the start-streaming time, UTC-offset text, and uptime fields. Subtype 3 selector 0x102 takes the UTC-offset-field path. Subtype 4 selector 0x102 parses the stored offset and, when changed and within the accepted range, updates the global offset and broadcasts opcode 0x1002E. Exact wire-level field semantics for subtype 3 remain unclear.

CSysTimer ACMD wrapper for registered target ID CSysTimer: accepts only opcode 0x10001, then forwards subtype/selector and arguments to CSysTimer_SubtypeDispatch; other opcodes return 0. The field initialized to "+00:00" is the default UTC offset, not the target ID.

CNotify_RDK ACMD dispatcher. Opcode 0x10023 builds a “Sleep” log message from the requested duration and current log count, stores a timestamp, then calls a notification operation. Opcode 0x10001 subtype 6 enables/disables notifications based on object state and may update state. Opcode 0x1000D returns 0x18; opcode 0x10024 calls notification stop/cleanup routines.

CThermal ACMD handler. Opcode 0x1001C calls thermal-state setup then FUN_ram_c0c73558; 0x10022 calls setup then FUN_ram_c0c7374e; 0x10025 calls setup then FUN_ram_c0c7376e; 0x100A2 calls setup then FUN_ram_c0c7378e with its three supplied values. Each path returns 0. The previous 0x100C4 parse was incorrect; that value is not accepted here.

CEventReporter vtable entry. This is not an opcode-switch dispatcher: it first checks the gate at this+0x6E4 and a referenced object at this+0x558; only if both checks pass does it tail-dispatch through the primary vtable with an extra zero argument. Otherwise returns 0x10. Exact target interface semantics remain unresolved.

CBootReason ACMD dispatcher. Opcode 0x10001 handles subtype 2/5 with selector 0x102 (returning a field or invoking a helper). Opcode 0x1002D subcommand 0 reports the reboot reason; 1 forces system reboot; 2 forces assertion; 4 deliberately triggers a null-pointer exception; 5 enters a stack-overflow exception loop; 6 triggers watchdog reset. These are intentional diagnostic/destructive actions.
CUart ACMD handler accepts opcodes 0x10023 and 0x10024; either invokes the UART object's virtual method at slot +0x50 with no additional arguments and returns 0. Other opcodes return 0x0D.
CUart adjustor thunk subtracts 0xA8 from the registered RuntimeObject pointer and enters CUart_AcmdDispatch.
UART configuration maps baud enum at object+0x1c through c0e86c90. Application uses enum 10 -> 921600 baud; data enum 3 -> 8 bits; stop enum 0 -> 1 stop; parity enum 0 -> none.

CUart registers an embedded RuntimeObject at outer offset +0xA8 with target name CUart. Its actual ACMD slot +8 is adjustor thunk c0c7c704, dispatching 0x10023/0x10024. The adjacent outer-vtable function b015d320 is not the registered ACMD handler.
Flash-read analysis: Read one byte at uint32 address and return it. Status ignored; destination is uninitialized on failure.
Flash-read analysis: Preserve prefix before requested erase start in this+0x18 scratch buffer.
Flash-read analysis: Preserve suffix after requested erase end before erasing its containing block.
Flash-read analysis: Absolute flash read after whole-device bounds check. Retry up to 1000 times until positive result, then assert on failure.
