CStorageElement base ctor (CFileDesc-derived). Calls CFileDesc ctor then initializes vtable (ram:0xc0cb4750), cursors +0x220/+0x228/+0x230, capacity +0x238, mode +0x240 and three mutex handles (+0x248, +0x2f0, +0x3a0).

CStorageElement::GetBytesAvailable. read=+0x228, write=+0x230, capacity=+0x238. if read<=write: write-read; else: capacity+write-read. Returns the circular occupancy but clamps neither operand to capacity, so an out-of-range cursor yields a wrong (possibly huge) count.

CStorageElement::Write (vtable slot +0x18). long __thiscall Write(void *src, ulong len).
mode 0 (linear): WriteRaw(this->write_position, src, len); write_position += len. NO capacity check: a stream longer than capacity_238 walks the write cursor past the partition end and keeps programming the next flash region. mode 1 (circular): chunk = min(len, capacity_238 - write_position), wraps. src==0 asserts (prov_stack_chk_fail_report 0x29). A 4th register arg (file offset from CFileDesc::WriteDevice) is ignored here; the ACS uses this->write_position (+0x230).
Reachability of an over-long write: Centcom/HTTP config-body handlers (CCentcom_WriteConfigFileFromHttpBody @ ram:0xb012b358) feed attacker-sized chunks through PWrite -> CFileDesc::WriteDevice -> this function.

CStorageElement::Read (vtable slot 2, overrides CFileDesc::ReadBuffered). Signature: long Read(void *dst, ulong len). Locks mutex_3a0, then dispatches on mode (this+0x240): mode 0 (linear): ReadRaw(this, read_position(+0x228), dst, len); on ret>=0 read_position += ret; no local bounds check -> relies on fm_flash_read's partition size check. mode 1 (circular): loop min(len, capacity_238 - read_position); ReadRaw; advance dst/read_position; wrap read_position to 0 when read_position >= capacity_238. other modes: assert/log then stack_chk_fail abort. Returns total bytes read, or 0 on any ReadRaw error (error is logged, offset left unchanged). NOTE: total is accumulated with 32-bit `addw` (truncates totals >= 2^31). Uses 64-bit unsigned `capacity - read_position`, which underflows if read_position > capacity_238 (see eol).
linear mode: ReadRaw(this, read_position(+0x228), dst, len). No read_position vs capacity check here.
BUG(cosmetic): s2 = (int)ReadRaw_ret + (int)s2 -- 32-bit addw accumulation; a total read >= 2^31 wraps. Not memory-unsafe.
wrap: if read_position < capacity_238 continue, else read_position = 0.

circular: a3 = capacity_238 - read_position (64-bit UNSIGNED). If read_position > capacity_238 this underflows to ~2^64, but the following bgeu then selects len (min), so the (invalid) huge value is not used as a length; fm_flash_read still bounds the offset.
if len < (capacity-read_position) then a3 = len else keep remaining; bgeu is unsigned.

CStorageElement_ACS::SetWritePosition(ulong pos): stores this->write_position (+0x230) with NO validation against capacity_238 or the partition size. Combined with linear-mode Write (no capacity check) this is the origin of an out-of-partition write_position. Callers include CUpdate_ARES (OTA descriptor offset at this+0x2f4), CFlashConfig::ReloadFactoryConfig (0), and Centcom config handlers (0).

FlashPageMergeCallback(scratch, page_off, src, processed, chunk_len): copies chunk_len bytes from src[processed ..] into scratch[page_off ..] and returns non-zero if any 0->1 bit change requires an erase. Bounds: page_off = addr&0xfff, chunk_len = min(0x1000-page_off, remaining), so scratch usage stays within 0x1000 and src usage within len. No overflow found (proven).

CStorageElement_ACS::ReadRaw (ACS vtable slot 14; base returns Stub_ReturnNeg6). long ReadRaw(ulong offset, void *data, int len): tail-calls main_app::fm_flash_read(partition(this+0x3a8), -1, offset, (int)len, data) and returns its result. len is sign-extended 32-bit (`addiw`). fm_flash_read re-validates offset+len against partition->size(+0x10), so out-of-range offsets normally yield -10. Proven by the `jr` tail call.
Flash-read analysis: Tail-call fm_flash_read with this->partition, offset, length and destination; return its byte count/error.

CStorageElement_ACS::Fill (ACS vtable slot 15; base returns Stub_Return0). Fills count(param_4) bytes with value(param_2) one byte per WriteRaw under mutex_2f0. mode 0: WriteRaw(write_position, &byte, 1) until count==0. mode 1 (circular): uVar8 = (capacity_238 != write_position); WriteRaw(write_position,&byte,uVar8); expects return == uVar8; advance/wrap write_position; count -= uVar8. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error. BUG(candidate): if capacity_238 == 0 then uVar8 is always 0, WriteRaw(...,0) returns 0 (ProgramFlashRange returns 0 for len 0), so count never decreases -> infinite loop. Also in mode 1 it never validates write_position < capacity_238.

CStorageElement_ACS::ProgramFlashRange(absolute_flash_addr, len, src, callback). Read-modify-write over 4KB pages starting at addr&~0xfff (c.lui sign-extends, mask is ~0xfff): chunk = min(0x1000 - (addr&0xfff), remaining) fm_flash_read(0,-1, page_base, 0x1000, scratch 0xc0ea7fa0) callback(scratch, addr&0xfff, src, processed, chunk) -> needs-erase? if needs-erase: fm_flash_erase(0,-1, page_base, 0x1000) fm_flash_write(0,-1, page_base, 0x1000, scratch) Serialized by global flash mutex DAT_ram_b0218f50 (asserts on lock failure, lines 0x49/0x51). Returns bytes carried out (negative on error). No bounds bug found in the page/scratch arithmetic. CONFINEMENT: passes flash_src_type=0 to fm_flash_read/write/erase so the per-partition size check (+0x10) is bypassed. For writes, fm_flash_write/erase still call check_flash_area_writeable (ram:0xb00e59e6) against the global partition table, limiting targets to writable regions -- but not necessarily to the caller's own partition. The page read here is NOT range-checked at all.

ProgramFlashRange passes flash_src_type = 0 to fm_flash_read/write/erase, so fm_flash_* SKIP the partition size check (+0x10). Only check_flash_area_writeable (if any) constrains the target; there is no partition confinement here.
Flash-read analysis: Read full aligned 4KB page to shared scratch for callback-based read/modify/erase/write.

CStorageElement_ACS ctor. Builds CStorageElement base with capacity = partition_descriptor->+0x10, stores partition_descriptor at this+0x3a8 and installs the CStorageElement_ACS vtable (ram:0xc0cb47f8). Alloc size 0x3b0.

CPwrClk ACMD dispatcher. Opcode 0x10001 forwards a subtype to the power/clock state routine. Opcode 0x1000E subcommand 0 logs and initiates system reboot; subcommand 1 reports current power state. Other subcommands/opcodes return 0x0D.

CFile::CFile(this, name) [base class of CFile_KVS_ACS]
Calls CFileDesc::CFileDesc (ram:0xc0c807f0) first, then sets the CFile vtable ram:0xc0cb4fd0 (assert string "CFile" at ram:0xc0cb4fb8) and stores name at this+0x220. Confirms CFile : CFileDesc and the 0x228 total object size.

CFileDesc::ReadBuffered (CFileDesc_vtable slot 2; OVERRIDDEN by CStorageElement::Read on storage objects). Returns min(len, valid_len(+0x218) - (offset & 0xffffffff)) bytes copied from buffer(+0x20)+offset, or 0 when offset >= valid_len. Bounds the copy to valid_len (not to the malloc size capacity(+0x18)); correct only if every writer keeps valid_len <= capacity. `this` is not asserted non-null here.

CFileDesc::PRead (slot 9). Positional read: asserts dst!=0 and len!=0, locks mutex at +0x160, resets last_error(+0x210); if flag_a0==0 -> last_error=4; if field_98==2 -> last_error=9; else calls vtable slot 2 (ReadBuffered / or CStorageElement::Read) with offset = param_4, or current position int_a8(+0xa8) when param_4 == -1. Afterwards int_a8 = (int)offset + (int)result (32-bit arithmetic). Returns the slot result.

Reads a file's Stat size into a dynamic byte vector, growing it to the full reported size before the Read call. There is no application-level maximum size. The vector growth path allocates the requested capacity and does not check the allocation result before initializing/copying. If flash-controlled KVS metadata can make Stat report a very large positive size, this can exhaust heap or fault on allocation failure. Confirm backend reachability and metadata size limits before rating as exploitable.

Loads a nontransactional auth-storage value through CAuthStorage_ReadWholeFile, converts the complete byte vector to a string, parses it as JSON, then imports fields. The parser receives the entire flash-reported file size; assess with CAuthStorage_ReadWholeFile's uncapped allocation.

CLogger_CoPro ACMD dispatcher. Opcode 0x10023 calls a logger snapshot/report helper; 0x10024 calls a second logger helper; 0x1000D iterates a table of sender/core/port/write counters and emits usage-memory-test logs.

Security review: opcode 0x1000D / selector 0x19 treats param_4 as an iteration count with no upper bound. The loop is `for (uVar3 = 1; uVar3 <= param_4; uVar3++)`; at UINT64_MAX it wraps and never terminates, and large values cause prolonged log/CPU exhaustion. Shell numeric parsing accepts unsigned 64-bit values, so this is potentially command-triggerable if the ACMD console is reachable. Availability issue; no memory corruption observed in this path.

CNtpClient ACMD dispatcher. Opcode 0x10001 forwards to the NTP state/query routine. Opcode 0x10011 subcommands 0..6 create/start or stop the NTP request, request synchronization, log time source/current time, reset sync counter, and set system time from supplied fields. Unrecognized subcommands log and return 0x0D.

Copies the top-level Wi-Fi profile and its four 0x1b-byte subprofiles. It bounds the primary SSID and primary credential lengths, but does not validate each subprofile's length byte before copying the slots. CWifi_BuildStaConfigFromStoredAndConnect later uses those subprofile lengths as memcpy sizes.

Loads named KVS property WifiCred_config_0 into a zeroed 0xb4-byte destination and only increments the credential-slot count if kvs_read_named_property returns exactly 0xb4. The named-property decoder inherits the KVS record integrity/authentication caveats recorded at Flash_ReadFileDecode; static xrefs show no callers for this function in the current program.

Flash-controlled credential length overflow: for security mode 1, the selected key length comes from the stored profile slot length and is passed to memcpy into WifiHal_SelectedCredentialBuffer at ram:c0e8d5c2. The preceding 0x40-byte clear covers ram:c0e8d5c0..d5ff, leaving only 62 bytes from the copy start. A length of 64 overwrites adjacent globals including WifiHal_SSIDLength at d601 and later credential lengths overwrite SSID/BSSID state. The join task consumes the modified globals before the caller checks its stack canary. Its downstream connect helper FUN_ram_c0c89f9c rejects SSID lengths outside 1..32, so downstream code execution is not established; the fixed global overwrite remains confirmed.

Join task consumes WifiHal_SSIDLength, WifiHal_SSIDBuffer, BSSID, security mode, and selected credential state populated by CWifiHal_StartConnectAP. A stored-profile credential copy can overwrite these globals before this task is launched. The selected SSID length then reaches FUN_ram_c0c89f9c, which rejects lengths outside 1..32; assess other state corruption separately.

Security review: copies the scan-record byte at src+0x20 directly as the memcpy length into each 0x34-byte output record, without enforcing the 802.11 SSID maximum (32) or the record/buffer capacity. The same length is stored in the result record. If the upstream scan callback can provide an oversized length, records overlap and the final entry can overrun the 0x824-byte caller buffer.

Reachable post-boot flash-profile stack overwrite: wifi_control_dispatch -> CWifi_MapControlCommand -> CWifi_DispatchStoredConfigOp case 0x18 -> CWifi_LoadStoredConfigAndProfile -> CWifi_LoadStoredProfileFromKvs reads attacker-controlled WifiCred.profile bytes into 0xc0e8d780. In security case 1, four profile length bytes at offsets 0x7c/0x97/0xb2/0xcd drive memcpy to the stack configuration at offsets 0x2c, 0x47, 0x62, and 0x7d with no 0x1a-byte bound. CWifi_ConnectUsingStoredConfig and reconnect events feed this configuration to CWifi_ConnectSTA before this function checks its stack canary. The stack frame places canary at sp+0xf8 and saved return at sp+0x138; determine whether in-frame structure corruption is exploitable beyond crash. Raw wifi control command 14 maps to internal operation 0x18 through WifiControlCommandMap.
App console command descriptor table: 19 {name, description} pointer pairs, searched by CShell_DispatchCommand; table order is the command ID passed to CShell_CommandHandler.

nanopb pb_field_t list for the credential body submessage (reached from the id==0xc request via c0ca0ef0 tag2). Two length-prefixed BYTES fields: tag1 BYTES data_size=0x12 (18) -> max payload 16 == BleProvRequest::creds tag2 BYTES data_size=0x0e (14) -> max payload 12 == BleProvRequest::secret Pb_DecodeField (ram:0xb01b8d5c) stores the u16 length at the field data_offset and rejects (len+2 > data_size) with "bytes_overflow", so credsLen<=16 and secretLen<=12. These maxima exactly tile the 0x1e-byte stack serialization buffer in BleProv_HandleReq0C_CredsMsg (2 + 16 + 12 = 0x1e), i.e. the copies cannot reach the canary at sp+0x28.

nanopb pb_field_t list for request id/tag 0xc (credential provisioning body, 0x24 bytes): tag1 varint (1 byte) == BleProvRequest::subcmd / credsType selector tag2 submessage -> c0ca0eb0 == { creds BYTES[max16]; secret BYTES[max12] } Referenced from c0ca1554 (the dispatcher wrapper schema).
CAdaptiveIRLed ACMD interface vtable. Its slot +8 points to adjustor thunk c0c5d0fc, which subtracts 0x10 and dispatches at c0c5d0d2.
CSettingsParser_NonSAX registered interface vtable. Its slot +8 is b00df5fe, the generic unsupported-command method (returns 0x0D); parser behavior is through its other methods.
CFileDesc interface (inherited from CFileDesc_vtable slot 0); stub on base CStorageElement

CStorageElement_vtable (16 slots). Slots 0-12 = CFileDesc interface layout (0 Reset,1 Open,2 ReadBuffered->overridden by CStorageElement::Read,3 WriteBuffered->overridden by CStorageElement::Write,4 WriteDevice,5 dtor,6 deleting_dtor,7 Seek,8 Close,9 PRead,10 PWrite, 11 GetLastError,12 NoOp). Slots 13-15 are the storage-element extensions: 13 WriteRaw, 14 ReadRaw, 15 Fill (base stubs return Neg6/Neg6/0). Mirrors exist (d0..).
CFileDesc interface (inherited); stub on ACS

CStorageElement_ACS_vtable (16 slots). Same layout as CStorageElement_vtable: slots 0-12 = inherited CFileDesc interface (slots 2/3 overridden by CStorageElement::Read/Write, slot 4 shared WriteDevice), slots 5/6 ACS dtors. Slots 13-15 = storage overrides: 13 WriteRaw, 14 ReadRaw, 15 Fill -- all talk to fm_flash_*/ProgramFlashRange. Mirrors exist (d0..).

Outbound ATT send. Bounds param_3 (len) against the negotiated MTU at conn+0x14: returns 0xd if len > MTU. opcode 0x23 path validates the multi-packet payload with BLE_l2cap_validate_multi_write. Good bound.

Walks a [u16 tag][u16 len][data] sequence; rejects if fewer than 5 bytes remain or if the declared len exceeds the remaining bytes (returns 0xd). Bounds-checked; called from BLE_send_att_data for opcode 0x23. Renamed from FUN_unk_type_65__c001082f0.

ATT MTU request handler. Clamps the peer-requested MTU to [0x17, peer_mtu] (peer_mtu from BLE_conn_get_peer_mtu) then writes the 2-byte result into a fixed 0x44-byte HCI tx buffer (BLE_att_get_tx_buffer, size class 0x15) at payload+0x24+0x26. Length is clamped, so not an attacker-length copy.

GATT/ATT request dispatcher (CYBT/WICED-style). p_data (ble_att_req_t @ DAT_unk_type_65__c0011cf30): +0 conn_id, +4 opcode, +8 handle, +10 offset, +12 len, +16 value ptr. Opcode map: 0x12 WRITE_REQ / 0x52 WRITE_CMD / 0x16 PREPARE_WRITE -> app write cb _DAT_ram_c0011cee0(conn,0,p,handle,offset,len,resp,auth,value); 0x18 EXECUTE_WRITE -> _DAT_ram_c0011cee8; 0x0A READ -> _DAT_ram_c0011ced8; 0x1E CONF -> _DAT_ram_c0011cef8; 0x02 MTU -> _DAT_ram_c0011cf08 + BLE_att_handle_mtu_req. NO length/bounds validation here: parsed ATT len and value pointer are forwarded verbatim to the app callback. Control-flow target: indirect slots c0011cee0/c0011cee8/c0011ced8/c0011cef8/c0011cf08 (inferred - heap corruption of these gives direct call).

GATT server event callback, registered via FUN_unk_type_65__c00114fc2 -> FUN_unk_type_65__c00108730 (stored at stack_ctx+0x10 -> +0x28). Dispatch: event 4 -> BLE_prvGattsReqCb; connect/disconnect -> _DAT_ram_c0011ce90; event 5 checks _DAT_ram_c0011ce90 != 0 but then calls _DAT_ram_c0011cf00 (NULL-call candidate if cf00 unset while ce90 set); event 7 -> (*(code*)p_data[1])(p_data[0]) - function pointer read from event data. No peer-controlled bounds in this layer.

FUNCTION.NAME: video_coded::encode_one_frame

FUNCTION.NAME: video_coded::avp_queue_push_desc

FUNCTION.NAME: video_coded::avc_stream_params_load
video_coded::avc_stream_frame_cmd
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: avc_stream.c:0x313: execute one 0x48-byte host frame command: luma/chroma ptrs -> 0x700d9408/0x700d940c; update bits in cmd[5]: 0x80=bitrate chg (rc_set_bitrate), 0x10=GOP chg + rc_set_framerate, 0x02/0x01=qp max/min, 0x08=force IDR (ctx+0x74), 0x04=force key (ctx+0x78), 0x40=rc restart (rc_enable, assert if already on), 0x20=flush; then enc_cmd_reg_write_wait, host_sync_barrier(0..3), rc_frame_qp, build full register image, encode_one_frame, enc_status_read, rc_post_frame -> ctx+0x79 needs-more-frames flag; rc_disable on flush.

FUNCTION.NAME: video_coded::slice_header_write
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Slice header (NAL 5/1): first_mb=0, slice_type=nal flags>>6, pps_id ctx+0x8b, frame_num 6b ctx+0x9d, idr_pic_id ctx+0x9f (type 5), poc_lsb 6b ctx+0x9e, qp_delta se(param_4+3 - +2), deblock idc/alpha/beta offsets, slice-QP rewind via bw checkpoints (bw_pos_restore).

FUNCTION.NAME: video_coded::sps_write
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: SPS NAL (avc_nal.c): profile ctx+0x7c (High=100 adds 0x2c constraint byte), pic_width/height_in_mbs_minus1 from ctx+0x30/0x31, crop = MB*16 - ctx+0x2c/0x2e, VUI timing_info (0x3011) num_units_in_tick=ctx+0x94 / time_scale=ctx+0x90 (32b); assert if HRD flag ctx+0x98 set.

FUNCTION.NAME: video_coded::pps_write
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: PPS NAL: pps/sps ids ctx+0x8b/0x8a, deblock_control_present regimage+0x2c, init_qp se(pic_init_qp-26) regimage+0x02, chroma_qp_offset regimage+0x2e, constrained_intra +0x2d, High-profile extra chroma offset.

FUNCTION.NAME: video_coded::enc_cmd_reg_write_wait
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: 0x700b0c90 = (p4&1)<<17 | (p1&1)<<16 | (p3&0xff)<<8 | (p2&0xff) (go bit16 + MB dims); spin until enc_done_flag set by SPE IRQ, then clear it.

FUNCTION.NAME: video_coded::avp_output_desc_submit

FUNCTION.NAME: video_coded::avp_wait_status_release

FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: audio_dsp::Opus_PacketParseImpl. Mostly bounded: frame count from param_1[1]&0x3f (<=63) and total samples/frame checked <= 0x1680. It writes up to that many shorts into caller-supplied param_6. Safety therefore depends on the caller sizing param_6 for the max frame count; no internal OOB observed. FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::heap_5_ext_pvPortMalloc
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: FreeRTOS heap_5_ext region allocator (read-only context). Block header = 0x10 bytes: [0]=next free ptr XOR'd with global cookie DAT_ram_b021f788 (safe-linking); [8]=u32 block size (incl 0x10 header). User ptr = block+0x10. Request size is rounded up: total = req+0x10, then if (req&0xf) total=(total&~0xf)+0x10; i.e. usable = total-0x10 >= req. For malloc(0x138): total=0x150, user usable 0x140. Consequence: an OOB write past a 0x138 buffer must exceed offset 0x140 (from user ptr) to hit the next block's size/next fields; the free-list next pointer is XOR-encoded so it cannot be forged without the global cookie (not BLE-leakable).

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::Platform_CreateAndSetBootMode
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Derives application boot_mode boolean from validated FWBL unlock-mode handoff, not reset reason. Reads selector 0x1018 (4 bits at bit offset 24) from 0x90000f24. Successful read with unlock mode !=4 => boot_mode=0; read failure or mode 4 => boot_mode=1. FWBL restricted command setup publishes 4; authenticated debug setup publishes mapped unlock modes 0..3. Application console creation requires boot_mode==0 OR fqc_main byte0 !=0.

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::AudioCore_AcmdDispatch
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: AudioCore ACMD dispatcher. Opcodes 0x10022 and 0x10025 invoke two audio-core operations unless the busy/state byte at +0x6C1 is set; 0x10023/0x10024 are successful no-ops. Opcode 0x10089 reads/sets one of 12 audio feature flags (selector 0xFF snapshots the full 12-byte block) and notifies a listener. Opcode 0x1008F clamps a scalar to 0x1F and forwards it to an audio component. Unsupported inputs return 0x0D.

FUNCTION.NAME: CPfmHdkMarsRed::InitLocalSetupNetwork
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Application serial shell is constructed iff boot_mode == 0 OR fqc_mode_enabled != 0. FQC flag is loaded from byte 0 of fqc_main in InitStorage. Creates CShell and CConsole_MARS over serial_channel/UART0. Console listener greets Hola!, prompts rfw>, submits lines on CR (0x0d). No '=' entry sequence in this path.

FUNCTION.NAME: CPfmHdkMarsRed::InitStorage
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: InitStorage reads fqc_main[0] into fqc_mode_enabled. When nonzero it also calls NotifySetEnabled(field2043_0xac0, 1), which ultimately sets 0c_networking::NotifyOutputEnabled at 0xB0200C40. Clearing the byte therefore suppresses app notification/log output as well as bypassing the FQC credential override. This is a logger/notification gate; it is distinct from RingUart_AdoptIfMuxed and RingUart_PutChar, which are the payload's direct UART path.

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::kvs_list_keys

No GCM authentication is performed on listing path. No static callers, thunks, or literal entry-address bytes found; syntactic scan of 38,525,264 initialized executable bytes also found no common direct/address-forming reference. Reachability and secure-boot bypass are NOT established.

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::check_flash_area_writeable
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT:
check_flash_area_writeable(fm, partition, addr, len): the ONLY write confinement.
- partition valid: allow iff ((*(u32*)(partition+0x18) >> 1) & 3) == 3. - partition == 0 (ProgramFlashRange path): iterate the global table (fm+0x30, count byte fm+0x38, stride 0x1c). For each entry: if addr < size(+0x10)+base(+0x14) then (a) if addr+len <= base -> no overlap, accept; (b) else overlap -> reject only when type != 3. addr past every partition -> accept.
NO-OP IN THIS BUILD (proven): the table at ram:0xb01f59b8 (gp=0xb01f5f00, 20 entries) has field_18 == 0x06 or 0x07 for EVERY entry, so ((field>>1)&3) == 3 (writable) for all. The function therefore never returns false on the global path, and gaps outside all partitions are accepted too. Note also the overlap test uses a 32-bit add (int)addr+(int)len which can wrap, and fm_flash_write later truncates addr with c.addiw (sign-extend low 32 bits).

Insertion-sorts the table by the +0x14 field (base offset) using prov_memcpy 0x1c-byte swaps, then stamps each entry's +0x19 byte with the instance index (g_fm_num). Instance[0] lives at g_fm_instances (ram:b0203670, stride 0x58): +0x00 handle, +0x08 param2, +0x20 iot_flash_open result, +0x28 iot_flash_getinfo result, +0x30 table ptr, +0x38 count, +0x40 malloc(0x78), +0x50=5. Asserts gfm_num < FM_FLASH_INSTANCE_NUM (ram:b01cbe28).

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::fm_flash_read
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Public partition read (retries on BUSY). a0=FlashPartition* p (or 0), a2=src_addr (partition-relative), a3=len, a4=dst. if p: if (*(u32*)(p+0x10) < (len & 0xffffffff) + src_addr) return -10; src_addr += *(u32*)(p+0x14); then iot_flash_read(primary_handle, (long)(int)src_addr, dst, len & 0xffffffff). BUG CANDIDATES: (1) src_addr is checked as a full 64-bit add but truncated to 32-bit SIGNED for the transfer (c.addiw s1,0 @ b00e5e9a) -> base/offset >= 0x100000000 aliases to low 32 bits, base in [0x80000000,0xffffffff] is rejected by iot_flash_read; (2) p==0 skips the partition-local bound entirely. Global bound is still enforced by iot_flash_read against g_spi_flash_size, so this is a partition-isolation/truncation issue, not a raw OOB. Proven offsets; exploitability inferred.
FUNCTION.TYPEINFO_CMT: undefined __stdcall fm_flash_read(undefined8 flash_src_type, ulonglong unused_maybe, undefined8 src_addr, undefined8 len, byte * dst)

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::fm_flash_write
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT:
fm_flash_write(partition, unused, flash_location, len, data) -> flash_partition_write.
If partition != 0: reject when *(u32*)(partition+0x10) < (len&0xffffffff)+flash_location, then flash_location += *(u32*)(partition+0x14). Then check_flash_area_writeable(fm, partition, flash_location, len).
BYPASS: ProgramFlashRange always passes partition=0, so the per-partition size check (+0x10) is skipped entirely; only the (no-op) global check remains. flash_location is then truncated with (long)(int) before flash_partition_write.

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::CCentcom_CopyFileContents
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Copies file contents between CFile_KVS_ACS-compatible objects through CCentcom_Rdk's 0x8FC-byte scratch buffer at +0x2C0. Queries source size (slot +0x68), opens source in mode 1 and destination in mode 0x14, then copies chunks capped at 0x8FC via source Read (+0x48) and destination Write (+0x50). Used for ring-config backup/restore: primary -> backup before config replacement, and backup -> primary when restoring. Source-size or open failures call RFW_AssertAndHalt and do not continue, so the stack size output is not consumed on a failed size query. A zero-byte read or short destination write is logged and exits the copy loop; both files are then closed, but the function does not propagate that partial-copy failure to its callers. If either close fails, the outer loop reaches the fatal assertion helper. No chunk can exceed the 0x8FC-byte scratch buffer based on the requested size.

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::CCentcom_WriteConfigFileFromHttpBody

CCentcom_WriteConfigFileFromHttpBody(this): network-reachable config write.
open(this+0x2a8, mode 2) -> SetWritePosition(this+0x2a8, 0) -> loop { n = CSerializer_ParseHttpBody(serializer, buf, 0x8fc); if (n==0) break; PWrite(this+0x2a8, buf, n, -1); // vtable +0x50 if (PRead error) ... } then SetWritePosition(0) and writes an 8-byte "moel"+len trailer.

CStorageElement::Write has NO capacity check, so an HTTP body larger than the target partition overflows write_position into the next flash partition (confinement is only the no-op check_flash_area_writeable). FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::CSframeE2ee_Decrypt
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT:
CSframeE2ee_Decrypt(e2ee, data, len, &outLen) - inbound E2EE entry for audio media frames.
Order of operations: *outLen>=len; len!=0; data!=NULL; (data&0x3f)==0; len<=0x140 ELSE prov_stack_chk_fail_report(0x14a) NORETURN; lock e2ee->0x210; require key-installed flag *(e2ee+0xf48); prov_memcpy(DAT_ram_b0217940, data, len); SFrame_Decrypt(e2ee+0x908, DAT_ram_b0217940, len, data, &outLen); unlock; *outLen updated.
NOTE: CMediaStreamAudio_HandleFrame (b018e13e) calls this ONLY AFTER it already did prov_memcpy(DAT_ram_b021b480, frame, len) with no bound. Any len that overflows that 0x2b2 buffer (>0x2b2) is also >0x140 and therefore triggers the noreturn abort above immediately after the copy. => bounded BSS corruption followed by a guaranteed halt (DoS), not code exec. The ABI-visible check is len<=0x140; staging copy is therefore always in-bounds (0x141 buffer).

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::CSocket_Mbed_ServerTlsSetup
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Setup HTTPS server TLS: mbedtls_ssl_conf_authmode(cfg, 0) == MBEDTLS_SSL_VERIFY_NONE. No client certificate / mutual auth on the local setup channel.

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::CSocket_Mbed_LoadEmbeddedCA

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::CLedSpinner_AcmdDispatch

FUNCTION.NAME: CFlashConfig::GetConfigField
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: INFOLEAK ASSESSMENT (CFlashConfig::GetConfigField 4-byte heap OOB read): BUG PROVEN: this->cfg_fields(+0x118) = pvPortMalloc(0xc) but GetConfigField always reads 8 bytes at +(idx-0x40); idx=0x48 (used by the ctor itself) reads 4 bytes past the block. EGRESS: the over-read dword lands in the caller's local and is consumed only as a flash read length / base offset (FUN_ram_b01568da / FUN_ram_b015725c), never returned to the attacker. No egress. CANARY: unreachable — heap-adjacent bytes, not the .data canary at b0297260.

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::CFlashConfig_LoadRingConfigJson
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Parses flash-backed RingConfig JSON in chunks of at most 0x41 bytes into a 0x578-byte serializer buffer. Chunk capacity is adequate. The loop subtracts the storage Read result from remaining length without checking for zero, so a truncated payload can cause a non-progressing loop.

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::CRingConfig_BuildFromNvs
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CRingConfig_BuildFromNvs(this, storage): builds the RingConfig tree from factory NVS. Calls FUN_b0162bd2(fixed_key, "", 0) ~58x to append key nodes into the global CTree builder (DAT_b0220088), then FUN_b0162e84/FUN_b0162c70 to nest the ledpattern/streaming groups, then FUN_b01636a4(CConfig,"RingConfig",tree,0) and stores it at this->ring_config (+0x120). NOTE: the NVS values here are the constant empty string DAT_b01edec0; the key list is static. No flash-controlled length is used to size a local buffer in this function. BuildFromNvs is not itself a memory-safety bug; the untrusted flash bytes go through CSerializer_JSON (capacity-checked, see CFlashConfig/CSerializer). Also installs this->ring_config and calls FUN_b015695c(this, ringconfig, this->storage_element2) to parse flash JSON. Proven.

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::FUN_ram_b0157338
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CFlashConfig::ReloadFactoryConfig: cfg_fields = pvPortMalloc(0xc) is filled with 12 flash bytes. GetConfigField(this,0x44,&local_20) reads offsets 4..11 (ok, must == 0x4c); GetConfigField(this,0x48,&lStack_18) reads offsets 8..15 -> 4 bytes of heap OOB read past the 12-byte block (see CFlashConfig::GetConfigField). The over-read high dword pollutes lStack_18, which is then used as the byte count for FUN_ram_b01568da (flash read in 0x41-byte chunks into factory_buf[0x41]) and as the base offset in FUN_ram_b015725c (b01572c6: *param_2 = *param_3 + 0x4c). Chunking keeps the destination bounded, so this is an OOB READ / read-length influence bug, not a write-overflow primitive, unless the storage-element vtable+0x50 consumer copies more than the chunk.

FUNCTION.NAME: CFlashConfig::CFlashConfig
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CFlashConfig ctor (caller allocates 0x130 bytes). Layout proven from disasm: +0x00 vtable=&CFlashConfig_vtable (ram:b01e1d10) +0x08 storage_element (param_2, CStorageElement_ACS*) +0x10 char factory_buf[0x41] (scratch for raw flash/NVS reads) +0x58 lock (passed to FUN_b00cd3c0(4,...) and scope-locked by FUN_b01015bc/FUN_b00dfd6a) +0x100 field_100 (FUN_b00cd3c0 result) +0x108 storage_element2 (param_3, used for factory NVS reads) +0x110 loaded flag +0x118 cfg_fields = malloc(0xc) (12 x 8-byte fields, indices 0x40..0x4b) +0x120 ring_config (CRingConfig*, malloc(0x28)) +0x128 json_serializer (CSerializer_JSON*, malloc(0xf0); base CSerializer allocs a 0x578 data buffer, capacity stored at CSerializer+0x20) Asserts s_CFlashConfig (ram:b01e1bc0). FUNCTION.NAME: CTimeTrig_AcmdDispatch
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CTimeTrig ACMD dispatcher. Opcode 0x10003 validates a non-null event record and compares its event ID/type with the supplied value; opcode 0x10004 processes timer/event state (including next-deadline updates, expiry/repeat handling, and trigger-state notification). Opcode 0x10023 calls the global time-trigger scheduling helper; opcode 0x10024 calls a second schedule/update helper; opcode 0x1002A invokes the per-object scheduling helper. Unsupported commands return 0x0D; malformed required event pointers trigger the stack-check failure path.

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::CFile_KVS_makeClusterName

main_app::CFile_KVS_makeClusterName(name, uint cluster, char ctx[0x30]) -> bool
Zero-fills ctx then formats "%s%c%hx" (name, '#', cluster). Returns false if the formatted length would reach 0x30 (=> "Filename too big"). The %hx format truncates the cluster index to 16 bits.

FUNCTION.NAME: CFile_KVS_ACS::CFile_KVS_ACS
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT:
CFile_KVS_ACS::CFile_KVS_ACS (ctor)
Class: CFile_KVS_ACS (name string ram:0xb01e3240, vtable ram:0xb01e3420). Allocation: callers malloc(0x228). FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::CFile_KVS_getValueSize
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Reads cluster 0 and returns the flash-controlled signed 32-bit logical value length from header offset +4 after checking KVS magic and Flash_ReadFileDecode status. It applies no upper bound to positive lengths. CFile_KVS_ACS::Stat preserves this value; readers that allocate by Stat size must impose their own cap.

FUNCTION.NAME: CFile_KVS_ACS::Stat
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT:
CFile_KVS_ACS::Stat(this, int out[3]) [vtable slot 13]
Fills out[0]=size (signed 32-bit from header, ram:b015be2e), out[1]=(size+0x207)&0xfffffe00 (rounded cluster bytes), out[2]=(short)this->field_98 (0x98). If getValueSize<0, zeroes the 12-byte output. Asserts out != 0 (0x117).
BUG B4 (inferred, integer overflow): (int)size + 0x207 at ram:b015be34 can overflow int32 when the on-flash size is near 0x7fffffff.

FUNCTION.NAME: CFile_KVS_ACS::ReadInternal
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT:
CFile_KVS_ACS::ReadInternal(this, dst, len, offset)
On-flash KVS read primitive (called by ::Read). * locks (FUN_b01015bc), size = CFile_KVS_getValueSize(this->name). * rejects if size<0 or offset >= (unsigned)size [ram:b015c0ee-b015c0f4] * file byte offset = (int)(offset + 8) [ram:b015c116, 32-bit addiw] * cluster index = (fileoff >> 9) & 0xffff, in-cluster = fileoff & 0x1ff * per cluster: makeClusterName -> Flash_ReadFileDecode(handle,ctx,buf,0x200) then copies min(len - copied, bytes-to-end-of-cluster) into dst.
BUGS (see plate on ram:b015c0ee / b015c116): B1 missing bound: only offset<size is checked, never offset+len<=size, and len is not clamped to size-offset. Reading past a record's length walks into later clusters (other records / stale data) => over-read. B2 32-bit signed overflow: offset+8 at ram:b015c116 (addiw) can wrap for large on-flash size (>=0x7ffffff8), yielding negative file offset. B3 cluster index is truncated to 16 bits (ram:b015c118-b015c11e), and makeClusterName formats it with %hx => aliasing for >64K clusters.

FUNCTION.NAME: CFile_KVS_ACS::Read
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT:
CFile_KVS_ACS::Read (vtable slot 2, overrides CFileDesc::ReadBuffered)
Signature (RISC-V ABI): Read(CFile_KVS_ACS *this, void *dst, ulong len, ulong offset) a0=this, a1=dst, a2=len, a3=offset (the 4th arg is forwarded to CFile_KVS_ACS::ReadInternal; it is NOT stale). Zeroes this->last_error (0x210); if dst==0 or len==0 sets last_error=5 and returns 0; otherwise tail-jumps to ReadInternal.
NOTE vs base: CFileDesc::ReadBuffered clamps len to valid_len(0x218)-offset; this override does not (see ReadInternal bug notes).

FUNCTION.NAME: CFile_KVS_ACS::WriteInternal
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT:
CFile_KVS_ACS::WriteInternal(this, void *src, ulong len, int offset): writes `len` bytes of a KVS value starting at logical byte offset `offset` (a3; CFile_KVS_ACS::Write tail-jumps here passing the caller's a3 through). It splits the value into 0x200-byte clusters named "%s#%hx" where cluster = (offset+8)>>9, TRUNCATED to 16 bits by %hx, and calls Flash_WriteFileEncode per cluster.
The flash address is derived from the cluster NAME, not from `offset`, so a huge offset does not directly index flash; the practical risk is cluster-name aliasing / writing beyond the value's declared size (CFile_KVS_getValueSize is fetched but not enforced). This is NOT the strongest raw-address primitive — see CStorageElement_ACS::WriteRaw.

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::CSerializer_ReadHttpBody
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CSerializer_ReadHttpBody (AddData, serializer vtable slot +0xd8): appends a chunk (param_2, length param_3) byte-by-byte into this+0x80, bounded by this+0x88 < this+0x20 (capacity). Asserts (this+0x20 < param_3). The JSON callback then parses incrementally. FUNCTION.NAME: CTree::InsertKeyStr
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CTree::InsertKeyStr(name, value, type): appends one 0x18-byte CTreeNode at DAT_b0220088 + count*0x18 (count=DAT_b0220082) with NO capacity check, then pushes `count` at index slot DAT_b0220078 + DAT_b0220080*4 while DAT_b0220080 decrements. The 0xfffe underflow guard fires only AFTER the slot store. Node fields: +0x00 name, +0x08 value, +0x10 type/value_len, +0x12 order=0xffff, +0x14/0x15 flags=0, +0x16/0x17=0. UNBOUNDED-INSERT BUG (proven arithmetic, latent): a caller inserting more than `capacity` nodes overruns the node region into/past the contiguous index stack and ultimately the FreeRTOS heap block. Audited callers (BuildFromNvs, CSetupMethodWifi, CEventReporter, CFastpingTest, CEgressTest, CRingNM, CHttpServer, CHttpClient, RssCmd, token/JSON-RPC serializers) all size capacity to the exact node count; no attacker-derived count was found, so it is not reachable as of this audit.

FUNCTION.NAME: CTree::InsertGroup
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CTree::InsertGroup(name, flags): same unbounded append path as InsertKeyStr; zeroes the value and stores `flags` at CTreeNode+0x14. Consumes one node slot and one index slot. Used for group/parent nodes.

FUNCTION.NAME: CTree::InsertSchemaKey
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CTree::InsertSchemaKey(name, type_word): same unbounded append path; zeroes the value and stores type_word at CTreeNode+0x14. Builds schema-only leaves (no value). One node + one index slot.

FUNCTION.NAME: CTree::CloneNode
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CTree::CloneNode(src): appends a new CTreeNode copying src->name/src->value/src->type, using the same unbounded node-index path as InsertKeyStr, and pushes its index. Returns the new node. Used by CTree::RepeatGroup. LATENT unbounded-insert bug; node growth is members*(repeat-1).

FUNCTION.NAME: CTree::PushChildCount
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CTree::PushChildCount(neg_count): pushes -neg_count into the index stack (group marker for the preceding neg_count nodes). No node is allocated; consumes one index-stack slot without a capacity check. Guard 0xfffe after store.

FUNCTION.NAME: CTree::RepeatGroup
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CTree::RepeatGroup(group_marker_handle, repeat): repeats the preceding child group (repeat-1) extra times by cloning each member node and re-pushing its marker; node growth = members*(repeat-1). No capacity check. Callers must size BeginBuild capacity for the multiplied node count; e.g. 0c_networking::FUN_c0c63f5e passes repeat=10 with capacity S+3+6*10 (over-allocates, safe). repeat<1 -> assert.

FUNCTION.NAME: CTree::InsertChecksumArray
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CTree::InsertChecksumArray(prefix, n, shorts): for n in [1,1000) inserts n named nodes (prefix+checksum, value from shorts[n]) and pushes the -n child marker. n==0 or n>=1000 -> assert. Used by RssCmd_BuildJsonRequest with n == the table-entry byte field; BeginBuild(n,1) is an exact fit. Proven.

FUNCTION.NAME: CTree::InsertStringArray
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CTree::InsertStringArray(char** vec, n): inserts n key nodes (one per vec entry) then pushes the -n child marker; consumes n node slots + n+1 index slots. n==0 -> assert. Unbounded; used by CHttpClient ctor (BeginBuild(8,1), n=8 exact) and 0c_networking::FUN_c0c62d6a (BeginBuild(N+1,2), n=N exact).

FUNCTION.NAME: CTree::BeginBuild
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CTree global builder allocator: BeginBuild(node_capacity, extra_index_slots). Allocates (extra + capacity*7)*4 bytes = capacity*0x18 node region + (capacity+extra)*4 index stack. Globals: DAT_b0220088=node base; DAT_b0220078=base+capacity*0x18 (index stack top); DAT_b0220080=capacity+extra-1 (index cursor, ushort, decrements); DAT_b0220082=0 (node count, ushort). capacity==0 -> assert/halt. PROVEN: node region holds exactly `capacity` 0x18-byte CTreeNode slots; index stack holds capacity+extra 4-byte signed entries (negative value = child-count marker). No capacity check exists in the Insert* family, so every caller MUST pass capacity == number of inserted nodes.

FUNCTION.NAME: CTree::ClearValues
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CTree::ClearValues(node): walks a materialized CTree's node list (count at node[idx+0x18]-2) and releases each node's value object via vtable+0x18, clearing node+0x08/+0x10. No writes outside the materialized CTree; not related to the builder overflow.

FUNCTION.NAME: CTree::Materialize
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CTree::Materialize(dst, root_name, tree_handle, external_src): converts the global builder arena into a permanent CTree object (size 0x28). Allocates depth*2 + (count+1)*0x18 and deep-copies the `count` nodes (DAT_b0220082), allocating value objects via FUN_b01619a6 and vtable +0x28/+0x30, then frees the arena and clears the builder globals. Reads DAT_b0220082 directly, so an over-count from the unbounded insert would also drive this copy out of bounds. CTree layout: +0x00 node_array, +0x08 value_alloc, +0x10 nodes_copy, +0x18 index_table, +0x20 depth, +0x21 owns_nodes.

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::CTree_SetExistingValueByKey
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CTree helper: find an existing entry by key and replace its value. The actual entry writer reallocates when the replacement string exceeds the current storage capacity; this helper does not impose a key-specific value-length cap.

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::FUN_ram_b01655ac
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: During Wi-Fi/network initialization, reads three OTP rows 0x36B..0x36D (six bytes) through the app OTP accessor and passes the bytes to a networking helper if nonzero. This looks like a provisioned network identity/MAC, but the callee semantics are unresolved.

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::bundle_load_element_to_addr
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: main_app::bundle_load_element_to_addr(type, dst). Reads bundle element `type` from flash into dst. PROVEN: header comes from Peripherals::SYSCTL.BUND_HDR @0x90000000; offset/size = BUND_HDR_ELEMENT0_FILE_OFF/SIZE[idx]. flash_xip_read_to_ram(file_off+0x200+slot_base, dst, size). Then SHA-256(data) is compared to the 0x20-byte digest at 0x9000022c+idx*0x34; on mismatch dst is zeroed and error returned. NOTE: the flash read into dst happens BEFORE the hash check, so an oversized (authenticated) size would overflow dst transiently, then be zeroed. bundle_hdr_install copies the 0xd20-byte header from the authenticated/decrypted SBIH image (sbih_auth_and_decrypt_G), so size+digest are authenticated under secure boot.

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::flash_read
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: flash_read(offset,dst,len) -> flash_xip_read_to_ram(offset & 0xffffffff, dst, len, 0). No bound check here and len is NOT masked to 32 bits. The only guard is the (offset+len) <= chip->size 64-bit add inside flash_xip_read_to_ram, which wraps for huge/negative len. In practice the only caller (FUN_b016845a) uses a constant 0x10.

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::otp_read_row_checked_app
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Checked app OTP row accessor: requires initialized handle and output pointer, rejects row indices >= 0x400, then delegates to otp_read_row_app. COtp_Mars_ReadBits uses this to read rows and extract requested bitfields.

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::crypt_LoadPublicKey
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: main_app::crypt_LoadPublicKey(pk_ctx, keybuf, keylen) == mbedtls pubkey parse Attacker fully controls (keybuf,keylen) (flash-resident bundle key). Requires keybuf[keylen-1]==0 to take the PEM path (mbedtls_pem_read_buffer needs a NUL-terminated buffer; the NUL is checked before strstr -> no over-read if the caller's buffer is exactly keylen and last byte is 0 -- the caller even mallocs exactly keylen, so keybuf[keylen-1] is in bounds). Non-NUL-terminated -> treated as DER via mbedtls_x509_get_pubkey with an explicit end pointer keybuf+keylen. ASN.1 lengths are bounds-checked against that end pointer. No length-prefix used as a copy/alloc size without an end check found. NOTE: caller must still provide 1 spare NUL byte; only keylen bytes are allocated, so a PEM blob lacking an internal NUL is still parsed as DER (bounded).

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::x509_crt_parse_der_core
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: x509_crt_parse_der_core(crt, buf, len, alloc_mode, ext_cb, ext_ctx). This is the standard mbedtls DER certificate parser (own_buffer path copies the raw cert with prov_memcpy(...,raw_len) into a buffer allocated via thunk_FUN_ram_b00c4436(1,<size>)). All ASN.1 field reads go through mbedtls_asn1_get_tag/get_len which bound each field against the end pointer for that TLV; the many explicit end-pointer comparisons (pbVar4/pbVar14/pbVar15) enforce it. Reviewed: no missing bounds check found in the length math; this is upstream mbedtls. Attack surface is the TLS server certificate (pre-auth), but the code is the stock parser.

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::crypt_RsaVerify
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: main_app::crypt_RsaVerify(sig, siglen, msg, msglen, expected, explen, key, keylen, mode) s4=sig s5=siglen s2=msg s3=msglen s1=expected s9=explen s6=keyblob s8=keybloblen. Guards: msg,msglen,expected non-NULL, explen==0x100 exactly, keyblob,keybloblen non-NULL. Parses the flash keyblob via crypt_LoadPublicKey(this=&pk_ctx_on_stack, keyblob, keybloblen) then verifies with crypt_RsaPkcs1Verify @ b017499e using expected (hdr+0xa0,0x100). Stack has a canary (g_stack_canary checked on exit). pk_ctx is a 16-byte mbedtls_pk_context {pk_info*, pk_ctx*}; the RSA context itself is heap-allocated (mbedtls_pk_setup b0171a3a). No attacker-controlled write reaches pk_ctx here.

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::crypt_RsaVerify_BundleKey
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: crypt_RsaVerify_BundleKey(sig, siglen, msg, msglen, expected, explen, key, keylen) Thin trampoline: stores 1 as the 9th (stack) argument and tail-calls crypt_RsaVerify @ b017c318. The extra arg is the pk type/mode used by the b0171a7a pk_info dispatch. All eight register args are forwarded unchanged (a0..a7), so VerifySignature's call maps 1:1 onto crypt_RsaVerify. Verified: disasm b017c452 sets sp[0]=1 then calls b017c318 (no register clobber).
FUNCTION.TYPEINFO_CMT: long __stdcall crypt_RsaVerify_BundleKey(long sig, long siglen, long msg, long msglen, long expected, long explen, long key, long keylen)

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::Json_DecodeString
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Json_DecodeString(node, ctx): decodes a quoted JSON string in place. Output buffer is allocated with size = raw_span - backslash_count + 1 (ctx[4] allocator), which is always >= the number of decoded bytes (a \uXXXX escape consumes 6 raw bytes for <=4 UTF-8 output), so no overflow. Sets node+0x18=0x10 and node+0x20=decoded buffer. Uses node+0x100/0x200 flag bits in the free path.

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::Json_NodeAlloc
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Json_NodeAlloc(alloc_fn): (*alloc_fn)(0x40) + memset. alloc_fn comes from ParseCtx[4] = PTR_pvPortMalloc (ram:b01f8ef8 -> ram:b00d0c72), i.e. the FreeRTOS heap_5_ext pvPortMalloc (malloc_sram/psram per DAT_ram_b01fa270). Always 0x40-byte Json_Node. This is the allocation performed *during* a recursive parse, so it is the consumer of any heap metadata corrupted below a task stack; free-list pointers are XOR-masked with the mcycle-derived cookie and range-asserted, so forging is infeasible.

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::Json_ParseValue
main_app::Json_ParseStringCore
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Json_ParseStringCore(str,out_end,strict): builds the stack ParseCtx {ptr,len,pos,depth=0,alloc=PTR_pvPortMalloc ram:b01f8ef8 -> ram:b00d0c72/ram:b00c43ea}, allocates the 0x40 root node and calls the recursive Json_ParseValue. NO stack/depth budget of its own; the only bound is ctx[3]<1000 inside Json_ParseValue. On overflow it frees the partial tree (Json_NodeFreeRecursive). Security analysis: see Json_ParseValue ram:b017cfc0 (RULED OUT for CF hijack; DoS).

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::Json_ParseString_Internal
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Json_ParseString_Internal(str): thin wrapper -> Json_ParseStringCore(str,0,0). Reached from Json_ParseString ram:b0138638 and JsonDocument_ParseString ram:b0138652.

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::CMediaStreamAudio_HandleFrame
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Audio inbound E2EE/decrypt entry (network RX). param_2 is a holder whose *param_2 is the depacketized packet; vtable slot1 returns {data=obj+0x50, len=*(u32*)(obj+0x44)} (CRtpPayloadBuffer). If E2EE ctx (media+0x408)==0 the raw frame is pushed straight to CSpeakerJitterBuffer (no copy). Otherwise prov_memcpy(&g_audioStaging_b021b480, data, len) is UNBOUNDED but is immediately followed by CSframeE2ee_Decrypt which noreturn-aborts for len>0x140; staging is 0x2b2 and max len = pool node 0x540-0x50 = 0x4f0, so any len>0x140 corrupts <=0x23e bytes of adjacent BSS then halts (DoS). len<=0x140 copy is in-bounds. VERDICT: bounded-BSS + guaranteed halt, no in-hart control-flow target; not RCE.

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::RTP_AcquirePayloadBuffer
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: RTP_AcquirePayloadBuffer(outHolder, poolObj, srcCtx): gets a fixed-size buffer from the media pool, sets vtable to CRtpPayloadBuffer_vtable (b01e8630), capacity=*(u32*)(pool+0x9320)-0x50, payload_len=0, and binds srcCtx (packet+0x20) via FUN_ram_b010ba0a. Pool slot2 (b00fac56) returns pool+0x9318; slot3 (b0100f60) aborts if requested size > *(u32*)(pool+8). Capacity is thus a fixed node size, not attacker-controlled.

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::RTP_DepacketizePacket
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: RTP depacketizer. Input packet object (CRtpPayloadBuffer) read via vtable slot2 -> {data=+0x50, len=+0x44}. All accesses bounds-checked against end=data+len: version==2, header=12+CC*4<=end, extension header bounded, padding `end-=end[-1]` re-checked by `hdr<=end`. Payload len=end-hdr. Allocates via RTP_AcquirePayloadBuffer; capacity = node_size-0x50 (fixed, pool slot2 = pool+0x9318/field+8); memcpy only if capacity>=payload_len. VERDICT: no OOB found.

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::SRTP_GetStreamIndexFromSsrc
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Maps an incoming SSRC (param_2) to a fixed stream slot 0..3 by comparing against session+0x14/+0x18/+0x1c/+0x20. Returns 0 for the first match / unknown. Bounded: never yields >3.

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::SRTP_BuildNonceAndIndex
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: SRTP_BuildNonceAndIndex(session, idx, seq, roc, outNonce16, outLen, isRtcp): copies the 12-byte session nonce salt (session+0x6a RTP / +0x8a RTCP) to outNonce, XORs seq bytes, and for RTP XORs the 4-byte session+0xa0+idx*0xc counter; for RTCP XORs the 4-byte session+0x9c+idx*0xc index. idx is the 0..3 value from SRTP_GetStreamIndexFromSsrc, so all offsets are bounded (<=0xc7). Sets *outLen=0xc.

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::Mbedtls_GcmAuthDecryptStaged
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: SRTP AES-GCM decrypt helper. Copies param_8 (ciphertext length) into a 1400-byte stack staging buffer AFTER checking `if (0x540 < param_8) noreturn abort`; then mbedtls_gcm_auth_decrypt. Max 0x540 < 1400 => staging copy in-bounds. VERDICT: bounded.

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::SRTP_ProcessPacket
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: SRTP/SRTCP inbound processing. Packet is {void*data; u32 len}. Rejects CSRC!=0. SSRC (RTP data[8..11]; SRTCP data[4..7]) mapped by SRTP_GetStreamIndexFromSsrc to a fixed 0..3 index; index only addresses session+0x9c+idx*0xc and session+0xa0+idx*0xc. Len validated >= header (0xc RTP/8 RTCP) before header reads. SRTP_BuildNonceAndIndex derives nonce/rollover. SRTP_AesGcmCrypt enforces len>=hdr+0x10(+4 RTCP). VERDICT: index and lengths bounded; no OOB found.

FUNCTION.NAME: CJsonRpcResponseRss::SendResponse
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CJsonRpcResponseRss::SendResponse (vtable slot +0x10): builds a response CTree (Centcom_RssLst_Get + opcode 0xdf), writes byteswapped int and the response string (length *(short*)(this+8)) via FUN_ram_b01648ca, then enqueues via the Rss list vtable+0x28. Note the copy length is this+8 low 16 bits, i.e. attacker-influenced response content; tree setter allocates, so bounded by tree semantics (inferred).

FUNCTION.NAME: CJsonRpcResponseRss::SetDingId
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CJsonRpcResponseRss::SetDingId (vtable slot +0x18): parses attacker "ding_id" field to an int and stores it as a std::string at this+8. Called by JsonRpc_ParseAndDispatch before handler invocation. No memory-unsafe copy.

FUNCTION.NAME: CJsonRpcResponseRss::BuildResponseJson
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CJsonRpcResponseRss::BuildResponseJson (vtable slot +0x38): formats "{\"jsonrpc\":\"2.0\",\"id\":..., ...}" response with the stored ding_id/std::string. Uses fixed format strings; no attacker format string.

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::CCvSettings_AcmdDispatch
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CCvSettings ACMD dispatcher. Opcode 0x10096 sets a boolean setting and propagates; 0x10097 updates an integer and propagates; 0x10020 writes indexed setting tuples (indices <0x13, 100..118, or 200..218); 0x10093 refreshes CV settings; 0x10001 subtype 6 copies pending 0x16C-byte settings into active once, propagates, and notifies another subsystem; 0x10099 copies pending settings into active if different; 0x10013 builds the event-notification list. Unknown commands return 0x0D.

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::CIpV4_AcmdDispatch
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CIpV4 ACMD dispatcher. Opcode 0x10001 forwards a subtype to the IPv4 state/query routine. Opcode 0x10009 subcommands: 0 static mode (virtual slot +0x68); 1 enable DHCP (+0x78); 2 renew (+0x88); 3 release (+0x90); 4 rebind (+0x98); 5 logs IPv4 address, mask, DNS and DHCP counters. Unknown subcommands/opcodes return 0x0D.

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::CNwAccessWifi_AcmdDispatch
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CNwAccessWifi ACMD dispatcher. Opcode 0x10007 subcommands: 0 mount, 1 dismount, 2 connect, 3 disconnect, 4 factory reset, 5 read/log MAC, 8 stop AP, 9 set profile, 10 get profile, 11 config placeholder, 12 invoke a vtable operation, 13 enumerate/log profiles, 14 invoke another vtable operation, 16 read/log current SSID+BSSID, 17 read/log profile SSID+BSSID, and 33 read/log Wi-Fi channel. Other selectors in the allowed range through 33 are no-op/default paths. Opcode 0x10001 includes status subtypes: 2 exposes RSSI/channel/MAC/integrity/beacon-loss/profile/activity fields; 5 resets counters for arg4==10; 6 calls two virtual status methods. Unsupported opcodes/subtypes generally return 0x0D.

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::CSetupMethodWifi_HandleE2eeSetup
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CSetupMethodWifi registered interface body (adjustor thunk b01b46ba subtracts 8 from this). It recognizes opcodes 0x1000B (selector 11 path) and 0x1004B (selectors 0/1); the latter branches into setup-state helpers and uses state stored in the object. Further semantic names for those helper paths are unresolved. Unknown commands/selectors fall through the handler's default result.

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::SFrame_ParseNalUnitsH264
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: SFrame_ParseNalUnitsH264: walks up to n_units descriptors. SPS(NAL 7) -> Avc_ParseSps into ctx+0x120 (stride 0x14, cap 6, count at ctx+0x198); PPS(NAL 8) -> Avc_ParsePps into ctx+0x19c (stride 0xc, cap 6, count at ctx+0x1e4). Existing entries matched by id and overwritten; otherwise count is only incremented while != 6 and slot = count-1, so indices stay 0..5. Copies exactly sizeof(AvcSps)/sizeof(AvcPps). AUDIT: NEGATIVE.
FUNCTION.TYPEINFO_CMT: long __stdcall SFrame_ParseNalUnitsH264(long ctx, long data, AvcNalUnit * units, long n_units, long parse_enabled)

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::SFrame_ParseNalUnits
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: SFrame_ParseNalUnits: splits a media payload into AvcNalUnit descriptors. Mode selection: (ctx[0]-2)&0xfffffffd == 0 (ctx[0]==2 || ctx[0]==3) => length-prefixed (AVCC): iterates 4-byte big-endian lengths; descriptor = {offset=(int)(p+4)-(int)data, length=be32, type=0, flags=0}. Else Annex-B: scans for 00 00 01 / 00 00 00 01 start codes. Both branches: descriptor writes are gated by index < max_units; zero-length rejected; final index clamped to max_units. Then dispatches by ctx[0] to SFrame_ClassifyNalUnitsHevc (ctx[0]==3/4) or SFrame_ParseNalUnitsH264. REACHABILITY: network. Called via computed calls from 0c_networking at ram:c0c59270 / c0c5931a / c0c59c64. AUDIT: NEGATIVE (bounds above re-verified this pass).
FUNCTION.TYPEINFO_CMT: ulong __stdcall SFrame_ParseNalUnits(int * ctx, byte * data, ulong len, AvcNalUnit * units, ulong max_units, ulong parse_enabled)

FUNCTION.TYPEINFO_CMT: long __stdcall SFrame_SliceHeaderSizeH264(long ctx, void * nal, ulong len)

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::SFrame_InsertCodecConfigH264
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: SFrame_InsertCodecConfigH264: parses an AVCC config blob (param_8[0]==1, param_8[5]=numSPS, then 16-bit big-endian length+payload entries, then numPPS). Extracts last SPS and last PPS, bounds-checks total (sps_len+pps_len+8 + ctx_len <= dst_cap) before shift+memcpy. Clamps on overrun. AUDIT: no OOB write found; note puStack_58 is only used when high word of the saved length is nonzero, which requires a PPS entry to have been accepted.

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::SFrame_RewriteSpsH264
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: SFrame_RewriteSpsH264: NAL type 7 -> Avc_ParseSps, then Avc_WriteSps into dst. All three memmove/extents are gated by (uVar2<=dst_cap) && (src_len - delta <= dst_cap - uVar2). AUDIT: NEGATIVE.

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::Pb_ReadVarint
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Varint decode with strict 32-bit overflow rejection (sign-extended high bytes must be 0xff/0x00; rejects >5 bytes). param_3 optional eof flag.

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::Pb_ReadRaw
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Raw read helper. If dest param2==0 and stream is a plain buffer (not callback), it drains in 0x10-byte chunks (discard). Otherwise requires bytes_left>=len else "end_of_stream"; calls stream->read_cb; on failure sets "io_error"; else bytes_left-=len.

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::Pb_IStreamInit
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Init pb_istream_t from a memory buffer: read_cb=plain-buffer reader (LAB_ram_b01b85b8), data=param2, bytes_left=param3, errmsg=0.

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::Pb_SkipField
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Skip unknown/ignored field by wire type: 0=varint (<=10B), 1=8B, 2=len-prefixed (Pb_Read len), 5=4B; other -> "invalid_wire_type".

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::Pb_ReadFieldLength
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Read length-prefixed submessage: varint32 len; memcpy substream=stream(0x20); require parent bytes_left>=len else "parent_stream_too_short"; substream.bytes_left=len; parent.bytes_left-=len. Bounds nested messages to the parent buffer.

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::Pb_EndSubmessage
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Require substream fully consumed (bytes_left==0), then copy data pointer/errmsg back to parent stream.

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::Pb_DecodeField
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Pb_DecodeField - protobuf field decoder. BOUNDS (proven): wire type 0 varint: value must fit the descriptor data_size (1/2/4/8) else "integer_too_large". wire type 6 bytes: u16 len read as varint32; requires len<0x10000 and len+2 <= field.data_size (else "bytes_overflow"); stores u16 len at dest, copies len bytes to dest+2. wire type 7 string: requires len+1 <= field.data_size (else "string_overflow"); copies len bytes and writes a NUL at dest+len. wire type 8 submessage: length from Pb_ReadFieldLength, which rejects len > remaining parent bytes ("parent_stream_too_short"); submessage fields are placed by their own fixed descriptor offsets. arrays: index bounded by descriptor count ("array_overflow"). => Every length the provisioning handlers later read from a bytes/string field is capped by the descriptor data_size. This is why Req0C creds(<=16)/secret(<=12) cannot overflow its 0x1e buffer.

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::Pb_DecodeMessage
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Message decode loop (stream, table, dest). Reads tags via Pb_ReadTag; Pb_FieldIterFind; for repeated nested (modifier 0x30, kind 8) performs reset prov_memset(dest,0,data_size)+Pb_ReleaseMessage when the ctrl tag word != tag, then writes tag. Unknown tags -> Pb_SkipField. Extension/unknown handler linked list + kind==9 catch-all. Enforces packed fixed-count (array_size) and required-field presence bitmap ("missing_required_field"). Feeds Pb_DecodeField.

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::Pb_DecodeSubmessagePtr
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: DecodeSubmessagePtr: Pb_ReleaseMessage(table,dest) then Pb_DecodeMessage(stream,table,dest). Entry used by CDeviceProvision_DecodeMessage with table ram:0xc0ca0d48 and dest=CDeviceProvisionFlow+0x58 buffer.

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::otp_app_clock_gate_set
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: App OTP clock control helper: saves CLK_CTRL and writes 0x164 for read mode, or 0 when disabling; caller restores the saved value after the read.

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::otp_app_status_read_clear
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: App OTP interrupt/status helper: returns INT_STATUS; when passed nonzero, clears the status register before returning.

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::otp_read_row_raw_app
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: App raw OTP row-window read: loads 32 bits from 0x90126000 + byte_offset and returns the value. The app wrapper supplies row_index * 4, matching the bootloader OTP data alias.

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::Avc_ParseSps
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Avc_ParseSps: H.264 SPS parser. All bit reads go through the bounded BitReader; writes AvcSps (0x14 bytes) into out. Every parsed count that indexes a table (num_ref_frames_in_pic_order, etc.) is range-checked. Returns true(1) on failure, false(0) on success. AUDIT: NEGATIVE.
FUNCTION.TYPEINFO_CMT: bool __stdcall Avc_ParseSps(void * nal, uint len, AvcSps * out)

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::Avc_WriteSps

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::Avc_ParsePps
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Avc_ParsePps: H.264 PPS parser; BitReader-bounded; writes AvcPps (0xc bytes). FMO (slice_group) rejected; id fields bounded. AUDIT: NEGATIVE.
FUNCTION.TYPEINFO_CMT: bool __stdcall Avc_ParsePps(void * nal, uint len, AvcPps * out)

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::Avc_ParseSliceHeader
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Avc_ParseSliceHeader: parses slice header against caller-supplied SPS/PPS arrays (sps_count/pps_count). PPS lookup loops while index < pps_count; SPS lookup loops while index < sps_count; no unchecked index. ref_pic_list_modification / dec_ref_pic_marking loops are BitReader_InBounds-gated and reject counts > 0x1f/3. Returns consumed bit position or 0. AUDIT: NEGATIVE.

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::Pb_FieldIterInit
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Init pb_field_iter_t: [0]=table,[1]=cursor,[0x10]=int index=0,[0x18]=base. If base!=0: dest=[0x20]=base+first.data_offset; ctrl=[0x28]=dest+first.size (size is signed, may be negative). Returns first.tag!=0.

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::Pb_FieldIterNext
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Advance cursor by one 0x13-byte pb_field_t. If the next tag is 0, re-init and return 0. SPECIAL CASE: if current.type&0x30==0x30 AND next.type&0x30==0x30 AND next.data_offset==0xffff (union/oneof alias, e.g. ram:0xc0ca1478 members f2..f14), dest/ctrl are left UNCHANGED. Otherwise dest = prev_dest + cur.data_size*(cur.array_size if packed) + next.data_offset; ctrl = dest + next.size. Reads next.data_offset at byte 0x16 and next.size at 0x18 (= next+3 / next+5).

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::Pb_FieldIterFind
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Find field with tag==param_2 by walking the table; skips entries with (type&0xf)==9 (callback/catch-all marker). Wraps to start and returns 0 if absent. On success iter->dest corresponds to the matched field.

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::BitReader_Init
FUNCTION.TYPEINFO_CMT: void __stdcall BitReader_Init(BitReader * br, void * buf, uint len, uint emulation_prevention)

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::BitReader_ReadBits
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: BitReader_ReadBits: reads up to 32 bits MSB-first from br->buffer, with optional H.264 emulation-prevention (0x000003) removal. Bounds: if length*8 < cur_byte*8+bit_offset+nbits it only advances bit_offset (marks out-of-bounds, returns 0). The per-byte loop advances cur_byte only while cur_byte+1 < length. The initial partial-byte read is reached only when length*8 >= cur_byte*8+bit_offset+nbits, so cur_byte < length. AUDITED (this pass): no OOB byte read found. NOTE: length<<3 is 32-bit; safe for the sub-2^29 media-frame lengths used here.

FUNCTION.NAME: main_app::BitReader_InBounds
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: BitReader_InBounds: (cur_byte*8 + bit_offset) <= length*8. ReadBits/TellValid use this to decide success. Returned bit position is used by Avc_Parse* to set the "valid bits" / consumed length fields in the output structs.
