FUNCTION.NAME: ram::uart_settings_load
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: uart_settings_load reads the persisted UART settings at flash offset 0x43000. If validation fails, it sets the baud field to 0xe1000 (921600) and marks settings initialized; this is the firmware default console baud.

FUNCTION.NAME: ram::boot_retry_fallback_check
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: boot_retry_fallback_check: OtpContents.BOOT_ATTEMPT (reg 6) nibble [7:4] vs system-controller boot count (@0x90000091); switch boot slot + reboot if otp+1 < sysc.

FUNCTION.NAME: ram::actually_boot_the_device
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: First-stage secure-boot flow confirmed from disassembly/decompilation: actually_boot_the_device reads SBIH header from active OTA slot, calls sbih_auth_and_decrypt_G(header,0xf20), and compares the result against BL_OK 0xc0ab6. A failure logs secure-boot authentication failed and reboots/marks the slot unsuccessful; bundle_hdr_init_G and second-stage loading occur only after success.

FUNCTION.NAME: ram::stack_canary_init_trng
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: stack_canary_init_trng: one-shot boot init of the global stack canary. Calls trng_fill(&buf,8,0); if it fails -> reboot_device_G(0). Stores the 8 TRNG bytes to g_stack_canary @ ram:0xb0297260 (disasm ram:b0280a42-b0280a4a: c.ldsp a5,0x8(sp); sd a5,-0x7e6(a4) with a4=b0297a46). Canonical caller: ram:b0280a64 (boot init), UNCONDITIONAL_CALL. NOTE: g_stack_canary is a single process-wide global, NOT per-task and not copied into the TCB; every function reloads it in its prologue and compares on return. So one 8-byte disclosure defeats the canary for every task/frame.

FUNCTION.NAME: ram::fwbl_main_boot
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: FWBL main boot: init uart/flash/OTP, regenerate unique number, security thermometer check, rotatable key provisioning, SBIH verify, unlock state eval (reboots-left lockout), then cli_boot_entry_gate (50ms '=' window) before booting image.

FUNCTION.NAME: ram::keyslot_blank_check
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: keyslot_blank_check(slot): all 16 regs of OtpContents.AES_KEY_SLOTn must read 0 (base from otp_partition_key_base_table @0xB0292DD0).

FUNCTION.NAME: ram::keyslot_read_key
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: keyslot_read_key: reads 16 regs of OtpContents.AES_KEY_SLOTn (raw AES-256 key material) into buffer; slot from OtpContents key-index counters; zeroize+panic on ECC error.

FUNCTION.NAME: ram::keyslot_provision_new_key
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: keyslot_provision_new_key: TRNG 32 bytes -> OtpContents.AES_KEY_SLOTn regs (otpw path), then bumps OtpContents.CNT5_ROTATABLE_KEY_IDX via otp_counter_burn(5).

FUNCTION.NAME: ram::antirollback_check_fwbl
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: FWBL anti-rollback startup check: target level is hdr_get_fwbl_ar_level() == 5; reads OTP counter 1, and when current < 5 < max, sets SYSCTL.boot_ctr_greater_than_10 bits via sysc_burn_counter_fwbl, clears boot-attempt count, and reboots to advance the thermometer counter. This routine alone does not reject when the OTP counter is already above this image's target level; do not interpret it as proof that an older FWBL is rejected. External ROM behavior is outside this loaded binary.

FUNCTION.NAME: ram::cli_process_command
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: FreeRTOS+CLI prvProcessCommand: walks registered command list (head at gp-0x7f0), matches name (case-insensitive), checks cExpectedNumberOfParameters @+0x18 (-1 = any), calls handler @+0x10 with (writeBuf, writeBufLen, params).

FUNCTION.NAME: ram::cli_console_main_loop
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: FreeRTOS+CLI console main loop. Reads chars via function ptrs set up by serial_console_enter (a0=cmd buffer ctx, a1=console out fn, a2/a3=uart in/out bufs). Echoes/backspaces, on ENTER calls cli_process_input_chars -> cli_process_command.

FUNCTION.NAME: ram::cli_read_char_kick_wdt
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Serial-console input helper: calls uart_readc() for UART0, stores one received byte at the supplied buffer and returns 1; when no byte is available, kicks the watchdog and returns -1. Used by the stage3_memconsole payload for line input.

FUNCTION.NAME: ram::cli_setup_gate_check
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Anti-tamper gate: checks unlock_get_last_status()==0x95432 and stack cookie; if OK -> cli_register_standard_commands (b0282d0c) and return; else loops calling cli_register_debug_commands + error print forever (bricked state).

FUNCTION.NAME: ram::serial_console_enter
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Enters the serial console: loads uart in/out fn ptrs + prompts ("\r\n[Input a command and press ENTER]\r\n>") and tail-calls cli_console_main_loop.

FUNCTION.NAME: ram::cmd_fwxmod
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: FWBL CLI command handler, not an ACMD target. Parses a flash start offset and maximum transfer size, then calls xmodem_write_flash. The command itself has no partition/writeable-area whitelist check; xmodem_write_flash erases the sector-rounded range and receives/programs up to the supplied size. Lower-level spi_flash_erase enforces sector alignment and checks range against flash_end.

FUNCTION.NAME: ram::cli_register_standard_commands
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Restricted FWBL command setup: resets command list; registers status, getunlock, unlock; publishes unlock mode 4 in validated RAM handoff. Application maps mode 4 to boot_mode=1, suppressing application serial shell unless FQC flag is set.

FUNCTION.NAME: ram::cli_register_debug_commands
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Registers 12 standard commands from CliCommand table at b0293c58 using index table b0293c48 (order: genpekey,fwxmod,frxmod,poa,pob,aerasebcb,get,l,otpr,otpw,chbr). Only reached when cli_setup_gate_check passes (magic 0x95432).

FUNCTION.NAME: ram::cmd_otpr
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Console command handler for `otpr <addr>`: decimal row index 0..0x3FF, reads a 16-bit OTP row through otp_read_register, reports ECC/status, and prints the value.

FUNCTION.NAME: ram::cmd_otpw
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: FWBL CLI OTP write command, separate from ACMD. Restricts row index to 0..0x3ff and, for nonblank rows, only permits valid non-decreasing thermometer updates; this is not an arbitrary RAM/flash write.

FUNCTION.NAME: ram::cmd_getunlock
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: getunlock [load|store]: generates/loads/stores 256-byte vendor unlock challenge. Challenge contains unique-number hash(0x14)@+0x08, reboot counter@+0x1c, 0x10 random bytes; exported from unlock partition record at 0xb02b10e0. Prints hex for signing.

FUNCTION.NAME: ram::cli_boot_entry_gate
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Boot-time CLI entry gate. If setup OK: 50ms window polling UART for '=' (0x3d) to enter CLI; else prints "Setup is not correct, entering CLI." and enters CLI unconditionally.

FUNCTION.NAME: ram::xmodem_write_flash
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Bootloader CLI XMODEM flash writer used by cmd_fwxmod and OTA slot programming. Erases the sector-rounded [start, start+size) range, then receives data and writes at start+offset. This is an SPI flash write primitive, not a general RAM/MMIO write.

FUNCTION.NAME: ram::otp_counter_start_verify?
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Boot-time OTP verification setup: enqueues the three ranges in verified_data and starts the controller's queued verification operation.

FUNCTION.NAME: ram::fwbl_early_hw_init
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Early hardware initialization processes the app anti-rollback bump request staged in SYSCTL/BL-PUBLIC config: clears the trigger, reads OTP CNT4_BUNDLE_ANTIROLLBACK, compares it with staged bundle_ar, and calls otp_counter_burn(4) when OTP is lower. This is the irreversible commit path for a newer signed app version; the config shadow is a staging/control record, not the OTP fuse itself.

FUNCTION.NAME: ram::read_flash
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: FWBL bounds-checked flash read: requires len!=0, read_to!=0, param_1 <= flash_end and param_1+len <= flash_end. NOTE: `len + param_1` is a 64-bit add, so a very large caller-supplied len can wrap the sum and bypass the end check (callers today pass small lengths, e.g. 0xF20).

FUNCTION.NAME: ram::uart_write_byte_polled
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Polled UART transmitter: uart_write_byte_polled(port, byte, retries). Checks periph_is_initialized(), polls uart_tx_idle_any(port), then writes the byte with periph_reg_write(port, 0, byte); returns 0 if unavailable or the retry limit expires. Candidate for a one-byte observable ROP marker, provided the chosen UART port is initialized and configured to the host baud.

FUNCTION.NAME: ram::uart_console_putc_hart
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: FWBL's per-hart serial-console byte writer. It selects g_uart_port_by_hart[mhartid] and calls the bounded polling UART transmit path. In this image, the hart-0 mapping is port 0. Stage3 can use this initialized console route directly without reconfiguring the app RingUart driver or depending on interrupts.

FUNCTION.NAME: ram::otp_read_reg_raw
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Raw OTP word-window read: reads a 32-bit value from 0x90126000 + byte_offset. otp_read_register passes row_index*4 as the offset; the indexed counters use rows listed in g_otp_counter_ranges. This is a platform-specific MMIO/OTP alias, not a RISC-V architectural address.

FUNCTION.NAME: ram::fwbl_fatal_halt_loop
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Fatal halt "loop": stops/re-inits timer then spins forever. Reached from FUN_ram_b02802a6 on unrecoverable init failure.

FUNCTION.NAME: ram::flash_read_sbih_header_G
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Reads a fixed 0xF20-byte SBIH header from flash at `read_from` into `read_to`. Caller MUST provide a >= 0xF20-byte buffer (actually_boot_the_device passes the 0xF20 global header_data at 0xB02AF010); there is no length parameter. Returns BL_OK 0xC0AB6 on success, 0x8EC4B on bad args / read error.

FUNCTION.NAME: ram::bundle_ar_counter_update
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Bundle anti-rollback update. Reads OTP counter 4 (CNT4_BUNDLE_ANTIROLLBACK) and its maximum. Equal version stages the same level and succeeds; lower version returns the initialized error status; higher version stages the new level plus feature flag 1 and reboots so the OTP counter can be advanced. sbih_auth_and_decrypt_G rejects this error result on locked devices.

FUNCTION.NAME: ram::sbih_auth_and_decrypt_G
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: SBIH authorization path: parses the 0x200-byte catalog in the supplied sbih_header, finds `Image.sig` and `Image`, and takes the candidate application version from the `Image` record header's `version_num` byte (first_0x50_sbih_header_bytes +0x39). It checks the signature and invokes bundle_ar_counter_update(version_num); that function compares against OTP counter index 4 (CNT4_BUNDLE_ANTIROLLBACK).

FUNCTION.NAME: ram::x509_verify_rsassa_pss_sha256_G
FUNCTION.TYPEINFO_CMT: bool __stdcall x509_verify_rsassa_pss_sha256_G(first_0x50_sbih_header_bytes * img_header, long img_header_len, byte * img, long img_len, byte * sig, long sig_len, byte * pub_key, long pub_key_len, int is_1)

FUNCTION.NAME: ram::sbih_verify_wrapper_G
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Thin wrapper: RSA-PSS-SHA256 verify of the Image element (x509_verify_rsassa_pss_sha256_G) with siglen=0x50, sig=param_3, len=param_4, pubkey=param_5, key_len=0x100, blob=param_7, blob_len=param_8). Returns bool.
FUNCTION.TYPEINFO_CMT: bool __stdcall sbih_verify_wrapper_G(long param_1, long param_2, long param_3, long param_4, long param_5, long param_6, long param_7, long param_8)

FUNCTION.NAME: ram::get_bund_element_load_addr_size
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: ram::get_bund_element_load_addr_size: returns BUND_HDR_ELEMENT0_LOAD_ADDR[index] and SIZE[index] for the element type. Note the header already carries both a load address and a size, yet callers like bundle_load_element_to_addr ignore the load address and use a caller-supplied dst -- so the header size is not cross-checked against the intended destination at all.
FUNCTION.TYPEINFO_CMT: int __stdcall get_bund_element_load_addr_size(undefined8 bund_element_type, ulong * size, ulong * load_addr)

FUNCTION.NAME: ram::validated_load_bund_element_at_address
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: ram::validated_load_bund_element_at_address(type, where): same as FUN_ram_b016820c but "validated" refers only to the post-copy SHA-256/digest check, NOT the size. The element size (BUND_HDR_ELEMENT0_SIZE[index]) is passed verbatim to flash_read_to_ram_G into caller-supplied `where` with no bound. On hash mismatch a memset(where,0,size) also writes `size` bytes. Digest table at 0x9000022c (persist_data) is zero in the image -> populated at boot.

FUNCTION.NAME: ram::otp_config_field_write
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Writes fields in the SYSCTL/BL-PUBLIC shadow at 0x90000f24 through bitfield_write. This is mutable staging state with CRC commit; it is distinct from OTP counters, which otp_read_counter reads from OTP registers.

FUNCTION.NAME: ram::safe_sha256
FUNCTION.TYPEINFO_CMT: undefined8 __stdcall safe_sha256(byte * data, ulonglong len, byte * output)

FUNCTION.NAME: ram::check_image_related_hash_against_otp
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: otp_pubkey_hash_verify: reads OtpContents.IMG_PUBKEY_SHA256[slot][0..15] (regs (slot+0x14)*0x10 + i, slot from signed header), consttime-compares the 32-byte SHA-256 against the bundle pubkey hash.

FUNCTION.NAME: ram::bl_check_sig
FUNCTION.TYPEINFO_CMT: undefined __stdcall bl_check_sig(byte * key, undefined8 data, undefined8 length)

FUNCTION.NAME: ram::check_sbih_constant
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: SBIH constant gate: compares the u32 at g_sbih_constant (0xB02CB8C0) against 0xA7E5C369. Returns BL_OK 0xC0AB6 when equal, BL_ERR 0x8EC4B otherwise. The decompiler's `_a3a_aec_pipeline_run` alias was a bogus auto-name; renamed g_sbih_constant.

FUNCTION.NAME: ram::otp_verify_enqueue
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: OTP hardware verify queue entry: accepts start/end page values below 0x400, fills one of eight VERIFY_JOB slots with range and mode flags, and returns the slot index.

FUNCTION.NAME: ram::otp_verify_start
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Starts the OTP controller's queued verification jobs by setting VERIFY_START bits 0x14.

FUNCTION.NAME: ram::otp_read_counter
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Reads a thermometer-encoded OTP counter using otp_counter_table: each table entry gives a starting OTP word offset and a count of words; each word must decode to a valid monotonic thermometer value. Returns the sum, rejecting invalid/non-monotonic contents.

FUNCTION.NAME: ram::otp_counter_reg_step_burn
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: otp_counter_reg_step_burn: burns next thermometer step into counter reg (OtpContents counter fields; base/count from otp_counter_table @0xB02944F0).

FUNCTION.NAME: ram::otp_counter_burn
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: One-way OTP counter burn routine. Reads the current thermometer counter, rejects targets below current or above count*5, encodes the requested level into OTP words, and programs the corresponding OTP registers. App anti-rollback uses index 4 / CNT4_BUNDLE_ANTIROLLBACK.

FUNCTION.NAME: ram::otp_counter_max_get
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: otp_counter_max_get: computes max = count*5 from otp_counter_table (does NOT write).

FUNCTION.NAME: ram::otp_read_unique_number
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: otp_read_unique_number: reads OtpContents.UNIQUE_NUMBER (regs 0x2E1..0x2E4). QUIRK: loop index (i&3)+0x2E1 for i=0..9 -> the 8 real bytes are repeated to fill 20.

FUNCTION.NAME: ram::otp_unique_number_provision
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: otp_unique_number_provision: burns 4 TRNG bytes into blank OtpContents.UNIQUE_NUMBER regs.

FUNCTION.NAME: ram::unlock_validate_and_auth
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Unlock record auth state machine. UState@+0x60: 0xff=blank, 0xff0=one-time, 0xf00f/0xff00=vendor. Verifies .unlock magics @+0/+0x166, device unique-number match, RSA-signed blob vs embedded pubkey (PEM @b0295278). If vendor-unlocked reboots exceed 30 (OTP counter idx 3), downgrades UState to 0xf00f (one-time).

FUNCTION.NAME: ram::settings_read_var
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: settings_read_var: gates on OtpContents.KEYPROV_STATUS (reg 8) bit 11, then thermometer-reads/burns the caller's counter regs (security thermometer update).

FUNCTION.NAME: ram::add_header_to_catalog_record
FUNCTION.TYPEINFO_CMT: undefined __stdcall add_header_to_catalog_record(catalog_record * param_1, sbih_header * param_2, long is_0x200, long is_0)

FUNCTION.NAME: ram::catalog_record_next
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Pre-authentication SBIH record parser note: catalog_record_next processes attacker-controlled header bytes before signature validation. It bounds record-header assembly to 0x50 bytes, validates record magic and CRC, and limits parsing to the 0x200-byte catalog. Its returned Image record length is checked by sbih_auth_and_decrypt_G before signature verification. The remaining extent concern is Image length <= 0xf20 despite the +0x200 pointer offset into an input buffer filled with 0xf20 bytes.

FUNCTION.NAME: video_parser::Core3_TrapEntry
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Core3_TrapEntry: machine-mode trap vector target / core3 boot stub. Sets mtvec=ram:b02c84e8 then calls FUN_ram_b02b750e(mhartid,0,0). Reached from sec_mon::core_boot_core3_start (ram:b00009a6) and sec_mon::boot_fwbl_register_type1 (ram:b00052f4). This proves the whole ram:b02b7xxx-b02bdxxx section is the camera/ISP core3 firmware image, not a main-core network parser.

FUNCTION.NAME: video_parser::Video_Init
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Video_Init: core3 ISP pipeline bring-up (video.c). Allocates SRAM/PSRAM frame buffers, programs VPE1/VPE2 ring buffers via CircBuf_Program, computes buffer counts from sensor dimensions, starts the H.264 encoder via H264_StartEncoder. Inputs are sensor/ISP configuration and hardware state; no network/media parsing. Inferred name.

FUNCTION.NAME: video_parser::H264_StartEncoder
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: H264_StartEncoder: h264.c - reads a config struct (param_1[0..0xe]), writes hardware globals b02d1040/b02d1048/b02d1050/b02d1068..b02d1090, programs H.264 FIFO/registers and starts the hardware encoder (dependency of Video_Init). Inferred name; config comes from the ISP pipeline, not from inbound NAL data.

FUNCTION.NAME: video_parser::CircBuf_Program
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CircBuf_Program (circbuf.c): for buffer index param_1<6, computes a hardware address from ISP registers (700c0028/700c006c region), writes pointer table b02cc990[idx] register fields and the per-index descriptor at b02d2900+idx*0x20 (ptr/current/length/total). Index asserted <6. Data are hardware/DMA addresses, not attacker input. Inferred name.

FUNCTION.NAME: video_parser::CbtBuf_Read
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CbtBuf_Read (cbtbuf.c): drains up to param_3 bytes from circular buffer param_1 (<0x19) into param_2, using FUN_ram_b02bc750 to get a contiguous chunk and FUN_ram_b02bbfa6 to translate it. Advances and wraps the buffer pointer. Lengths come from the buffer's internal state. Inferred name.

FUNCTION.NAME: video_parser::a3a_ae_state_init
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: A3A AE state init. Creates the pipeline (a3a_aec_pipeline_create) and the weight grid at param_1+0x6b0 with descriptor {storage=param_1+0x700, capacity=0x100}. Fixes the weight-grid storage as a 0x100-byte buffer, which is why all generate_grid writes are capacity-checked.

FUNCTION.NAME: video_parser::A3AWeightGrid_ctor
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: A3AWeightGrid_ctor. param_1 = weight_grid; a1 = {storage,capacity} descriptor. Embedded A3ABaseWeightCalc at +8 via A3ABaseWeightCalc_ctor. Storage=grid+0x700, capacity=0x100.

FUNCTION.NAME: video_parser::a3a_grid_validate_tuning_type3
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Validate a type-3 grid-config blob: requires payload[0]==3 and u32 payload size > 0x3f (>=0x40). Returns the payload pointer (a1) unchanged when valid, else 0. Side-effect-free - no writes.

FUNCTION.NAME: video_parser::a3a_weight_grid_config
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: video_parser::a3a_weight_grid_config - consumes type-3 (grid config) and type-1 (weight-calc) blobs from the TuningGRID bundle (namespace 2, version 3). Storage is the fixed 0x100-byte buffer param_1+0x700, so all grid writes are capacity-checked. Delegates remaining blobs to a3a_base_weightcalc_import_tuning / a3a_weight_grid_parse_fail.

FUNCTION.NAME: video_parser::a3a_base_weightcalc_generate_grid
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: INFOLEAK ASSESSMENT (a3a_base_weightcalc_generate_grid OOB read): BUG PROVEN: entry_count = u32@payload+0x43 is gated only by blob size > 0x4a; the entry loop then reads ~10 bytes * entry_count from payload+4, over-reading the tuning blob. Values feed only the weight-grid math (stores bounded to the 0x100 grid). No write primitive, no egress to attacker. CANARY: unreachable — read bytes are transformed into weight values, never returned, and the target is the tuning blob (heap/flash), not g_stack_canary.

FUNCTION.NAME: video_parser::A3ABaseWeightCalc_ctor
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: A3ABaseWeightCalc_ctor: vtable b02cdea0; stores {storage,capacity} from descriptor into +8/+0x10 and zeroes the storage buffer. Called with storage=weight_grid+0x700, capacity=0x100 by a3a_ae_state_init.

FUNCTION.NAME: video_parser::a3a_base_weightcalc_import_tuning
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Import a type-1 (weight-calc) tuning blob into the base weight-calc object. Reads u16 width@payload[0], u16 height@payload[2]; computes count = (int)(width*height) via mulw and requires storage_capacity >= count before calling a3a_base_weightcalc_generate_grid. The blob's declared size at header+4 must be >0x4a only. Writes in generate_grid are bounded by the capacity check; the OOB is the entry-table over-read there.
FUNCTION.TYPEINFO_CMT: int __stdcall a3a_base_weightcalc_import_tuning(long weightcalc, byte * blob_header, byte * * payload_out)

FUNCTION.NAME: video_parser::A3AAecCameraStage_ctor
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: A3AAecCameraStage ctor: sets vtable b02ce498 and zeroes +0x18/+0x20/+0x28/+0x30 (gain tables). The type-10 config later fills payload@+8, payload+0xc0@+0x10 and the gain table ptr/count pairs.

FUNCTION.NAME: video_parser::A3AAecGridStage_ctor
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: A3AAecGridStage ctor (stage #2 at pipeline+0xf8, pipeline+0x70 pointer). Sets vtable b02ce110, +0x20/+0x24/+0x28=0xff, default accessor fn a3a_aec_grid_accessor_direct @+0x458. Type-2 config fills dims/strides/buffer later.

FUNCTION.NAME: video_parser::A3AAecPipeline_ctor
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: A3AAecPipeline_ctor. Base ctor sets vtable b02ce768 then this sets vtable b02cded0 (A3AAecCamera/Pipeline). Embedded stages: +0x68->+0xc0 (camera, b02ce498), +0x70->+0xf8 (grid, b02ce110), +0x78->+0x590, +0x80->+0x5d8, +0x88->+0x610 (dist, b02ce350). No tuning data involved.

FUNCTION.NAME: a3a_aec_grid_set_input_buffer
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: A3AAecGridStage vfunc +0x20: stores *param_2 into +0x470 (input grid buffer pointer). The buffer is caller-owned; +0x470 is only ever READ by a3a_aec_grid_accumulate. No write sink.

FUNCTION.NAME: video_parser::a3a_aec_grid_import_configure
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: A3AAecGridStage::config (type-2 blob, size >0x13). Reads width=byte@payload+0xe, height=byte@payload+0xf (rejects 0 and width*height>0x4000); row_stride=byte@payload+0x12+1; col_stride=row_stride*width+byte@payload+0x13. Clears +0x470 (buffer installed separately). All values byte-derived and area-capped, so the stored dims/strides are themselves bounded; they are only used for READS of +0x470.

FUNCTION.NAME: video_parser::a3a_aec_grid_accumulate
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: A3A_AEC_GRID accumulate. PROVEN: writes only to obj+0x2c histogram (0x400, indexed by min(weight,obj+0x20)<=0x3fc, bounded) and to the 16-byte output struct param_3. The obj+0x470 buffer (set by a3a_aec_grid_set_input_buffer from a caller-owned buffer) and the accessor struct at obj+0x438 are READ only. Loop bounds obj+0x440/0x444 vs dims obj+0x478/0x47c mismatch can cause an OOB READ of obj+0x470, not a write. NO OOB WRITE.

FUNCTION.NAME: a3a_aec_grid_process
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: A3AAecGridStage vfunc +0x18: iterates input stat sets (param_2[1]) and calls a3a_aec_grid_accumulate per set. Writes are bounded inside the callee.

FUNCTION.NAME: A3AAecDistStage::config
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: A3A_AEC_DIST stage, vtable b02ce350 slot +0x10. Consumes type-6 blob (declared size >99). Stores payload@+0x58, dist_ptr=payload+0x10@+0x60, dist_count=u32@payload+0x60@+0x68, hdr_ptr=payload+4@+0x70, hdr_count=u32@payload+8@+0x78 (must be <=1). Then calls (*(*(this+0x50)+0x20))(obj50,-1,0x400,hdr_count,payload). PROVEN: this+0x50 = pipeline+0xc0 (A3AAecCameraStage, vtable b02ce498); slot +0x20 = a3a_aec_camera_lookup_gain_index (0xb02cb020). That callee ignores a3/a4 (the raw payload) and only indexes the camera stage's own gain tables. No write from the type-6 payload. Consumers of +0x60/+0x68 (a3a_aec_dist_table_interp) are read-only. NO OOB WRITE.

FUNCTION.NAME: A3AAecDistStage::ctor
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: A3AAecDistStage ctor (param_1 = pipeline+0x610). Sets vtable b02ce350; +0x8/+0x20/+0x38 point at the embedded sub-vtable descriptors (b02ce3a0/b02ce3b8/b02ce3d0). Sets +0x50 = pipeline->vfunc_0x10() = A3AAecPipeline_get_camera_stage = pipeline+0xc0. +0x8c=0 (bounded scratch count).

FUNCTION.NAME: video_parser::a3a_aec_dist_table_interp
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: A3AAecDistStage reference-table interpolation. param_2={ptr,count}; count comes from the type-6 payload (dist_count @+0x68). Indexes piVar4[i*2] up to count with no upper bound vs the real array -> OOB READ only. No store.

FUNCTION.NAME: A3AAecCameraStage::config
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: A3AAecCameraStage::config (type-10 blob, declared size >199). Stores payload@+8, payload+0xc0@+0x10; if payload+0xc selector==1 uses analog table else digital, storing ptr=payload+0x10 and count=u32@payload+0xa0 (only checked !=0, so a huge count is accepted) at +0x18/+0x20 or +0x28/+0x30. Those counts feed A3AAecCameraStage::lookup_gain which only READS -> OOB read, no write.

FUNCTION.NAME: A3AAecCameraStage::lookup_gain
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: A3AAecCameraStage vfunc +0x20 (vtable b02ce498). Signature (this, uint value, uint cap). PROVEN from disasm: args a3/a4/a5 are dead; the routine reads this->payload@+8 (u32 selector @payload+0xc), then does a lookup / interpolation over the camera stage's own gain tables (+0x18/+0x20 digital, +0x28/+0x30 analog). FUNCTION.NAME: unk_type_6::hart_barrier_5way
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: 5-hart spin barrier (arg = leader hart, always 1 here). Flags: u32[5] at *(hart_barrier_flags_ptr)=0x02000000. Leader waits for all other harts to set their flag, then clears all 5. Followers set their own flag, fence rw,rw, spin until leader clears it. mstatus.MIE cleared; mie.MSIE set during the wait (IPI-breakable).

FUNCTION.NAME: unk_type_6::hart_wait_go_and_boot
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Per-hart boot entry (called from _start with a0=hartid,a1=0,a2=0): 1. mscratch=0; spin: t0 = *(u32*)(0x20020000 + mhartid*4) until nonzero. t0==0xFFFFFFFF => clear mailbox, keep waiting (park marker). 2. mscratch = go-ptr (boot data); sp = go_ptr[1] & ~0xf (per-hart stack). 3. copy .data (no-op, LMA==VMA), clear bss [gp-0x4c0, gp-0x338), tp=0. 4. if hartid==1 call hart1_placeholder_hook (ret stub). 5. pmp_unlock_flash_xip(): PMP locked NAPOT RWX 32MB over 0xd0000000+0xe0000000. 6. register_exit_callback(run_fini_runner@b02eed24); mie=0; FPU on if misa has F/D/Q; custom CSR 0x7c1 (cache ctrl) &= ~7. 7. main(1, &argv_ptr, &argv_ptr) -> metal_main; then metal_exit(main_ret).

FUNCTION.NAME: unk_type_6::hart_park_into_bootstub

FUNCTION.NAME: 0c_networking::CDeviceProvision_DispatchRequest
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT:
0c_networking::CDeviceProvision_DispatchRequest
Table g_BleProvDispatchTable (ram:0xc0ca0bd8) stride 16 = {u32 id; u32 pad; code* handler}. Loop ends at ram:0xc0ca0c78 (10 entries). id read from request+8 (u32); request[0] must be 1. handler(flow, request+8) is invoked. No per-field length validation occurs here.
IMPORTANT: several handler pointers point at 4-byte `j`/`addi a1,N; j` thunks that sit just before the Ghidra-named function body, e.g. id 0xc -> c0c22cc0 (`addi a1,8; j c0c22bd6`), id 9 -> c0c22b2e (`j c0c22a86`), id 0xd -> c0c22bd2 (`j c0c22b32`). No authentication/pairing check is present on this path; the virtual callback in DecodeMessage (flow+0x78 -> vtable+0x18) runs before this but its result is discarded.

FUNCTION.NAME: 0c_networking::CDeviceProvision_DecodeMessage
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT:
0c_networking::CDeviceProvision_DecodeMessage
Inbound BLE message entry. Inputs: param_2 = decoded-frame length, param_3 = raw frame ptr. Pb_IStreamInit then Pb_DecodeSubmessagePtr(stream, &DAT_ram_c0ca0d48, flow+0x58). The decoded request struct lands in the 0x138 buffer at flow+0x58.
Decode bound (PROVEN in main_app::Pb_DecodeField ram:0xb01b8d5c): a length-prefixed BYTES field (case 6) is accepted only if `len+2 <= field.data_size` else "bytes_overflow"; a STRING field (case 7) only if `len+1 <= field.data_size` else "string_overflow". So any u16 length the handler later trusts is capped by the descriptor's declared data_size, UNLESS the handler reads a length word out of a field that is not actually length-prefixed.
Before DispatchRequest it calls (*(flow+0x78)->vtable+0x18)(obj, &flow) - a notification hook; its return value is NOT used to gate dispatch. No pairing/bonding/encryption check exists in this function or its callee CDeviceProvision_DispatchRequest.
Caller: CDeviceProvision_RxLoop (ram:0xc0c22794) which reads frames from the BLE transport (flow+0x68, vtable slot 1 = ram:0xc0c1f864, refills via FUN_ram_c0c20376).

Frame type byte: 0 = data -> CDeviceProvision_DecodeMessage; 1 = ignored; 2 = receive error (tears down after 3); 3 = disconnected. Transport c0c1f864 grows a buffer via FUN_ram_b0116f26(...,0x1000) => max reassembled frame 0x1000 bytes. Created from CDeviceProvisionFlow_Constructor (ram:0xc0c21eb4).

FUNCTION.NAME: CDeviceProvisionFlow::HandleReq09_GetDeviceKind
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: BleProv_HandleReq09_GetDeviceKind (dispatch id 9). COPY SOURCE CORRECTION: source = *(u64*)(sp+8) = the std::string's DATA pointer (_M_p), NOT the object header. So it does NOT copy ptr/size/cap. DEVICE-KIND STRING: CPlatform_GetInstance()->vtable[0x60](3). The platform jump table (ram:b00d1c90, table ram:b01c96b0 indexed by id-3) maps index 3 -> ram:b00d1d5e -> "doorbell_sunray" (15 chars, ram:b01c95c8). strlen=15 => SSO: _M_p = object+0x10 = sp+0x18, and byte 15 is NUL (StdString_ConstructFromCStr). LATENT OOB READ: FUN_b01c3ff8(resp+0x18, sp+0x18, 0x28) reads 0x28 bytes from the 16-byte SSO buffer; sp+0x28 (copy offset 0x10) holds g_stack_canary and sp+0x30/0x38 hold saved s2/s1 (s1 = flow heap ptr). Destination is inside the 0x138 resp buffer: no corruption. EGRESS: the response field f10 is a STRING (prior descriptor note data_size 0x28); BleProv_EncodeAndSendResponse -> FUN_b01b80d4 case 7 uses strlen bounded by data_size, and the source is NUL-terminated at offset 15, so only "doorbell_sunray" is emitted. NO canary/heap leak on the wire (unless the field is encoded as fixed BYTES, which the handler does not set up). Verdict: latent stack OOB read, infoleak REFUTED for the current schema.

FUNCTION.NAME: CDeviceProvisionFlow::HandleReq0D
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: BleProv_HandleReq0D (dispatch id 0xd; via thunk ram:c0c22bd2). VERDICT: len is NOT attacker-controlled from BLE. len = *(u64*)(provider_output+0x8). provider_output is the 0x30 stack struct at sp+8 (zeroed, field0=1). The provider callback at flow+0x70 (CSetupSystem->CCentcom_Rdk callback table, "BleProvProvider") is member cb1e0: call (provider+0x1e0)->invoker(provider+0x1e0, provider_output). Invoker = FUN_ram_b0122bea, which runs an RDK transaction (FUN_ram_b0122a8c) then FUN_ram_b011f9a0(provider_output, &DAT_ram_b02128e0): copies tag(+0), u64(+8), 0x11 bytes(+0x10), u32(+0x24), u64(+0x28) from the trusted CCentcom/RDK cache DAT_b02128e0. So len = DAT_b02128e0+8, written only by the CCentcom Rdk path, not by any prior BLE request. The callback only populates 0x11 bytes at +0x10, so any len>0x11 is a stale-stack read; the 0x138 resp block has 0x140 usable bytes, so memcpy overflows only if len>0x126. No BLE-reachable setter for DAT+8 found. NOT a proven primitive. Requires prior RDK compromise.

FUNCTION.NAME: CDeviceProvisionFlow::HandleReq0C_CredsMsg
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT:
0c_networking::BleProv_HandleReq0C_CredsMsg (BleProvRequest *param_2; cmd==0xc, credsType==2).
REACHABILITY (proven): g_BleProvDispatchTable id 0xc (entry ram:0xc0ca0c58) -> c0c22cc0, a 4-byte thunk `addi a1,8 ; j c0c22bd6`. DispatchRequest passes request+8, so param_2 == request+0x10. (The prior "id 0xd" note was wrong.)
BODY: serializes {u8 subcmd, u8 2, creds[N], secret[M]} into a fixed 0x1e-byte stack buffer at sp+0x8 and hands &buf to the credentials callback (*(*(this+0x70)+0x1d8))(this+0x1c0,&buf): prov_memcpy(sp+0xa, param_2->creds, param_2->credsLen) prov_memcpy(sp+0x1a, param_2->secret, param_2->secretLen)
BOUNDING (proven, removes the prior "unchecked" claim): - creds and secret are length-prefixed BYTES fields; Pb_DecodeField (ram:0xb01b8d5c) rejects len+2 > field.data_size ("bytes_overflow"). Their descriptors (c0ca0eb0, reached via the id==0xc schema c0ca0ef0) declare data_size 18 (creds, max 16) and 14 (secret, max 12). - Maxima 16/12 exactly tile the buffer: 2 + 16 + 12 = 0x1e (sp+0x8..sp+0x25). Stack geometry: canary g_stack_canary at sp+0x28; saved s4..s0 at sp+0x30..0x50; ra at sp+0x58. To reach the canary would need credsLen>=0x1e or secretLen>=0xe; to reach ra, credsLen>=0x56 or secretLen>=0x46. With the enforced maxima (16/12) NEITHER copy reaches the canary. Both return paths compare against the canary and call prov_stack_chk_fail (noreturn) on mismatch.
VERDICT: bounded by construction - not a stack-buffer overflow.

FUNCTION.NAME: 0c_networking::CSetupSystem_InitProviderCallbacks
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CSetupSystem_InitProviderCallbacks(provider_new, blueprint): move-constructs a 0x220 BleProvProvider by moving each of the 17 std::function members (functor at +0x00..0x0f, _M_manager at +0x10, _M_invoker at +0x18) from `blueprint` into `provider_new`, zeroing the source. Called by CSetupSystem_Construct right after malloc(0x220).

FUNCTION.NAME: 0c_networking::CRingConnection_LoadBleBundle
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CRingConnection_LoadBleBundle: loads bundle element type 0x65 (101) directly into the fixed 0x1c2c0-byte BLE-stack segment at ram:0xc0010000 via FUN_ram_b016820c(0x65,0xc0010000). On success zeroes the 0x1058 struct at 0xc002c2c0 and regs the stack. DEST SIZE (0x1c2c0) IS NOT CHECKED AGAINST THE HEADER ELEMENT SIZE -> see FUN_ram_b016820c.

FUNCTION.NAME: CRingConnection::LoadBleBundleAndInit
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CRingConnection_LoadBleBundleAndInit: one-shot init. Calls LoadBleBundle (loads element 0x65 into c0010000), sets flag at this+0x11, then opens the BLE session (SUB c001c46c), registers GATT (SUB c002139e with DAT b01f9ed8), enables radio (SUB c001c6ac), waits on stack timeout. The GATT write characteristic is what delivers attacker bytes into the CRingConnection / CDeviceProvision handlers.

FUNCTION.NAME: CRingConnection::DispatchBleData
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Copies the connection handler list at this+0xb8 under mutex (this+0xb0), allocating a 0x30 CRingConnection_Handler per entry, then releases the mutex and invokes each copied handler (node+0x28) with the BLE event param_3. Node layout: +0x10 copied payload, +0x20 copier fn, +0x28 handler fn. Only a !=0 check precedes the indirect calls; if a handler node is heap-corrupted this is a direct control-flow target (inferred). param_2 (transport id) is stored at this+0xd0 and the previous value freed with size 0x18.

FUNCTION.NAME: 0c_networking::CRingConnection_OnBleWriteCharReq
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: App-side GATT write callback candidate (registered table ram:b01f9f20+0x10). Rejects the write unless byte at param_5+0x10 == 0xff (format check only - no pairing/auth check). Builds event {ptr=*(u64*)(param_5+8), len=*(u16*)param_5, type=1} and calls CRingConnection::DispatchBleData. Sends a 25-byte ATT response when param_4==1. UNCERTAIN MAPPING: the BLE-stack write slot _DAT_ram_c0011cee0 is invoked with a4 = ATT offset (integer), not a pointer, so param_5 here is an app-level write-event struct, not the raw ATT request; which registered slot this function occupies is unproven.

FUNCTION.NAME: CRingConnection::DispatchBleEvent
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Sibling of DispatchBleData for non-data events (connect/disconnect/MTU). Same handler-list copy+invoke. Frees the stored this+0xd0 event with size 4 whereas DispatchBleData frees it with size 0x18 (inconsistent size passed to the tracked allocator; param_2 is always 0 on current callers so the free is not reached). Renamed from FUN_ram_c0c254c8.

FUNCTION.NAME: CUpdate_ARES::ParseOtafuVersion
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CUpdate_ARES::ParseOtafuVersion(this, image_index, version, checksum). Parses the cloud OTAFU descriptor for image_index 0/1, sets update_valid_mask(this+0x2d0) bit image_index, and stores the cloud-provided checksum at img_ver[image_index]+0x10. Attacker (cloud) controls both.

FUNCTION.NAME: CUpdate_ARES::CommitAndSelectBootSlot
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CUpdate_ARES::CommitAndSelectBootSlot(this). Marks *(this+0x25c) bootable then sets it active via bootctl2. This is the persistence sink: the slot selected here is what the device boots next. Commit slot is derived from active/other slot bytes set in PrepareOtaSlotFile.

FUNCTION.NAME: CUpdate_ARES_AcmdDispatch
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CUpdate_ARES ACMD handler accepts opcode 0x10048. It checks the updater's +0x1D4 state/sentinel, queries an 8-byte record at +0x1D8, logs current/previous slot or version values, and returns 0. Other opcodes return 0x0D.

FUNCTION.NAME: CUpdate_ARES::VerifyBundleSha256
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CUpdate_ARES::VerifyBundleSha256(this, hdr, slot, secureboot). Per-element SHA-256 over data re-read from otaA/otaB (slot selects); expected digest[32] (hdr element stride 0x34) is attacker-controlled. BUG (proven): extent = offset+size uses 32-bit c.addw at ram:c0c28832, wraps at 2^32 and bypasses the capacity guard at c0c2883c, feeding an out-of-range SetReadPosition. Contained by fm_flash_read's own offset+len partition check.

FUNCTION.NAME: CUpdate_ARES::IsFwblUpdateAllowed
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CUpdate_ARES::IsFwblUpdateAllowed(this) -> bool. Returns 1 when update_valid_mask(this+0x2d0)&2==0 (no FWBL in the cloud list). With FWBL listed: returns 0 unless fwbl_ota_enabled(this+0x268) is set; then returns fwbl_ota_standalone_enabled(this+0x269) (and requires it, or an APP in the list). Both enable bytes are set by HandleFwblOtaCommand opcodes.

FUNCTION.NAME: CUpdate_ARES::SetUpdateImageList
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CUpdate_ARES::SetUpdateImageList(this). If IsFwblUpdateAllowed()==0 clears both masks; else update_allowed_mask(this+0x2d8)=update_valid_mask and copies the cloud checksums into img0_checksum(this+0x2e0)/img1_checksum(this+0x2e8).

FUNCTION.NAME: CUpdate_ARES::ReadBundleHeader
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Reads the bundle header from OTA slot A/B into the caller buffer (param_2) of size param_3. Rejects param_3 > partition capacity; seeks to 0, PRead, then resets. `this` is otaA_partition when param_4==0, else otaB_partition. Callers use 0xF20 (CUpdate_ARES_VerifyImage).

FUNCTION.NAME: CUpdate_ARES::GetSlotToVerify
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CUpdate_ARES::GetSlotToVerify(this, image_index) -> 0=otaA,1=otaB,2=invalid. Requires active_slot(this+0x261) < 2 and image_index < 6. 2 -> 0 ; 3 -> 1 ; 4 -> active_slot ; 5 -> active_slot^1 0,1 -> commit_pending(this+0x267)==0 ? active_slot : active_slot^1 NOTE: in a pure FWBL flow commit_pending==0, so VerifyImage(1) verifies the ACTIVE (currently-running) OTA slot, not the FWBL target slot. In the APP flow OtaEventHandler_App event 3 sets commit_pending=1 first, so VerifyImage(0) verifies the other/target slot.

FUNCTION.NAME: CUpdate_ARES::SetFwblSlot
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CUpdate_ARES::SetFwblSlot(this, mode). mode 0/1/2 -> FUN_b0167fec(buf,0x80, 2-mode): 0 = compare+sync the two 0x20000 FWBL halves; 1/2 = copy primary<-> secondary. Then SYSCTL_set_fwbl_slot_G(0) selects PRIMARY. This is the FWBL persistence sink (fwbl boot register), analogous to CommitAndSelectBootSlot.

FUNCTION.NAME: CUpdate_ARES::VerifyFwblImageType
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CUpdate_ARES::VerifyFwblImageType(this, restore_slot_mode). Reads the 4-byte magic @flash+0 and the type byte @flash+0x1c of BOTH fwblB (ReadFwblMagicVersion arg1) and fwblA (arg0) directly from the FWBL partitions. PASS iff the two magics are equal AND (typeA==typeB==0 [MFG bootloader] OR both types are in 1..7 [PROD]). Otherwise logs 'FWBL OTA Update flow' and calls SetFwblSlot(this, restore_slot_mode) to restore, returning 0. SECURITY: reads attacker-controlled flash; it compares the two EXISTING slots and does NOT authenticate the newly written fwbl payload (no signature/hash). It only enforces 'same kind as the other slot' and cannot stop an unsigned FWBL.

FUNCTION.NAME: CUpdate_ARES::PrepareOtaSlotFile
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CUpdate_ARES::PrepareOtaSlotFile(this, image_type). image_type 0 (APP): require update_allowed_mask(this+0x2d8)&1; commit_slot = other_slot (asserted == active^1); running_slot(this+0x258) = active_slot; write target = otaA if commit_slot==0 else otaB; posts event 5. image_type 1 (FWBL): require update_allowed_mask&2; SetFwblSlot(this,2); write target = fwblA (0xb021f9d8); posts event 4. image_type 2: notify finalize (event 6). update_allowed_mask is set from the parsed cloud image list (SetUpdateImageList).

FUNCTION.NAME: 0c_networking::CUpdate_PemMarkerStateMachine
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: 0c_networking::CUpdate_PemMarkerStateMachine(this, state, count, buf, len) Byte-transition matcher for the PEM markers. state is a signed char (init 3), indexes a 4-entry table (safe, state restricted to {0,2,3} by the code). count is incremented when a marker byte matches / reset to 0 otherwise; that count is what FindBundleKeyOffset uses to size the key. No writes past buf+len.

FUNCTION.NAME: 0c_networking::CUpdate_ScanForBundleKey
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: 0c_networking::CUpdate_ScanForBundleKey(this, slot, end_out, count_out, scan_start) Uses fwblA/fwblB_partition globals (slot selects). Gets capacity, then walks backwards from scan_start in 0x80-byte windows, PRead() into a 0x80-byte stack buffer (sp+8..sp+0x88, canary at sp+0x90 -> exact fit). Each window is fed to CUpdate_PemMarkerStateMachine(this,&state,&count,buf,0x80) which matches PEM marker bytes against a 4-entry transition table and accumulates a byte count. *end_out = scan_start + accumulated_count. Bounds: requires scan_start < capacity. attacker-controlled flash only changes WHICH offsets are selected, never the window/buffer sizes -> no stack overflow (inferred, high confidence).

FUNCTION.NAME: 0c_networking::CUpdate_FindBundleKeyOffset
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: 0c_networking::CUpdate_FindBundleKeyOffset(this, fwbl_slot, key_end_out, key_size_out, scan_start) Outputs (disasm-verified): - *param3 (&sp[0xc]) = key_end_from_end = (end2 - 4) - cnt2 [0xc0c2941c] - *param4 (&sp[0x10]) = key_size = key_end_from_end - end1 [0xc0c2942c] where end1 = 1st ScanForBundleKey outA, end2 = 2nd outA, cnt2 = 2nd state-machine count. Checks: 1<slot rejected; cnt2+4 < end2; end1 < key_end_from_end (all unsigned 32-bit). NOTE (correcting earlier comment): param5 (scan_start) IS set by the caller (0 or *(this+0x24c)), it is not stale. SECURITY: *param4 (used as malloc size AND as ReadBundleKey length) is strictly smaller than *param3 (from_end), and both are <= partition capacity. No truncation: param4 is zero-extended to 64-bit at 0xc0c29428 before the sd at 0xc0c2942c.

FUNCTION.NAME: 0c_networking::CUpdate_ReadBundleKey
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: 0c_networking::CUpdate_ReadBundleKey(this, slot, dst, len, from_end). Re-opens fwblA (0xb021f9d8) / fwblB (0xb021f9e0) by slot, re-reads capacity, and if (from_end < capacity && len < from_end) reads len bytes at capacity-from_end into dst. This is the RSA public-key source used by VerifySignature -> it is attacker-writable flash, not a ROM/OTP anchor. TOCTOU: capacity/offsets are recomputed here after FindBundleKeyOffset's scan.

FUNCTION.NAME: CUpdate_ARES::VerifySignature
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Trust-anchor note (static analysis): VerifySignature obtains its PEM public key through FindBundleKeyOffset and ReadBundleKey, which read fwblA/fwblB flash. For image_index==1 the slot is 0 and scan_start is fwbl_dl_size. In the FWBL update flow, fwblA is the write target before this check. Treat the RSA key as flash-sourced; whether a separate hardware/root verification authenticates that key at boot is unresolved.

FUNCTION.NAME: CUpdate_ARES::VerifyImage
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Updater verification finding (static analysis): param_2/image_index controls whether VerifySignature runs. When image_index==0, the RSA check is skipped; the function still compares SHA-256 digests against values in the same OTA header. OtaEventHandler_App calls VerifyImage(this,0), then AppOtaFinalize can mark and select the slot when write_error==0. This proves an updater authentication gap for APP images. Whether the reset-time secure-boot loader independently rejects such an image remains unverified.

FUNCTION.NAME: CUpdate_ARES::HandleFwblOtaCommand
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CUpdate_ARES::HandleFwblOtaCommand(this, opcode). Jump-table dispatcher (opcodes 0..10) for the cloud/local bootloader-OTA feature control: 0/1 -> fwbl_ota_enabled(this+0x268)=1/0 ('FWBL OTA enabled/disabled') 2/3 -> fwbl_ota_standalone_enabled(this+0x269)=1/0 4/5 -> SetFwblSlot(this,1/0) 6/7/9/10 -> VerifyImage(this,2/3/4/5) 8 -> VerifyFwblImageType(this,1) default -> 'Bootloader OTA feature opcode %zu not accepted: use %d ~ %d'. These opcodes are the enable gate consumed by IsFwblUpdateAllowed.

FUNCTION.NAME: CUpdate_ARES::OtaEventHandler_App
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CUpdate_ARES::OtaEventHandler_App(this, event, ctx, payload). event 0: open OTA target slot for write. event 2: PWrite chunk. event 3: sets commit_pending(this+0x267)=1 then VerifyImage(this,0) -- APP path, which skips RSA signature verification (see VerifyImage).

FUNCTION.NAME: CUpdate_ARES::OtaEventHandler_Fwbl
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Updater verification finding (static analysis): event 3 closes the FWBL target, calls VerifyFwblImageType, compares fwbl_checksum with checksum of bytes written, then calls VerifyImage(this,1). PrepareOtaSlotFile(image_type=1) selects fwblA as target and calls SetFwblSlot(this,2). VerifySignature(image_index=1) selects FWBL slot 0 and uses fwbl_dl_size as scan_start; CUpdate_ReadBundleKey reads the extracted key from fwblA. VerifyImage's bundle header/payload comes from otaA/otaB, so this signature check does not authenticate the FWBL bytes just written. The type check only compares FWBL magic/type fields across slots. Reset-time secure-boot behavior is not established here.

FUNCTION.NAME: 0c_networking::FUN_ram_c0c2a260
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CUpdateStats_ARES registers its RuntimeObject with target name CUpdateStats_ARES. Its actual ACMD slot +8 is CUpdateStats_ARES_AcmdDispatch (c0c2a588), not the shared unsupported handler.

FUNCTION.NAME: 0c_networking::FUN_ram_c0c2a57a
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CUpdateStats_ARES subtype-7 ACMD helper clears the three counters at offsets +0x5C, +0x60, and +0x64.

FUNCTION.NAME: 0c_networking::CUpdateStats_ARES_AcmdDispatch
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CUpdateStats_ARES ACMD handler recognizes only opcode 0x10001 with subtype 7, which clears three OTA statistics fields (+0x5C/+0x60/+0x64). Other opcode/subtype combinations return 0x0D.

FUNCTION.NAME: 0c_networking::CAuthManager_AcmdDispatch
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CAuthManager ACMD dispatcher. Opcode 0x10001 virtual-dispatches an auth-manager subtype. Opcode 0x10049 subcommands 1..4: damage/clear a stored access header when its length is at least 0x1E; request token rotation via a Centcom event; switch auth fallback to basic mode; and mark the refresh token corrupt, attempting a storage update. Unsupported selectors return 0x0D.

FUNCTION.NAME: 0c_networking::CConsole_PrintfOrPrompt
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CConsole_PrintfOrPrompt(console, message): copies the caller-supplied string into the console's internal message buffer, then emits it through the configured channel vtable. This provides a marker path through the application's initialized console and does not depend on Notify_Enable's logger gate.

FUNCTION.NAME: 0c_networking::CConsoleMars_AcmdDispatch
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CConsole_MARS ACMD dispatcher. Opcode 0x10023 invokes the console mode/start path; 0x10024 invokes the corresponding stop/cleanup path; 0x100A4 sets a boolean state field at +0x41C. Exact end-user command labels are not recoverable from this wrapper alone.

FUNCTION.NAME: 0c_networking::FUN_ram_c0c2dc38
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: 0c_networking CFastpingTest report builder (assert tag s_CFastpingTest::CResultStatusRepo). BeginBuild(0x37=55, 10): 55 CTreeNode slots (55*0x18=0x528) + 65 index slots (0x104), total 0x62C bytes. Inserts exactly 55 static key leaves (4 + 1 + 3 + 1 + 2 + 1 + six 7-node groups + 3) and pushes exactly 10 child-count markers (4,3,2, six 6s, 10). EXACT FIT -> the unbounded-insert bug is NOT triggered. All keys/values are static strings/globals; no attacker byte influences the insert count. Materialized via CTree::Materialize into a 0x28 object stored at param_1[0xb]. PROVEN.

FUNCTION.NAME: 0c_networking::FUN_ram_c0c2ef0a
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: 0c_networking CEgressTest report builder (assert tag s_CEgressTest::CResultStatusReport). BeginBuild(0xc=12, 1): 12 node slots + 13 index slots. Inserts exactly 12 static key leaves (ipTarget, nPort, nPacketSize, msDuration, msPushing, nBytesSent, txshape, msMaxStall, pStalled, pContention, SO_SNDBUF, txrate) and pushes one child-count marker (12). EXACT FIT -> the unbounded-insert bug is NOT triggered. No attacker-controlled count. PROVEN.

FUNCTION.NAME: 0c_networking::CNetworkCheck_AcmdDispatch
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CNetworkCheck ACMD handler. Opcode 0x10049 acts only for subtype 0, invoking the nested object's virtual slot +0x38 with the stored object+0x1228 value. Opcode 0x10087 passes (arg3 != 0) to FUN_ram_c0c331f8, then either calls FUN_ram_c0c325fc when arg4 is zero and arg5 nonzero, or calls FUN_ram_c0c32d42 with arg4. Both recognized opcodes return 0; unsupported opcodes return 0x0D.

FUNCTION.NAME: 0c_networking::CDeviceLocation_AcmdDispatch
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CDeviceLocation ACMD dispatcher. Opcode 0x10001 accepts subtype 6 and calls CDeviceLocation_UpdateCC only when the enable byte at object+0x108 is nonzero. Opcode 0x1008A forwards to CDeviceLocation_Command. Other inputs return 0x0D.

FUNCTION.NAME: 0c_networking::CBatteryManager_AcmdDispatch
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CBatteryManager ACMD: opcode 0x10001 forwards the supplied subtype to vtable slot +0x110 (CBatteryManager_QueryOrRefreshStats). Opcode 0x1003C selector 0 invokes a virtual operation; selector 1 clears the sampling state/threshold fields and runs the reset helper; selector 2 stores the supplied threshold and marks it valid. Other selectors/opcodes return 0x0D.

FUNCTION.NAME: 0c_networking::CBatteryManager_QueryOrRefreshStats
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CBatteryManager virtual method used by ACMD opcode 0x10001. For subtype/operation 0, selector 0x200 or 0x80..0xFF requests the virtual query using object+0x154; other selector values refresh external-power diagnostics and derived battery metrics through c0c39f44/c0c3a0ee. Nonzero subtype returns success without action.

FUNCTION.NAME: 0c_networking::CRebootManager_AcmdDispatch
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CRebootManager handles opcode 0x1002E by recalculating the periodic reboot schedule. Opcode 0x1002F argument type 0 toggles periodic reboot, type 2 toggles reboot-when-idle, type 1 schedules reboot at next idle, and type 3 logs status including idle/periodic timer state. Other types log unsupported and return 0.

FUNCTION.NAME: 0c_networking::CGrecoController_OnMdsMigrationPackage
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CGrecoController_OnMdsMigrationPackage: cloud E2EE migration-message consumer. Gets a package buffer/len from CGrecoController_GetMdsMigrationPackage and calls Greco_TinyMlsMigrate(...,buf+2,len-2,...). Attacker source = cloud Greco/MDS message.

FUNCTION.NAME: 0c_networking::Greco_TinyMls_ParseGroupInfo
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Greco_TinyMls_ParseGroupInfo(out, dst, base, len, &offset): MlsCursor over (base,len); uStack_48/uStack_44 alias cursor.len/pos. Loop over `count` entries; the for-increment (uStack_44 - uVar1) correctly accumulates consumed bytes (NOT an infinite loop). Guard uVar5<0x861 before memcpy into dst (0x864 region) plus len>=pos check -> copies are in-bounds. NO OOB found.

FUNCTION.NAME: 0c_networking::Greco_TinyMls_ImportGroupState
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Greco_TinyMls_ImportGroupState(out, group, base, len, ...): MlsCursor reads into fixed sub-fields of the 0x32e8 group state (0x864, 0x1fc8, 0x680, 0x20, ...) all via MlsCursor_ReadBytes(dst,max) which zeroes the copy on overrun; and the entry loop is bounded to 6. Attacker lengths do not translate to unchecked copies. No OOB found.

FUNCTION.NAME: 0c_networking::Greco_TinyMls_MigrateParse
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Greco_TinyMls_MigrateParse: cursor.len/pos alias iStack_d8/uStack_d4. iVar3==0 path (param_5==0): ImportGroupState(base, len) where base=(pos-2)+buf = buf and len=(len+2)-pos = len; in-bounds. iVar3==1 path needs param_5!=0 AND a valid Greco_ExternalKey_VerifyPackageTag (crypto) before reaching ImportGroupState. The prior-pass "underflow" (uStack_d4-2)/(len+2-offset) only yields the intentional 2-byte rewind once pos>=2; not reachable with pos>len. No OOB proven.

FUNCTION.NAME: 0c_networking::Greco_ExternalKey_VerifyPackageTag
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Greco_ExternalKey_VerifyPackageTag(ctx, ..., tag, tagLen, ..., outLen). Copies 0x21 bytes from ctx+0x21 into a local 0x21 buffer (bounded). Checks tagLen==0x10 and tagLen <= *outLen before computing/compare the AEAD tag (constant-time 16-byte compare). Returns -1 on failure. No length-driven copy into a fixed buffer; the only memcpy source is the fixed 0x21 context field.

FUNCTION.NAME: 0c_networking::Greco_TinyMlsMigrate
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Greco_TinyMlsMigrate: length-relabeling wrapper. Strips 2 bytes when param_5!=0 ((int)len-2), then MigrateParse. Attacker-controlled buf/len from the cloud migration package.

FUNCTION.NAME: 0c_networking::Greco_TinyMls_ProcessMdsPackage
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Greco_TinyMls_ProcessMdsPackage: other ImportGroupState caller. Bound checks uStack_58 < uStack_54 (declared vs consumed) before import; the later copy into the 0x168 staging area is guarded by (iStack_70-2U < 0x9d). No unbounded attacker-length copy found.

FUNCTION.NAME: 0c_networking::E2eeCommon_ValidateJsonRequest
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: E2eeCommon_ValidateJsonRequest(str, label) - WEAK validation: only checks str != NULL and str[0] != 0. It does NOT validate JSON syntax/schema. Used by CPolicy_SetTargetsFromJson before handing the string to the JSON parser, so any non-empty attacker string reaches the JSON layer. Informational: not itself memory-unsafe, but defeats the stated "validate request" intent.

FUNCTION.NAME: 0c_networking::CManifest_BuildSignedManifest
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CManifest::BuildSignedManifest - assembles manifest JSON (schemaVersion/documentVersion/manifestId/owner/cekDetails/signedManifest/signature/attestationDetails) and signs it (SHA256withECDSA); verifies container/signature before returning.

FUNCTION.NAME: 0c_networking::CPolicy_AddTargetsFromCerts
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CPolicy_AddTargetsFromCerts: for cert extension 2 (SKID) the length returned by E2eeCrypto_GetCertExtension (a1) is passed to StdVector_AllocateElements(&vec, a1) (malloc(a1)) and then prov_memcpy(vec, ext_ptr, a1). Allocation size == copy size -> NO heap overflow. Prior-pass suspicion disproven (decompiler printed a single arg but a1=len at the call site). Certificate must pass CE2eeCrypto_VerifyCert first.

FUNCTION.NAME: 0c_networking::CPolicy_SetTargetsFromJson
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CPolicy_SetTargetsFromJson. SECURITY NOTE: its "validation" is E2eeCommon_ValidateJsonRequest, which only checks the string is non-null/non-empty (no schema check). Target public keys are then taken from attacker JSON but must pass CE2eeCrypto_VerifyCert (mbedtls_x509_crt_verify against the provisioned trust store). Per the threat model (crypto sound) that signature gate is the only real barrier; nothing here is pre-auth.

FUNCTION.NAME: 0c_networking::CController_InitServiceEndpoints
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CController::InitServiceEndpoints - configures base URLs for the Amazon "Cerulean" E2EE backend. prod/gamma branch uses https://{ring.|}{.prod.|.gamma.}<region>.cerulean.devices.amazon.dev with "key_mgmt" (CKMS) and "manifest_mgmt" (CMMS) service labels. The else branch (param_4 != 0) hardcodes PLAINTEXT http://ckms and http://cmms.

FUNCTION.NAME: 0c_networking::CController_RegisterProducerWithCKMS
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CController::RegisterProducerWithCKMS - builds a self-signed cert (CN=ProducerDevice, pikX509/keychainId/signedEncryptionPolicy), POSTs it to <CKMS base>/v1/participatingInstance/producer, then persists returned ASK/PIK certs via CE2eeLocalStorage.

FUNCTION.NAME: 0c_networking::CController_UploadManifestToCMMS
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CController::UploadManifestToCMMS - builds/signs an E2EE manifest (SHA256withECDSA), POSTs manifest to CMMS, then PUTs per-key /v1/manifest/<id>/cekDetails. Fetches target PIK/AEK lists via GET tPK and parses them with CPolicy.

FUNCTION.NAME: 0c_networking::SFrame_GetFooterSize
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT:
SFrame_GetFooterSize(in, len, out_version, out_magic).
Reads the 5-byte trailer at in[len-4] (magic LE: 'SCBC'=0x53434243 or 'GRCO'=0x4f435247) and the footer size byte at in[len-5]. Rejects size<6 or size>len. Returns the raw footer size; version = byte at in[len-size]>>4 (must be 1 or 2). NOTE: returns the attacker-controlled size byte directly to callers; see SFrame_ReadHeaderFields for the missing min-size check.
FUNCTION.TYPEINFO_CMT: ulong __stdcall SFrame_GetFooterSize(SFrame_Context * ctx, void * in, ulong len, uchar * outVersion, uint * outMagic)

FUNCTION.NAME: 0c_networking::SFrame_ReadHeaderFields
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT:
SFrame_ReadHeaderFields - parse attacker header at in+inLen-footer_size.
BUG (proven): footer_size only validated >=6 (and <=inLen) by SFrame_GetFooterSize, but the SCBC path reads header byte [0x15] (key id) and the GRCO path reads [0x1a..0x1e]. With footer_size in [6,0x15] the parser reads up to +0x18 past the *frame* end. For the inbound path the frame is at the start of the fixed staging global DAT_ram_b0217940 (0x141 bytes) with inLen<=0x140, so the overshoot passes the global only when inLen is near max: max read = b0217940+0x140-6+0x1e = b0217a98, i.e. 0x17 past the buffer. When inLen is small the overshoot stays inside the staging buffer (stale/zero bytes). CANARY unreachable (~0x7f920 away).
ESCALATION - NEGATIVE (proven by data-flow): the over-read bytes land in flags/version/keyEpoch/ counter/keyId/salt outputs. keyId is only compared against installed keys (bounded, max 4) and otherwise makes the frame decode fail; no field becomes a write length/offset, none is echoed, so the read cannot be escalated to a write or an infoleak. Callers: SFrame_Decrypt c0c59de6, c0c5a238.
FUNCTION.TYPEINFO_CMT: ulong __stdcall SFrame_ReadHeaderFields(SFrame_Context * ctx, void * in, ulong inLen, uint * magic, uchar * version, uchar * flags, uint * f7, uint * f8, uint * keyId, uint * f10)

FUNCTION.NAME: 0c_networking::SFrame_Encrypt
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: SFrame E2EE encoder (CSframeE2ee). Handles NAL/slice parsing, optional codec padding, header/footer write, AES-GCM encrypt and auth tag. Contains an unimplemented SFRAME_FLAG_CODEC_CONFIG_SEPARATE_AUTH path (see 0xc0c59474).

FUNCTION.NAME: 0c_networking::SFrame_Decrypt
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT:
SFrame_Decrypt(SFrame_Context *ctx, in, inLen, out, &outLen) - inbound E2EE decryptor.
Entry checks: ctx->key_count!=0; in/out/outLen != NULL; *outLen >= inLen; no overlap. Then: SFrame_GetFooterSize (validates footer_size in [6,inLen] and version in {1,2}); ctx->version saved; branch on ctx->codec: 1..4 -> video NAL/slice path, >=5 -> simple audio path. Audio path: ReadHeaderFields -> key lookup (bounded by key_count) -> SFrame_BuildNonce* -> FUN_b01b651a setkey/IV -> FUN_b01b66fa start -> FUN_b01b6786 AAD accumulate -> FUN_b01b67f8 GCM/CBC decrypt -> SFrame_VerifyAuthTag at (in+ptLen+5|10) -> replay window.
WRITE-SAFETY (proven by inspection + disasm): the only ciphertext length is ptLen = inLen - footer_size; out capacity was checked >= inLen at entry, so decrypt never writes more than *outLen. Header fields from the attacker (incl. the OOB over-read in ReadHeaderFields) only select a key (bounded index), build the nonce/AAD, or feed the replay counter - none is used as a write length/offset. Cipher is GCM (cipher_mode==1) or CBC; AES-CBC round-down copy is bounded. Video-path emulation-prevention fixup write `*in[inLen-5-cnt] -= cnt` stays inside the frame; out-cap check accounts for added NAL overhead. No escalation of the header OOB read to a write. Only caller: CSframeE2ee_Decrypt (b01439f2).
FUNCTION.TYPEINFO_CMT: long __stdcall SFrame_Decrypt(SFrame_Context * ctx, void * in, ulong inLen, void * out, uint * outLen)

FUNCTION.NAME: CStorageElement::CStorageElement
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CStorageElement base ctor (CFileDesc-derived). Calls CFileDesc ctor then initializes vtable (ram:0xc0cb4750), cursors +0x220/+0x228/+0x230, capacity +0x238, mode +0x240 and three mutex handles (+0x248, +0x2f0, +0x3a0).

FUNCTION.NAME: CStorageElement::GetBytesAvailable
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CStorageElement::GetBytesAvailable. read=+0x228, write=+0x230, capacity=+0x238. if read<=write: write-read; else: capacity+write-read. Returns the circular occupancy but clamps neither operand to capacity, so an out-of-range cursor yields a wrong (possibly huge) count.

FUNCTION.NAME: CStorageElement::Write
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT:
CStorageElement::Write (vtable slot +0x18). long __thiscall Write(void *src, ulong len).
mode 0 (linear): WriteRaw(this->write_position, src, len); write_position += len. NO capacity check: a stream longer than capacity_238 walks the write cursor past the partition end and keeps programming the next flash region. mode 1 (circular): chunk = min(len, capacity_238 - write_position), wraps. src==0 asserts (prov_stack_chk_fail_report 0x29). A 4th register arg (file offset from CFileDesc::WriteDevice) is ignored here; the ACS uses this->write_position (+0x230).
Reachability of an over-long write: Centcom/HTTP config-body handlers (CCentcom_WriteConfigFileFromHttpBody @ ram:0xb012b358) feed attacker-sized chunks through PWrite -> CFileDesc::WriteDevice -> this function.

FUNCTION.NAME: CStorageElement::Read
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CStorageElement::Read (vtable slot 2, overrides CFileDesc::ReadBuffered). Signature: long Read(void *dst, ulong len). Locks mutex_3a0, then dispatches on mode (this+0x240): mode 0 (linear): ReadRaw(this, read_position(+0x228), dst, len); on ret>=0 read_position += ret; no local bounds check -> relies on fm_flash_read's partition size check. mode 1 (circular): loop min(len, capacity_238 - read_position); ReadRaw; advance dst/read_position; wrap read_position to 0 when read_position >= capacity_238. other modes: assert/log then stack_chk_fail abort. Returns total bytes read, or 0 on any ReadRaw error (error is logged, offset left unchanged). NOTE: total is accumulated with 32-bit `addw` (truncates totals >= 2^31). Uses 64-bit unsigned `capacity - read_position`, which underflows if read_position > capacity_238 (see eol).

FUNCTION.NAME: CStorageElement_ACS::SetReadPosition
CStorageElement_ACS::SetWritePosition
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CStorageElement_ACS::SetWritePosition(ulong pos): stores this->write_position (+0x230) with NO validation against capacity_238 or the partition size. Combined with linear-mode Write (no capacity check) this is the origin of an out-of-partition write_position. Callers include CUpdate_ARES (OTA descriptor offset at this+0x2f4), CFlashConfig::ReloadFactoryConfig (0), and Centcom config handlers (0).

FUNCTION.NAME: CStorageElement_ACS::FlashPageMergeCallback
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: FlashPageMergeCallback(scratch, page_off, src, processed, chunk_len): copies chunk_len bytes from src[processed ..] into scratch[page_off ..] and returns non-zero if any 0->1 bit change requires an erase. Bounds: page_off = addr&0xfff, chunk_len = min(0x1000-page_off, remaining), so scratch usage stays within 0x1000 and src usage within len. No overflow found (proven).

FUNCTION.NAME: CStorageElement_ACS::ReadRaw
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CStorageElement_ACS::ReadRaw (ACS vtable slot 14; base returns Stub_ReturnNeg6). long ReadRaw(ulong offset, void *data, int len): tail-calls main_app::fm_flash_read(partition(this+0x3a8), -1, offset, (int)len, data) and returns its result. len is sign-extended 32-bit (`addiw`). fm_flash_read re-validates offset+len against partition->size(+0x10), so out-of-range offsets normally yield -10. Proven by the `jr` tail call.
FUNCTION.TYPEINFO_CMT: long __thiscall ReadRaw(ulong offset, void * data, int len)

FUNCTION.NAME: CStorageElement_ACS::Fill
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CStorageElement_ACS::Fill (ACS vtable slot 15; base returns Stub_Return0). Fills count(param_4) bytes with value(param_2) one byte per WriteRaw under mutex_2f0. mode 0: WriteRaw(write_position, &byte, 1) until count==0. mode 1 (circular): uVar8 = (capacity_238 != write_position); WriteRaw(write_position,&byte,uVar8); expects return == uVar8; advance/wrap write_position; count -= uVar8. Returns 1 on success, 0 on error. BUG(candidate): if capacity_238 == 0 then uVar8 is always 0, WriteRaw(...,0) returns 0 (ProgramFlashRange returns 0 for len 0), so count never decreases -> infinite loop. Also in mode 1 it never validates write_position < capacity_238.

FUNCTION.NAME: CStorageElement_ACS::ProgramFlashRange
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CStorageElement_ACS::ProgramFlashRange(absolute_flash_addr, len, src, callback). Read-modify-write over 4KB pages starting at addr&~0xfff (c.lui sign-extends, mask is ~0xfff): chunk = min(0x1000 - (addr&0xfff), remaining) fm_flash_read(0,-1, page_base, 0x1000, scratch 0xc0ea7fa0) callback(scratch, addr&0xfff, src, processed, chunk) -> needs-erase? if needs-erase: fm_flash_erase(0,-1, page_base, 0x1000) fm_flash_write(0,-1, page_base, 0x1000, scratch) Serialized by global flash mutex DAT_ram_b0218f50 (asserts on lock failure, lines 0x49/0x51). Returns bytes carried out (negative on error). No bounds bug found in the page/scratch arithmetic. CONFINEMENT: passes flash_src_type=0 to fm_flash_read/write/erase so the per-partition size check (+0x10) is bypassed. For writes, fm_flash_write/erase still call check_flash_area_writeable (ram:0xb00e59e6) against the global partition table, limiting targets to writable regions -- but not necessarily to the caller's own partition. The page read here is NOT range-checked at all.

Calls CFileDesc::CFileDesc (ram:0xc0c807f0) first, then sets the CFile vtable ram:0xc0cb4fd0 (assert string "CFile" at ram:0xc0cb4fb8) and stores name at this+0x220. Confirms CFile : CFileDesc and the 0x228 total object size.

FUNCTION.NAME: CFileDesc::ReadBuffered
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CFileDesc::ReadBuffered (CFileDesc_vtable slot 2; OVERRIDDEN by CStorageElement::Read on storage objects). Returns min(len, valid_len(+0x218) - (offset & 0xffffffff)) bytes copied from buffer(+0x20)+offset, or 0 when offset >= valid_len. Bounds the copy to valid_len (not to the malloc size capacity(+0x18)); correct only if every writer keeps valid_len <= capacity. `this` is not asserted non-null here.

FUNCTION.NAME: CFileDesc::PRead
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CFileDesc::PRead (slot 9). Positional read: asserts dst!=0 and len!=0, locks mutex at +0x160, resets last_error(+0x210); if flag_a0==0 -> last_error=4; if field_98==2 -> last_error=9; else calls vtable slot 2 (ReadBuffered / or CStorageElement::Read) with offset = param_4, or current position int_a8(+0xa8) when param_4 == -1. Afterwards int_a8 = (int)offset + (int)result (32-bit arithmetic). Returns the slot result.

FUNCTION.NAME: 0c_networking::CAuthStorage_ReadWholeFile
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Reads a file's Stat size into a dynamic byte vector, growing it to the full reported size before the Read call. There is no application-level maximum size. The vector growth path allocates the requested capacity and does not check the allocation result before initializing/copying. If flash-controlled KVS metadata can make Stat report a very large positive size, this can exhaust heap or fault on allocation failure. Confirm backend reachability and metadata size limits before rating as exploitable.

FUNCTION.NAME: 0c_networking::FUN_ram_c0c8138c
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Loads a nontransactional auth-storage value through CAuthStorage_ReadWholeFile, converts the complete byte vector to a string, parses it as JSON, then imports fields. The parser receives the entire flash-reported file size; assess with CAuthStorage_ReadWholeFile's uncapped allocation.

FUNCTION.NAME: 0c_networking::CLoggerCoPro_AcmdDispatch
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CLogger_CoPro ACMD dispatcher. Opcode 0x10023 calls a logger snapshot/report helper; 0x10024 calls a second logger helper; 0x1000D iterates a table of sender/core/port/write counters and emits usage-memory-test logs.

FUNCTION.NAME: 0c_networking::CLoggerRDK_AcmdDispatch
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Security review: opcode 0x1000D / selector 0x19 treats param_4 as an iteration count with no upper bound. The loop is `for (uVar3 = 1; uVar3 <= param_4; uVar3++)`; at UINT64_MAX it wraps and never terminates, and large values cause prolonged log/CPU exhaustion. Shell numeric parsing accepts unsigned 64-bit values, so this is potentially command-triggerable if the ACMD console is reachable. Availability issue; no memory corruption observed in this path.

FUNCTION.NAME: 0c_networking::CNtpClient_AcmdDispatch
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: CNtpClient ACMD dispatcher. Opcode 0x10001 forwards to the NTP state/query routine. Opcode 0x10011 subcommands 0..6 create/start or stop the NTP request, request synchronization, log time source/current time, reset sync counter, and set system time from supplied fields. Unrecognized subcommands log and return 0x0D.

FUNCTION.NAME: 0c_networking::CWifi_ValidateAndCopyProfile
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Copies the top-level Wi-Fi profile and its four 0x1b-byte subprofiles. It bounds the primary SSID and primary credential lengths, but does not validate each subprofile's length byte before copying the slots. CWifi_BuildStaConfigFromStoredAndConnect later uses those subprofile lengths as memcpy sizes.

FUNCTION.NAME: 0c_networking::Wifi_LoadStoredCredentialSlot0
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Loads named KVS property WifiCred_config_0 into a zeroed 0xb4-byte destination and only increments the credential-slot count if kvs_read_named_property returns exactly 0xb4. The named-property decoder inherits the KVS record integrity/authentication caveats recorded at Flash_ReadFileDecode; static xrefs show no callers for this function in the current program.

FUNCTION.NAME: 0c_networking::CWifiHal_StartConnectAP
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Flash-controlled credential length overflow: for security mode 1, the selected key length comes from the stored profile slot length and is passed to memcpy into WifiHal_SelectedCredentialBuffer at ram:c0e8d5c2. The preceding 0x40-byte clear covers ram:c0e8d5c0..d5ff, leaving only 62 bytes from the copy start. A length of 64 overwrites adjacent globals including WifiHal_SSIDLength at d601 and later credential lengths overwrite SSID/BSSID state. The join task consumes the modified globals before the caller checks its stack canary. Its downstream connect helper FUN_ram_c0c89f9c rejects SSID lengths outside 1..32, so downstream code execution is not established; the fixed global overwrite remains confirmed.

FUNCTION.NAME: 0c_networking::CWifiHal_JoinTask
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Join task consumes WifiHal_SSIDLength, WifiHal_SSIDBuffer, BSSID, security mode, and selected credential state populated by CWifiHal_StartConnectAP. A stored-profile credential copy can overwrite these globals before this task is launched. The selected SSID length then reaches FUN_ram_c0c89f9c, which rejects lengths outside 1..32; assess other state corruption separately.

FUNCTION.NAME: 0c_networking::CWifi_CopyScanResultsToControlBuffer
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Security review: copies the scan-record byte at src+0x20 directly as the memcpy length into each 0x34-byte output record, without enforcing the 802.11 SSID maximum (32) or the record/buffer capacity. The same length is stored in the result record. If the upstream scan callback can provide an oversized length, records overlap and the final entry can overrun the 0x824-byte caller buffer.

FUNCTION.NAME: 0c_networking::CWifi_BuildStaConfigFromStoredAndConnect
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: Reachable post-boot flash-profile stack overwrite: wifi_control_dispatch -> CWifi_MapControlCommand -> CWifi_DispatchStoredConfigOp case 0x18 -> CWifi_LoadStoredConfigAndProfile -> CWifi_LoadStoredProfileFromKvs reads attacker-controlled WifiCred.profile bytes into 0xc0e8d780. In security case 1, four profile length bytes at offsets 0x7c/0x97/0xb2/0xcd drive memcpy to the stack configuration at offsets 0x2c, 0x47, 0x62, and 0x7d with no 0x1a-byte bound. CWifi_ConnectUsingStoredConfig and reconnect events feed this configuration to CWifi_ConnectSTA before this function checks its stack canary. The stack frame places canary at sp+0xf8 and saved return at sp+0x138; determine whether in-frame structure corruption is exploitable beyond crash. Raw wifi control command 14 maps to internal operation 0x18 through WifiControlCommandMap.

FUNCTION.NAME: unk_type_65::BLE_prvGattsReqCb
FUNCTION.REGULAR_CMT: GATT/ATT request dispatcher (CYBT/WICED-style). p_data (ble_att_req_t @ DAT_unk_type_65__c0011cf30): +0 conn_id, +4 opcode, +8 handle, +10 offset, +12 len, +16 value ptr. Control-flow target: indirect slots c0011cee0/c0011cee8/c0011ced8/c0011cef8/c0011cf08 (inferred - heap corruption of these gives direct call).

Dispatch: event 4 -> BLE_prvGattsReqCb; connect/disconnect -> _DAT_ram_c0011ce90; event 5 checks _DAT_ram_c0011ce90 != 0 but then calls _DAT_ram_c0011cf00 (NULL-call candidate if cf00 unset while ce90 set); event 7 -> (*(code*)p_data[1])(p_data[0]) - function pointer read from event data.
